title: GTM Engineering - ShareGate
description:
Company Description
Workleap is a Montreal-based tech company, founded in 2006. We're builders at heart, we make simple products that actually matter to the people who use them. We have two product lines: Workleap Agent, our newest solution built to make every manager more effective, and ShareGate, the world's leading solution for Microsoft 365 migration and governance. More than 15,000 companies worldwide trust us to do exactly that. We're intentional about who joins us. If you're the kind of person who gets excited by a hard problem and wants to help shape what comes next, there's a place for you here.
Your role
ShareGate’s customers generate rich signals (product usage, support interactions, renewal dates), but those signals aren’t yet connected into an engine that protects and grows the revenue we already have. As our GTM Architect, Expansion & Retention, you’ll design, build and ship AI agents and agentic workflows that turn those signals into saved renewals and cross-sell pipeline. This is an embedded engineering role within GTM, not back-office ops: you’ll apply the signal-based, agent-first approach we already use for new customer acquisition to the customers we already have.
 Your impact: 
Protect renewals by building AI agents that continuously monitor renewal health and flag at-risk accounts to Account Managers early, with context, recommended next steps and enough lead time to act.
Grow revenue from our existing customers by designing and running an agentic cross-sell motion: score fit for our second product line, research each account, personalize outreach, qualify interest and route genuine intent to the right salesperson with the full context needed to close.
Define the signals your agents need and partner with Revenue Systems, which builds and owns the data flow between product usage and the CRM. Validate the data with SQL before you act on it.
Replace manual workflows with AI agents and reusable pipeline modules (not one-off automations) that Account Management and Sales can run and own on their own.
Tune both motions by owning reporting on pipeline generated, conversion, renewal outcomes and revenue impact, and by running controlled experiments without adding headcount.
Drive adoption by turning everything you build into SOPs, demos and playbooks, so the team uses what you ship, not just appreciates it.
Your team
You’ll join a GTM engineering effort that already runs a signal-based, agent-first approach to new customer acquisition, and now points it at the customers we already have. The challenge: connect usage, support and renewal signals into agents that reduce the friction between signal and action. The tools, plays and channels will evolve; that mission won’t.
Our stack: low-code orchestration (n8n, Make, Zapier or similar), Python or TypeScript, SQL on our data warehouse, and our CRM (HubSpot).
What you'll bring
Background in RevOps, GTM/marketing operations, customer success operations or GTM engineering, with hands-on experience building automation;
Hands-on experience with low-code orchestration (n8n, Make, Zapier or similar), plus working knowledge of Python or TypeScript for API integrations and data transformation;
fluency with agentic tools and MCP connectors. Strong LLM workflow design (agent orchestration, tool use, evaluation), sound judgment on when AI adds leverage versus complexity, and a track record of shipping AI agents or LLM workflows to real users, not just prototypes;
Working SQL to query and validate usage, support and renewal data., so you can build and trust the data behind your agents;
CRM fluency (HubSpot a plus): enough to design agents on our data model and work with Revenue Systems on what you need.
Understanding of subscription business metrics (renewal rate, net retention, customer lifetime value), and experience with or strong interest in outbound and signal-based go-to-market motions;
The ability to work directly with Sales and Account Management, translate complex builds into plain language, and earn adoption through demos and handoff docs, without a PM to bridge the gap;
Bonus: experience building AI-driven qualification or scoring systems; a B2B SaaS background with multiple product lines, ideally product-led or demo-led; published technical content that makes complex systems accessible.
Most of this sounds like you? Apply.
What the job comes with
Base salary: $110,000 - $140,000. This range reflects our Canada-wide compensation scale. Final offers may be adjusted based on the candidate's region to align with local market conditions.
OTE: $120,000 - $155,000
LTIP program, share in Workleap's long-term growth.
RRSP + Family health insurance + telemedicine + annual wellness budget.
Flexible vacation policy.
Remote work, with access to our Montreal office.
In-person gathering twice a year.
Claude access, for everyone.
Note: The internal title for this role is GTM Architect.
 What drives us 
At Workleap, we build software that sits at the center of how people experience work, every day, at every level.
We move fast. Priorities shift, decisions get made with the information we have, and we iterate. If you thrive on intensity and ambiguity doesn't slow you down, you'll feel right at home.
We're builders. We do what it takes to move forward. AI is part of our toolkit. We use it to go faster and decide smarter, not to replace judgment.
If you want real impact and a place where your decisions matter, this is it.
 How we hire 
Transparency is how we hire — for you as much as for us.
Here's how it works: a first call with a recruiter, then a virtual interview with the hiring manager. You'll then complete a take-home case study, followed by a meet with future colleagues to discuss it together. Depending on the role, the process may vary slightly — your recruiter will walk you through it on your first call.
We use AI to support certain steps of the process, but every hiring decision remains human.
We can't wait to meet you.
By applying, you confirm that you have read and agree to our .
#LI-Remote

Working SQL to validate warehouse data (his is basic)

Competitive base salary with performance-based bonuses.
Comprehensive pension scheme and private healthcare coverage.
Flexible hybrid working model from our central London office.

Build strong, multi-threaded relationships across customer organisations, identifying key stakeholders, decision-makers, champions and potential detractors.
Establish trusted relationships with senior and executive stakeholders, introducing Nutritics Executive Sponsors where appropriate.
Develop and maintain customer success plans that align Nutritics solutions with customer objectives and clearly demonstrate value.
Lead regular Strategic Business Reviews with customers, using customer objectives, adoption, usage and outcomes to demonstrate value and agree future priorities.
Where appropriate, conduct in-person strategic customer meetings to strengthen relationships and alignment.
Act as the voice of the customer within Nutritics while representing Nutritics confidently and credibly to the customer.
 2. Customer Health, Retention & Growth

Proactively identify changes in customer health, adoption or sentiment and intervene before they develop into material retention risks.
Own retention strategies for at-risk customers, developing and coordinating clear mitigation plans across relevant internal teams.
Maintain clear visibility of renewal dates, customer sentiment, risks and dependencies to support strong renewal readiness.
Identify opportunities to increase adoption and value across existing customer organisations.
Map customer objectives and emerging needs against Nutritics solutions to identify qualified expansion and cross-sell opportunities, partnering with Account Management/Sales to progress commercial discussions.
Partner with Account Management and Finance on renewal, contractual, billing and notice-period matters as required.
 3. Business Continuity & Team Mentorship 
Work collaboratively across Customer Engagement, Account Management, Sales, Product, Solutions, Finance and other internal teams to ensure customer priorities, risks and opportunities are understood and appropriately actioned.
Provide clear visibility of significant customer activity, risks, successes and strategic initiatives to the wider business.
Capture and communicate customer feedback, recurring themes and emerging requirements to help inform product, service and customer experience improvements.
Ensure customer records, success plans, health status, risks, actions and key interactions are accurately maintained within ClientSuccess and other relevant systems.
Support continuity of service across our global customer base during North American working hours, providing senior Customer Success support and escalation coverage for UK and international customers where required.
 4. Senior Team Contribution & Development 
Act as a senior point of expertise within the Customer Success team, supporting colleagues with complex customer situations, relationship strategies and retention challenges.

Contribute to the development and continuous improvement of Customer Success processes, playbooks, Success Cycles and ways of working.

Provide customer and market insight to the Director of Customer Success & Engagement and wider Customer Experience leadership team to support strategic decision-making.

title: GTM Program Manager
description:
About This Role
 The GTM Program Manager leads oversight of the critical go-to-market programs for our key corporate verticals. The role makes sure each vertical program has shared objectives, a clear timeline, named accountability and transparent status, risks and outcomes, and that progress is reported clearly to broader and senior stakeholders.
Current priority verticals are Biopharma, Chemicals & Materials, Semiconductors & Electronics, and Energy & Vehicles. Priorities will shift as the market and business evolve, and the role is expected to flex with them.
It is a problem-solving, orchestration role designed to help teams move faster together, remove friction, and continuously improve how we take solutions and portfolios to market.
The role also supports the other program managers in building a more effective, consistent operating model, with shared templates, playbooks, checklists, processes and reporting formats, so every execution feels like part of one system and no program feels like a fresh relaunch. The role feeds vertical program progress into the Quarterly Performance Review and Quarterly Business Review cycle.
 Key Responsibilities
 Vertical program enablement
Drive end-to-end oversight of critical programs for priority verticals, from planning through delivery and outcome review.
Align vertical, sales, marketing, product and enablement stakeholders on shared objectives, scope, success measures and timelines.
Establish clear ownership and accountability for every milestone, dependency and decision.
Track program status, identify risks and cross-team dependencies early, and escalate or resolve issues to keep execution on track.
Re-sequence and re-plan programs as vertical priorities shift, keeping stakeholders informed of trade-offs.
 Reporting and governance
Run a regular program cadence (status reviews, steering updates, risk and decision logs) with consistent reporting for broader and senior stakeholders.
Consolidate vertical program progress, risks and outcomes into the QPR and QBR cycle, and translate the outcomes into actions with owners and timelines.
Provide senior leaders with a clear, concise view of progress across verticals, highlighting where support or decisions are needed.
 Operating model and program office support
Partner with the other program offices to design and drive a more effective, shared operating model.
Develop and maintain reusable templates, playbooks, checklists, processes and reporting formats that make execution consistent across programs and verticals.
Embed these standards in day-to-day practice, and capture lessons learned so each program builds on the last rather than starting from scratch.
Share best practices and coach program owners and teams on adoption.
 Experience And Capabilities
5+ years of experience in program management, PMO, GTM or commercial operations, or strategy and operations in a B2B environment.
Proven track record driving cross-functional initiatives across product, marketing, sales, and enablement.
Experience designing and running operating frameworks, governance rhythms and reporting for senior audiences.
Ability to bring structure to ambiguous, fast-moving environments and to influence without direct authority.
Strong communication and synthesis skills: able to turn complex programs into clear, actionable updates.
Commercial awareness and curiosity about industry verticals such as life sciences, chemicals and materials, semiconductors and electronics, and energy and vehicles.

 GTM Strategy & Operations takes product and pricing initiatives and creates commercially viable, operationally sound go-to-market motions. You're handed the objective and you decide how to execute: building the target lists, assigning appropriate account actions, segmenting customers by contractual and pricing eligibility, and tracking adoption.  What You'll Do

title: Revenue Operations Manager
description:
About Us: 
Vortexa was founded to solve the immense information gap that exists in the energy industry. By using massive amounts of new satellite data and pioneering work in artificial intelligence, Vortexa creates an unprecedented view of global seaborne energy flows in real-time, bringing transparency and efficiency to the energy markets. 
With offices in London, New York, Houston, Singapore, Geneva and the UAE, we are building the definitive platform for energy and freight analytics globally - backed by leading investors including Morgan Stanley & Notion Capital. 
 The Role: 
We are seeking a commercially minded Revenue Operations Manager to own the post-sales side of our revenue engine, based in our London office. Reporting to the VP of Revenue Operations and working closely with the VP of Customer Success, you will bridge Sales Ops and Customer Lifecycle Ops - making sure the customer journey from signature to renewal and expansion runs on clean data, sharp processes and well-timed signals. 
You'll be the operational partner to our Customer Success leadership, Account Managers, CSMs and Finance, turning product usage and contract data into early warnings, expansion opportunities and predictable renewals. This is an individual contributor role for someone who enjoys designing the system and rolling up their sleeves to run it. 
It's an ideal opportunity for someone who wants to shape post-sales operations at a scaling SaaS business, while learning about one of the world's most impactful and complex industries. 
 Your core priorities: 
Expansion and renewal signals: design and run the signal framework that surfaces expansion, upsell and renewal risk early - combining product usage, conversation insights, customer health data and Salesforce contract data into clear, actionable views for AMs and CSMs 
Automation and escalation precision engine: build customer intelligence automations that route the right alert to the right owner at the right time, with defined escalation paths when an account shows risk 
Entitlements, onboarding, and offboarding: own entitlement accuracy across Salesforce, CPQ and product access - ensuring customers get exactly what they've bought, and that downgrades, churn and offboarding are handled cleanly and on time 
Processes and playbooks: design, document and continuously improve post-sales playbooks across onboarding, adoption, renewals and expansion, so our CS and AM teams run a consistent, measurable motion 
 In this role you will also: 
Partner with CS leadership on onboarding, engagement, adoption and retention processes, including time-to-value tracking and health scoring 
Run the renewals operating rhythm with CS and Finance - renewal pipeline visibility, forecast accuracy and on-time renewals 
Administer Salesforce CPQ for post-sales motions (renewals, amendments, upsells) and own compliance and adherence to standard policies, ensuring renewal intent is documented well ahead of term end 
Own post-sales systems architecture and data flows across the tech stack, including but not limited to Salesforce, CPQ, Customer Success Platforms, Product Usage and Engagement tools, keeping data clean, connected and trusted 
Apply AI tooling to automate analysis, accelerate insight and strip manual admin out of the post-sales workflow 
Work internally with enablement to deliver content to AMs and CSMs on systems, processes and playbooks, so new ways of working actually stick 
Own book-of-business allocation for AMs and CSMs, working with Sales Ops to keep coverage balanced and aligned to territory design 
Report on post-sales KPIs - gross and net revenue retention, renewal rates, expansion pipeline and health trends - as part of our weekly business review cadence 
 Requirements
 You will have: 
At least 4 years of experience in Revenue Operations, CS Operations or Sales Operations at a B2B SaaS company, with meaningful exposure to post-sales motions 
Hands-on Salesforce expertise, including Salesforce CPQ knowledge (bonus) 
Experience with Customer Success Platforms, and other key CS tech stack tools 
A track record of building automations, health scores or signal frameworks that changed how a team acted 
A strong grasp of subscription mechanics - ARR, NRR, GRR, renewals, amendments and co-terming 
Practical AI proficiency - comfortable using AI tools (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) to build workflows, analyse data and automate repetitive work 
The ability to translate between Sales, CS and Finance, and earn trust with senior stakeholders 
A structured, proactive approach - you spot the gap, design the fix and ship it without waiting to be asked 
 Great if you have: 
Experience bridging Sales Ops and CS Ops in a single role, or having worked on both sides of the handover. 
Salesforce Admin or CPQ certification, and familiarity with data or integration tooling such as SQL, Snowflake or Zapier.

title: Manager, Commercial Operations, New Markets
description:
About FareHarbor
 At FareHarbor, our mission is to make experiences better for everyone. Founded in 2013 in Hawaii and acquired by Booking Holdings in 2018, FareHarbor creates powerful tools that enable our clients (think boat rentals, museums, food tours, events and more!) to operate and grow.
With over 20,000 clients across 90+ countries—we’re the largest in our industry and shaping the future of travel, together.
Our team is an ‘Ohana of 1,000+ people around the world. We’re passionate about pioneering an industry, embracing challenges with open arms, and delivering value to the experiences industry.
 FareHarbor Core Values
Think Client First
We Are One ‘Ohana
Be Curious and Learn
Own It.
Act With Integrity
Embrace the Challenge
 Why FareHarbor?
 Founding FareHarbor required unwavering passion. Turning a start-up into the world’s leading and largest reservation software for tours, activities, and attractions required relentless dedication and vision. To date, we’ve helped over 20,000 global businesses operate successfully and are proud to have played a role in enabling business owners to live their dreams.
And since day one, we’ve known that our real success lies in our people—the Ohana.
With each new feature launched and new client onboarded, there is a team of incredible people behind the scenes who are full of dedication, passion, energy, and the will to succeed. We encourage everyone to bring their whole selves to work—to believe in their abilities, to freely express their creativity, and to contribute with their own uniqueness by wearing their true colors. We take care of one another and always prioritize health and wellbeing. We give our people the space and trust to learn, to try, to succeed, to collaborate, to think outside of the box, to make mistakes, and even to fail. And then we come together to try again.
From the minute you join, you have a voice. You find your space. You make an impact. We celebrate our victories, shout our successes, and are always eager to tackle new challenges. And we can’t wait to see all that’s to come.
 About The Role
 We are seeking a commercially minded strategy and operations leader to help scale FareHarbor's New Markets business. This is a people-management role with direct responsibility for team members across analytics and sales operations. You will act as a strategic partner to the VP of New Markets and Commercial leadership, bringing structure to ambiguous questions, translating data into clear commercial decisions, and ensuring those decisions are implemented effectively across the organization.
You will move fluidly between strategy and execution. One day, you may frame and synthesize an ad hoc analysis on market or sales performance; the next, you may sit alongside an Account Executive to understand the reality behind the numbers, refine a process, or coordinate a cross-functional launch. You will also oversee foundational sales operations processes such as lead allocation, account ownership, target setting, performance reporting, and budgeting inputs.
The ideal candidate combines commercial judgment, analytical depth, people leadership, and operational discipline. They can challenge constructively, make complex findings accessible, and build scalable ways of working without losing sight of how Commercial teams operate in practice.
 What You’ll Do Here
Build and lead a high-performing team: Manage, coach, and develop team members across analytics and sales operations; set clear priorities, raise the quality and speed of output, and foster a commercially oriented, data-driven culture.
Advise New Markets leadership: Act as a trusted sparring partner to the VP of New Markets and other Commercial leaders, helping frame strategic questions and make data-informed decisions on growth, market priorities, resource allocation, and operating model.
Turn data into commercial action: Direct or conduct ad hoc analyses, interpret and synthesize findings, and translate them into clear recommendations and operating decisions. Pair quantitative insight with front-line context by engaging directly with Account Executives, Account Managers, and other Commercial teams.
Own commercial planning and performance management: Lead the target-setting process for Sales and Account Management, establish and maintain relevant KPIs, monitor performance, and identify gaps and opportunities. Ensure goals reflect ground-level realities while supporting long-term revenue objectives.
Oversee core sales operations: Ensure the effective execution and continuous improvement of lead allocation, client and account assignments, reporting requirements, process governance, and other recurring operational activities within the Commercial organization.
Operationalize strategy and new initiatives: Translate decisions into practical execution plans, align owners and dependencies, coordinate cross-functional stakeholders, and manage rollout, adoption, and follow-through.
Connect Commercial with the wider organization: Partner with Business Intelligence on reporting and measurement, with RevOps on targets, commission, CAC, process improvements, with Finance on budgeting and planning, and with Product, Operations, Distribution, and Global Commercial Operations on growth initiatives. Translate what is happening in the field into clear business requirements.
Build scalable processes and tools: Design, roll out, and maintain workflows, playbooks, dashboards, and decision-support tools that improve productivity, consistency, and revenue outcomes across New Markets.
Champion practical AI and automation: Identify and deploy AI-enabled tools and workflows that improve analysis, reduce administrative work, strengthen execution, and help Commercial teams serve clients more effectively.
 Requirements
5+ years of experience in commercial strategy, strategic operations, sales operations, revenue operations, or a similar role supporting go-to-market teams, including at least 2 years in a people-management role.
Experience leading or working closely with both analytics and sales operations teams, with the ability to set direction, review output, and connect insight to execution.
Strong commercial acumen and strategic judgment, with a track record of advising senior leaders and influencing high-impact decisions.
Advanced analytical problem-solving skills, including the ability to structure ambiguous questions, work confidently with data, interpret findings, and communicate a clear point of view.
A hands-on operating style and a willingness to spend time with front-line teams to understand how processes and market dynamics work in practice.
Demonstrated experience setting and operationalizing performance targets, tracking results, and partnering with Sales, Finance, Business Intelligence, and Analytics stakeholders.
A proven ability to design, implement, roll out, and maintain processes and tools for large or distributed teams, with measurable adoption and business impact.
Excellent communication, leadership, and influencing skills, with the ability to build alignment across functions and translate between commercial and technical stakeholders.
The ability to lead through change in an entrepreneurial, fast-growing environment while maintaining a strong focus on growth, efficiency, and execution quality.
Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills
Experience with SQL and Tableau or another business intelligence platform
Demonstrated interest in, or experience with, applying AI and automation to improve team performance and operational efficiency.
Experience working in technology/software. 
 Preferred Qualifications
Master’s degree or equivalent. 
Experience in travel technology or marketplaces.
This role is a strong fit for someone who is equally comfortable asking the strategic question, validating it with data, and staying close enough to execution to make the answer work in practice.
 Benefits

title: Customer Success Manager
location: United States or North Carolina or New York or Durham
description:
About the Role 
Keebler Health is building the operating system for value-based care. Our mission is to help risk-bearing healthcare organizations thrive in value-based arrangements by unlocking the full power of their data. We empower leading primary care groups, ACOs, and health plans to act on real-time insights that improve outcomes, reduce costs, and fuel sustainable growth.
We are looking for a Customer Success Manager to be the face of Keebler Health for our customers. You will own the relationship, act as the customer’s advocate inside our company, and make sure they see real value from the platform and want to grow with us. You will work closely with our Implementation team, who own the technical build, while you stay the person the customer knows and trusts from the late stages of the sale through go-live and the long-term partnership that follows.
This is a US-based remote position. We have a strong preference for candidates based in North Carolina or New York, where our team hubs are.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Customer Relationships 
Own the relationship for your portfolio of accounts, from late-stage sales through onboarding and ongoing partnership.
Join late-stage sales conversations to help set realistic expectations before contract signature.
Build trusted relationships with executive, clinical, operational, and technical stakeholders, and keep building them as people and priorities change.
Be the customer’s advocate inside Keebler Health, making sure their needs, feedback, and concerns reach Product, Engineering, and Clinical teams and get answered.
Understand each customer’s goals, challenges, and measures of success, and tell their story clearly to our internal teams.
Develop account plans, stakeholder maps, and communication rhythms for each account.
Lead regular business reviews, executive check-ins, and planning conversations.
Be a key part of renewals, and help customers get the most from their relationship with us by identifying additional features and opportunities that fit their goals.
Monitor account health and address risks, gaps, and opportunities before the customer has to raise them.
 Managing a Portfolio 
Balance competing priorities across several customers, deciding where your time and our team’s time will have the most impact.
Manage requests, issues, and escalations through to resolution, coordinating with Implementation, Support, Product, Engineering, and Clinical teams.
Set honest expectations with customers about timing and scope, and say no or not yet when you need to.
Keep commitments visible so that important details do not fall through the cracks.
Hold stakeholders, internal and external, accountable while maintaining strong working relationships.
 Working with Implementation 
Partner with the Implementation team through onboarding so the handoff to ongoing account management is smooth and nothing is lost.
Drive adoption across practices and user groups, including bringing on new users and sites over time.
Share structured customer feedback and contribute to repeatable customer success processes and playbooks.
 What Success Looks Like 
We're moving fast as a company, and things will change rapidly, but below is a sense of what success could look like in this role:
First 30 days: learn our platform, customers, and internal teams, and meet the stakeholders for your accounts as well as take ownership of steady state customers.
First 90 days: own your account portfolio, with account plans in place and your first quarterly business reviews completed.
First year: customers who are live and using the platform, clear measures of value, and renewals or expansions that reflect it.
 About You 
 Your Experience 
3-5+ years in customer success, account management, or another customer-facing role, ideally in software.
A track record of owning customer relationships and growing or renewing accounts, with measurable results.
Sales skills: you are comfortable running a commercial conversation, spotting an opening, and asking for the next step.
Credibility with senior customers and the confidence to have difficult conversations.
Strong organization and the ability to juggle competing priorities across several accounts without dropping the ball.
Ability to work with technical and non-technical teams without direct authority.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Comfortable working in an early-stage or rapidly changing environment.
Value-based care or healthcare technology experience is a nice to have, not a requirement. If you’re strong in the rest and curious about the industry, we want to hear from you.
 How You Work 
Takes ownership of outcomes and drives them forward independently.
Combines real empathy for the customer with operational discipline.
Stays calm and clear under pressure, including when a customer is unhappy.
Advocates for customers without losing sight of what is realistic for Keebler Health.
Communicates credibly with everyone from a clinician inside a practice to an executive inside a parent organization.
Motivated by compounding results, where the second year of an account is stronger because of how the first year was run.
Uses LLMs and AI tools to remove friction and build capacity, and improves the team’s systems alongside their own output.
 What We Offer 
Competitive salary, equity options, and benefits package.
A fast-paced, innovative environment.
Professional growth and development opportunities.
A collaborative and supportive team culture.
The chance to shape a foundational role and make a meaningful impact on the healthcare industry.

title: Revenue Operations Manager
description:
About Us 
AfterShip, a Great Place to Work Certified company, is transforming the global eCommerce landscape. Founded in 2012, AfterShip is a post-purchase SaaS company on a mission to build the world’s leading automation platform for ecommerce merchants.
AfterShip unifies shipping & labels, order tracking, AI predictive delivery, and returns management into one system—giving merchants a single place to manage and automate everything that happens after checkout. By centralizing these workflows, AfterShip enables merchants to reduce customer support inquiries, deliver a more reliable and engaging customer experiences, and unlock incremental revenue at every post-purchase touchpoint.
AfterShip integrates seamlessly with eCommerce platforms including Shopify and TikTok Shop, and connects with more than 1,400+ carriers worldwide. Today, over 20,000 businesses—including Samsung, Gymshark, Mejuri, Dr. Squatch, and Alo Yoga—rely on AfterShip to turn every post-purchase moment into an opportunity to build trust, reduce costs, and drive repeat purchases.
Built for a global market from day one, AfterShip operates with an engineering-driven, internationally distributed team. The company employs more than 450 people across 8 offices, spanning North America, Europe, and Asia, and representing over 20 cities worldwide.
 Your Mission: 
As Revenue Operations Manager you will own the operational backbone that keeps our Sales, Customer Success, and Partnerships teams forecasting accurately, moving fast, and working out of clean systems. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Revenue Operations, you will partner across Sales, CS, Partnerships, Finance, and Legal to drive forecast accuracy, sales ops analysis, and cross-functional projects to completion.

 Run multiple AI agents in parallel every day to reconcile records, flag exceptions, and draft process documentation. Verify the reporting logic before sharing findings.

 Turn recurring questions into reports or workflows the team can use. Track adoption and fix the parts that slow people down. 
 What you bring 
 Experience in revenue operations, sales operations, marketing operations, business operations, or a related systems and process role. 
 Strong CRM and data judgment. You can distinguish a clean report from a trustworthy operating signal. 
 The ability to work with commercial teams in plain language and build processes people will actually use. 
 Hands-on AI fluency, including directing multiple agents to analyze, draft, reconcile, and check work while validating the outcome yourself. 
 Comfort creating custom apps or workflows with agent assistance to solve repeatable operational problems. 
 A self-starting approach to ambiguous work. You can identify what is missing, propose a workable version, and improve it as evidence arrives. 
 Care for data stewardship, documentation, access boundaries, and change management. 
 Experience supporting an early-stage or rapidly changing B2B revenue team, designing attribution or campaign-to-pipeline analysis, and improving CRM adoption through simple workflows and useful reporting. 
 You work independently. You can take an unclear goal, decide what to do first, find what you need, and carry the work through to a result. You bring people in early when a decision, risk, or dependency needs their input.

 AI agents are core to how we get work done. You'll spend a substantial part of your day running multiple agents in parallel, building tools and workflows with them, and checking what they produce. You own the result. Verify the facts, calculations, code, and claims before they go into a decision, a customer conversation, or a release. 
 What success looks like 
 Leaders and commercial teams can rely on the CRM for a clear, current view of pipeline and activity. 
 Attribution and reporting definitions are explicit, inspectable, and improved when evidence shows a gap. 
 Handoffs and follow-up work have clear owners and fewer preventable misses. 
 AI-assisted operations improve speed and coverage while governance and validation remain strong.

 Annual base salary is $130,000 to $155,000 USD.

 Eligible employees can enroll in medical, dental, and vision coverage.

title: Customer Success Lead, UK Education
description:
About Kanpla
Kanpla is software for contract caterers. Ordering apps, POS and self-service kiosks, tray scanners and digital signage all come together on one platform.
What started as a school project now serves more than 800,000 users across 5,000+ locations in 14 countries. We work with operators including Compass Group, Aramark, ISS, WSH, Thomas Franks and Bennett Hay, and we are a team of more than 65 people.
How we work:
We grow fast and set high targets.
We care about product detail, because caterers use what we build every service.
We like food service and want people who are curious about how it works.
We decide quickly, learn from mistakes and fix things fast.
We are one team across several countries and spend time together at off-sites twice a year.
Own Kanpla's work with UK education caterers
The UK is Kanpla's largest market, and education is a big part of it. Our education customers are caterers who run food in hundreds of schools each. Pupils, parents and school staff use Kanpla every day to order, pay for and collect their meals.
We are hiring a Customer Success Lead to own and grow this portfolio. You will be the main contact for our education clients, set the agenda with their senior teams and shape how Kanpla looks after schools as we grow. You will report to the head of our customer success team.
The role
A single caterer may run hundreds of schools, each with its own systems, staff and parents. Every school needs to go live smoothly and keep getting value from Kanpla.
You will keep the whole picture together: account health, risks, growth, open projects and key stakeholders. You will run business reviews with senior people at caterers, work with our Delivery team to take groups of schools live on plan, and work with Product on what schools need next, including integrations with school management systems and payment providers.
The role suits someone who wants ownership and enjoys building how things are done, not only running an existing process.
What you will do
Own a portfolio of UK education clients, with responsibility for retention, growth and account health.
Run business reviews, success plans and governance with senior stakeholders at caterers.
Lead large projects and rollouts with Delivery, so programmes of schools go live on plan.
Drive adoption across schools, so caterers, parents and staff get value from Kanpla.
Use data to spot risks and opportunities early.
Bring the customer voice into Product, including integrations with school systems.
Visit clients and schools across the UK.
Write and improve our education playbook, so what works gets repeated.
What success looks like
After three months, you have a clear view of every account: health, risks, growth, open projects and key stakeholders. Clients see you as their main contact.
After six months, you lead the key conversations and set the agenda in reviews. Big projects and rollouts land on plan, and satisfaction among client admins is going up. The education playbook is written and in use.
What you will bring
Five or more years in customer success or account management, owning retention across a portfolio of customers.
Experience at a growing software company serving operators or institutions, for example in edtech, foodtech or hospitality technology.
Experience leading large projects, multi-site implementations or rollouts.
Confidence with senior stakeholders, and examples of changing a client's plan, not just reporting on it.
Something you set up from scratch: a process, a playbook, a team or a new region.
Comfort with software and data. You do not need to code.
Happy to travel to client and school sites across the UK.
Useful additional experience
It would be helpful, but is not essential, if you have:
Worked with UK schools, for example in school catering, school payments, school management systems or school edtech.
Run projects involving MIS data sync, user management or parent payments with technology partners.
Worked in contract catering or food service.
We will help you learn the sector. If the core of the role fits, we would like to hear from you even if you do not match every point.
What Kanpla offers
A senior role with real ownership in a growing international company.
A product that improves school meals and reduces food waste.
A competitive salary based on experience.
Hybrid working, with the option to work from our London Bridge office.
Two company off-sites or workcations each year.
Close work with our Delivery, Product and leadership teams.
Room to grow as our UK education business scales.
Apply
If you want to own how Kanpla works with UK schools and the caterers who feed them, we would like to hear from you.

The Ideal Candidate

About MongoDB

title: Program Manager, Go-to-Market Experience and Productivity
description:
Who we are 
 About Stripe 
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.
 About the team 
The Seller Experience & Insights team is responsible for ensuring Stripe’s Go-to-Market teams have the tools, systems, processes and policies they need to sell effectively. We identify friction in how sellers get work done, translate seller needs into scalable solutions and partner across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Sales Operations and Enablement to improve productivity and the quality of Stripe’s customer engagement.
 What you’ll do 
Stripe is evolving how Sales Development Representatives identify, engage and qualify prospective users. Agentic workflows can remove repetitive work and help SDRs focus their time on judgement-rich customer conversations. Realising that value requires more than introducing new tools: it requires a coherent end-to-end experience across targeting, outreach, task execution, lead handoff, follow-up, qualification and reporting.
You will own the business experience and improvement roadmap for Stripe’s SDR workflows. You will work closely with SDRs and their leaders to understand how work happens today, identify the highest-value sources of friction and shape tools, processes and policies that make the organisation more effective. Your initial coverage will be Stripe’s agentic outreach solution and Gong Engage , including how these capabilities interact with Salesforce, Orum, Gmail, LinkedIn and supporting routing and data services. Over time, the remit may expand to other parts of the SDR tooling and workflow ecosystem.
You will act as the connective tissue between frontline sellers and the teams that build and operate these capabilities. You will turn ambiguous problems into clear requirements, prioritised roadmaps, measurable launches and continuously improving workflows.
 Responsibilities 
Own the end-to-end SDR experience roadmap across account and contact sourcing, targeting, outreach, task execution, handraiser management, meeting disposition and qualification.
Lead the business product and operational strategy for Stripe’s agentic outreach solution and Gong Engage within Sales Development, ensuring agentic and seller-led workflows solve meaningful seller problems and fit coherently into the broader SDR operating model.
Own the experience across the hand-offs between Stripe’s agentic outreach solution and Gong Engage, including cadence creation, SDR task execution, prospect responses, meeting hand-offs and downstream activity capture.
Map current workflows and redesign them to reduce manual work, duplicate actions, context switching and avoidable failure points across SDR tools and systems.
Establish scalable mechanisms to capture, synthesise and prioritise SDR and manager feedback, combining qualitative insight with product usage, workflow, support and pipeline data.
Translate frontline needs into clear business requirements, user journeys, success criteria and prioritised recommendations for Product, Engineering, Data Science, Sales Systems and Operations partners.
Define and monitor the metrics that matter across productivity, adoption, workflow health, data quality, follow-up speed, pipeline quality and prospect experience.
Partner with Sales Development leadership, Sales Operations and policy owners to ensure tooling and workflow design reflects routing, territory, rules-of-engagement and qualification requirements.
Build launch and change-management plans with Enablement and Communications so that new capabilities are understood, adopted and embedded in daily SDR work.
Create governance and operating rhythms for agentic workflows, including release readiness, feedback triage, incident escalation, experiment review and post-launch iteration.
Identify opportunities to simplify or consolidate the SDR tooling landscape and develop evidence-based business cases for investment, deprecation or process change.
Represent the SDR experience in cross-functional planning and communicate trade-offs, progress, risks and results clearly to frontline teams and senior leaders.
 Who you are 
We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
 Minimum requirements 
3-5+ years of experience in program management, product operations, revenue operations, sales operations, product management or process improvement in a technology or high-growth environment.
2+ years of experience building, improving or supporting Sales Development or broader GTM workflows, data and systems.
Demonstrated success leading complex, global and cross-functional initiatives from problem definition through launch, adoption and iteration.
Strong understanding of how modern prospecting and sales-development workflows operate, including targeting, contact sourcing, outreach, lead routing, qualification and CRM activity capture.
Ability to map complex user journeys, identify root causes and translate ambiguous seller problems into clear requirements and prioritised solutions.
Strong analytical skills, including the ability to define success metrics, interpret workflow and funnel data and use evidence to make trade-offs.
Experience partnering effectively with technical teams and communicating across frontline, operational, product and executive audiences.
A proactive, low-ego and hands-on working style, with comfort moving between strategy and detailed execution in a rapidly changing environment.
Strong change-management skills and a track record of driving adoption, not just delivering a launch.
 Preferred qualifications 
Direct experience in Sales Development, SDR Operations or the design of SDR productivity programs.
Familiarity with Salesforce and sales-engagement, conversation-intelligence, dialing, enrichment or routing platforms such as Gong, Orum, Salesloft, LinkedIn Sales Navigator or comparable tools.
Experience designing or operating AI-assisted or agentic workflows, including human-in-the-loop controls, quality measurement and responsible-use guardrails.
Experience with experimentation, funnel analysis, SQL or business-intelligence tools.
A strong understanding of data quality, routing, rules of engagement and the downstream effects of workflow changes on reporting and seller incentives.
Experience developing enablement, documentation or operating mechanisms for global sales teams.
A passion for understanding seller behaviour and improving both employee and prospective-user experiences.
flags: no pay stated in the ad or the feed, verify vs floor
Role is pre-sale SDR tooling and workflow ownership; Tom's depth is post-sale, with no SDR or sales-engagement platform experience.

title: Revenue Operations Manager
description:
About Us 
Perk (formerly TravelPerk) is the intelligent platform for travel and spend management. Built to tackle the time-consuming, manual work that gets in the way of real work, our tools automate everything from travel bookings to expenses, invoice processing, and more. By eliminating this shadow work that wastes hours, erodes morale, and saps innovation, we're on a mission to power real work, with real impact.
We're trusted by more than 12,000 companies worldwide, including Bolt, GoCardless, and Fabletics, and we're tackling the 7 hours of lost productivity per employee each week, a $1.7 trillion problem .
Founded in 2015, Perk has grown into a global company of more than 1,800 people across 12 offices globally, with headquarters in London and Boston. We combine innovation, control, and simplicity to transform how businesses work and how people feel at work.
At Perk, we're driven by our values, like being an owner, delivering a 7-star experience, and working as one team. We value curiosity, purpose, and mindset, not just knowledge, to unlock the power in your potential. Our talent team brings together leading minds from the travel, fintech, and SaaS industries, representing over 70 countries. If you're excited about having a real impact and shaping how millions of people experience work, we'd love you on the team.
Visit www.perk.com to learn more.
 The Role 
We're looking for a Revenue Operations Manager to join our Revenue Operations team and act as a broad, senior partner to our revenue organization. You'll set and execute the strategy for how we build revenue analytics across Salesforce and Looker, run insights that shape how revenue leadership sees the business, partner closely with revenue leadership on the full range of topics they face, and, as you ramp up, take on growing ownership of the forecasting cadence alongside the Director of Revenue Operations.
This is a generalist role by design: analytics is the foundation, especially in your first two quarters, and the role broadens from there to include business partnering and forecasting. What matters most is the versatility to move across all three, not depth in any single one.
 What You'll Do 
First 90 days: Scope the revenue analytics strategy and build the core dashboards.
First 180 days: Build a highly automated revenue insights engine using AI, while establishing yourself as the business partner revenue leadership.
First 12 months: Broaden into leading and supporting the forecasting cadence.
 What Will You Be Doing? 
 Revenue Analytics & Insights 
Partner with the Director of Revenue Operations to define the revenue analytics strategy: what we need to build across Salesforce and Looker, and in what order.
Map the current reporting landscape — what exists, what's trusted, what's duplicated or out of date — and use that map to shape the build plan.
Own execution of that plan: build and maintain the core dashboards and reports that revenue leadership and the wider revenue leadership team rely on.
Launch and run a recurring insights digest for revenue leaders, turning dashboards and data into a clear narrative — what changed, why it matters, what to do about it.
Bring a point of view on what's worth building versus what's noise, and be willing to push back on requests that don't earn their keep.
 Business Partnership to Revenue leadership 
Become the go-to Revenue Operations partner for revenue leadership, covering reporting, insights, and the broader range of topics that come up in running a sales organization.
Translate revenue leadership's open questions into structured analysis and clear, actionable recommendations.
Represent revenue's priorities into the Revenue Operations roadmap, and vice versa.
Support revenue leaders in business reviews, planning moments, and ad hoc requests with credible, fast turnaround.
 Forecasting 
Run the forecasting cadence with sales leaders alongside the Director of Revenue Operations — forecast calls, pipeline reviews, and accuracy tracking.
Build and refine forecasting models based on pipeline, productivity, and historical conversion.
Conduct strategic analyses to determine forecasting trends and identify opportunities for process improvement.
 What Will You Need to Succeed? 
5+ years of experience in Revenue or Sales Operations, preferably in a SaaS or technology company operating at a global or European level.
Exposure to Account Executive (AE) or similarly quota-carrying organization.
Strong Salesforce reporting skills and working fluency in a BI tool (Looker or equivalent), with a practical, business-first approach to data.
A genuine generalist mindset — as comfortable building a dashboard or an insights report, as running a forecasting call.
A track record of setting direction and quality bar for analytical work.
Strong stakeholder management, with the ability to work with and influence sales leadership and revenue executives.
Comfortable owning ambiguous problems end to end: framing the question, choosing the method, landing the recommendation.
Excellent written communication — the insights digest is a core, ongoing deliverable of this role.
Experience partnering with global or multi-region teams is a plus.
 What we Offer 
Receive competitive compensation and equity ownership in Perk
Rest and recharge with 25 days of annual leave plus bank holidays
Take control of your physical health with private medical cover and voluntary dental insurance from Bupa, and discounted gym memberships with GymFlex
Plan for your future with our qualifying earnings company pension plan with Aviva
Know that your loved ones are protected financially through your Life Insurance if the worst were to happen
Rest assured that you’re covered by income protection in case you experience a long-term sickness or absence
Leverage tax-efficient cycle and electric car schemes with Cycle2Work & Octopus
Join our unforgettable Perk events, including our spectacular annual summer party
Always feel supported with Spring Health, our market-leading wellbeing partner, providing fast, comprehensive access to 12x therapy and 12x coaching sessions for you and your loved ones
Focus on your family with 12-16 weeks’ paid parental leave
Contribute to your community with 16 paid hours per year to spend volunteering for your dearest charitable causes
Broaden your horizons with up to 20 "Work from Anywhere" days per year
Stay savvy with access to a wide variety of discounts and rewards
Follow your passions and take a four-week, fully paid sabbatical once you reach 5 years
Let us help you move to one of our hubs with relocation support
 AI at Perk 
AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes.
 How We Work 
At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.
For certain roles, we can help with relocation from anywhere in the world, English is the official language at the office. Please submit your resume in English if you choose to apply. Do not forget to submit an updated portfolio and/or resume.
Perk is a global company with a diverse customer base, and we want to make sure the people behind our product reflect that. We’re an equal opportunity employer, which means you’re welcome at Perk regardless of how you look, where you’re from, or anything else that makes you, well, you.
 Protect Yourself from Recruitment Scams 
All official communication from Perk will always come from email addresses ending in @ perk.com or @ externalperk.com , our verified social media channels, or recruiters listed on our official LinkedIn page. We will never ask you to pay for equipment, training, or fees, request sensitive personal information such as bank details early in the process, or communicate through unofficial apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or Signal. If you receive a message claiming to be from Perk that seems suspicious, please do not respond. Forward it to security [at] perk .com , and we will confirm whether it is legitimate.
#LI-Hybrid
hard_gaps: Building revenue dashboards and analytics in Looker
Running a sales forecasting cadence and pipeline reviews
flags: no pay stated in the ad or the feed, verify vs floor
The first two quarters are analytics-heavy (Salesforce and Looker dashboard builds), where Tom has no BI tool ownership.
Forecasting cadence ownership is a stretch, since Tom contributed accounts to a forecast forum but never ran one.

The posting mentions relocation help for certain roles, so it is worth confirming sponsorship eligibility early.
verdict: Strong pivot role at a credible SaaS brand, but the Looker-heavy analytics build and forecasting ownership expose real gaps; apply with targeted framing.

title: Senior Manager - Product and GTM Enablement
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE
We are looking for a Senior Manager - Product & GTM Enablement to lead and grow our Revenue Enablement function. You will own our enablement strategy and lead a team of two, ensuring the entire Revenue organization is equipped to sell, implement, and support DataSnipper with confidence.
You will be the connective tissue between Product, Product Marketing, and our Revenue organization, ensuring that every new product release, capability update, and strategic shift is understood, internalized, and actionable by our field teams. You will work closely with PMs and the broader Product team to translate roadmap developments into role-specific enablement that reaches leaders, managers, and individual contributors alike.
This role requires someone who can operate autonomously, manage and develop a small team, and move quickly in a fast-paced environment without sacrificing quality or alignment.
ABOUT DATASNIPPER
We believe trust is essential to how society works. Every day, we rely on information that's been independently verified, from financial statements to the products we buy, to the sustainability claims companies make. Behind that trust are audit and finance professionals who examine evidence, verify information and hold organizations accountable.
At DataSnipper, we build AI solutions that empower those professionals to make those judgements. With Alwin by DataSnipper, our new agentic platform, AI agents now take on end-to-end audit and finance procedures, while every conclusion stays traceable to its source. That frees professionals to focus on the judgment and expertise that make their work so important.
We're trusted by Fortune 500 companies, government agencies and all Big Four audit firms. Today, more than 600,000 professionals across 3,000+ organizations in 175 countries rely on our platform, and in 2025 alone DataSnipper delivered more than $1.4 billion in productivity savings to its customers.
Backed by a $100 million Series B led by Index Ventures, at a $1 billion valuation, we've built a strong foundation for what's next. And as proud members of 1% for the Planet, we care about how we grow, not just how fast.
WHAT YOU WILL DO
TEAM LEADERSHIP AND MANAGEMENT
 - Lead, manage, and develop a team of two Enablement Managers, setting clear goals, providing regular coaching, and creating space for them to grow
 - Own the team's roadmap and prioritization, ensuring work is aligned to the highest-leverage opportunities across the Revenue organization
 - Operate autonomously with strong judgment on when to escalate versus drive independently
PRODUCT ENABLEMENT AND GTM READINESS
 - Partner closely with Product Managers and Product Marketing to stay ahead of the roadmap, translating upcoming releases into role-specific enablement before they reach the field
 - Design and deliver launch enablement for new product features and capabilities, ensuring leaders, managers, and ICs are equipped to speak to and demonstrate them confidently
 - Build and maintain a scalable product knowledge infrastructure including training materials, release notes for the field, and quick-reference guides that keeps the team current as the product evolves
 - Serve as the go-to internal resource for questions about how DataSnipper works, what has changed, and how to position new capabilities
REVENUE ENABLEMENT PROGRAMS
 - Design and deliver enablement programs that span the full revenue team including AEs, CSMs, SEs, and frontline managers, aligned to where they are in the customer lifecycle
 - Build and run discovery, value realization, and objection-handling training that prepares the field for tough conversations with technical and finance buyers
 - Develop and maintain playbooks, training workbooks, and enablement assets that provide consistent depth and are usable by a global team across time zones
 - Measure the impact of enablement programs through clear metrics and use data to continuously improve quality, coverage, and field performance
CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION
 - Act as the primary point of contact between Product, PMM, and the Revenue org for all enablement-related alignment
 - Build strong relationships with Revenue leaders and managers to surface gaps, gather feedback, and ensure enablement stays relevant
 - Contribute to a culture of continuous learning across the Revenue organization
WHAT YOU BRING
 - 7+ years of experience in revenue enablement, sales enablement, or a closely adjacent role within B2B SaaS
 - Demonstrated experience managing or leading a team, with the ability to set direction, give feedback, and develop people

title: GTM Strategy & Ops, Senior Manager
description:
Technology is one of the biggest items in an enterprise CFO’s budget, second only to headcount. Traditional procurement is one of the most frustrating, friction-filled bottlenecks in the modern business.
Vertice is the world’s first Intelligent Procurement Platform eliminating this chaos. By combining agentic workflows, deep AI insights, and a global network of expert negotiators, we empower enterprises to buy smarter and scale at pace.
 The Market Response Has Been Unprecedented
$75bn+ in spend processed across our platform.
20% savings consistently delivered to our customers.
70% reduction in standard enterprise procurement cycles.
13X revenue growth achieved over the last two years alone.
Founded by serial technology entrepreneurs Roy and Eldar Tuvey, who have successfully scaled and exited two category-defining platforms and created $600M+ in enterprise value, we are backed by over $100M in Series C funding from tier 1 global investors including Bessemer Venture Partners, 83North, Lakestar . We have also been recognized as the #2 fastest-growing company on the Sunday Times' Tech 100 and the fastest-growing startup in the UK and Ireland by the FT’s Sifted (#4 in Europe) .
With headquarters in London and hubs in New York, Brno, Sydney, and Johannesburg, we are fundamentally reshaping the global B2B economy.
 The role
 In a nutshell, this role would suit someone who holds an unforgiving bar for excellence who feels personal accountability for the execution of the sales motion.
You'll drive GTM strategy and enablement for a global sales organisation with a strong team across our US and EMEA offices. Leonard Maassen on AI use cases across GTM, Caldwell Harden who focuses on our North American expansion, Chris Davis on GTM systems and Constantin Clement on wider GTM projects.
This is a role about the motion itself: how Vertice pitches, positions, negotiates and closes, and what the team needs to do all of that better. The reporting engine behind the sales org is already in a good place, so the leverage sits in the craft rather than in RevOps. The work is global and you'll spend most of your time in the London HQ.
 You'll focus on three things in your first twelve months:
 #01. Raise the ceiling & the floor
 Understand what it takes to win, then embed the standard throughout the sales motion, across the team. There is no prescribed way to do this.
 #02. Selling a broad product portfolio
 Vertice is selling a portfolio of products. The best reps already excel at selling the full portfolio, because they earn more from it. Your job is to accelerate that momentum, and to do it again for whatever comes next.
 #03. Programmes for scale
 There is huge headroom across newer channels, which need GTM programmes designed, shipped and measured, alongside sharpening the ICP and pushing AI use cases into a fast-growing sales org.
You'll report to Constantin Clement, who owns GTM Strategy & Ops, Business Development, Solutions, Deals Strategy and Special Projects with Roy. Both he and Roy recognise that more attention to GTM Strategy & Ops will yield far more juice from the squeeze.
For the right person, this is a rare chance to shape how a genuinely excellent sales organisation operates, at the point where it is scaling channels, geographies and products at once, with the CEO close enough to the work to back what you build.
 About You
 We're looking for an analytical generalist with operator instincts: someone who wins the confidence of senior sales leaders and pushes work all the way into execution.
In general, we find it takes a certain type of person to thrive at Vertice: someone with a spike in their craft who is also genuinely low-ego, communicates in plain English, doesn't settle for the status quo, and gets a kick out of company building with smart people.
 In practice, it's likely you'll have most of the following:
 #01. Hold an unforgiving bar for excellence
 You are a perfectionist about the craft, and you can tell good from great in the detail rather than in the aggregate. We think the best people feel the weight of performance on their shoulders, like the sales leaders they partner with.
 "The key here is a super high bar for excellence. Can they listen to a call and have the instincts and the bar to say this wasn't great, and this is how it should be different." - Constantin Clement, Hiring Manager
 #02. Have commercial horsepower and gravitas
 You frame decisions around revenue impact rather than activity, you are quick and confident with numbers, and you command the respect of AEs and senior sales leaders well enough to challenge them and be believed.
 #03. Have built the enablement craft
 You have built assets that win deals, embedded excellence in how a team operates, and measured the impact in hard numbers (it's not important if you've had an Enablement title - if anything it's likely you don't). You're happy to screenshare the work.
 #04. Think from GTM strategy to execution
 You have architected and shipped GTM programmes end to end with measurable revenue impact. For example, you built and defended an ICP from first principles and know the nuance of a good target list in practice.
 #05. Are a stage-appropriate leader
 You have done high-ownership work in a comparable high-agency, high performance environment. Ideally you have managed at least one person, though formal line management is preferred rather than required.
 What now?
 If you're keen to keep exploring this opportunity with Vertice, let's speak.
Complete the application form and we'll be in touch if we think it's a good fit on paper.
 Final things to note
 Vertice is an equal opportunities employer, although you must be legally able to work in the specified region of the job. Any personal data you provide will be processed in accordance with Vertice's privacy policy and applicable data protection law.
We use AI-assisted tools to help us review and assess applications more efficiently. These tools support our Talent team but do not make hiring decisions autonomously. You have the right to contest any AI-assisted decision, and exercise your data subject rights by contacting us; please follow the instructions in our privacy policy.
We like to deal directly with our candidates so no agencies please!
 If you aren’t sure this job applies to you, feel free to send your CV to careers@vertice.one, and we’ll be happy to take a look and see if you could be a good fit anywhere else in our business!

title: Revenue Operations Analyst (AI-Enabled GTM Builder)
description:
Job description
 Revenue Operations Analyst (AI-Enabled GTM Builder)
Are you the kind of RevOps analyst who gets frustrated when reports don’t reflect what’s really happening, CRM fields are unreliable, and teams recreate the same report five different ways? Do you enjoy building practical solutions—clean processes, reliable data, and AI-powered workflows—that help revenue teams work faster and with more confidence?
At AIMMS, our optimization technology powers mission-critical decisions for global enterprises—from keeping energy grids stable to optimizing complex supply chains. As we scale, we’re investing heavily in operational excellence across Sales, Marketing, Pre-Sales, and Customer Success. We’ve already connected Salesforce, product usage data and other data sources around the business, and teams are actively experimenting with AI. Now we need someone to bring structure, standards, and measurable impact. 
We are looking for a Revenue Operations Analyst who is hands-on, AI-native, and excited to own the day-to-day reality of our GTM stack—making it trustworthy, usable, and scalable.
 A Role You Can Shape 
This is a role with real ownership—not a back-office reporting position. You’ll build, improve and scale how our revenue organization works, partnering with teams across Sales, Marketing, Pre-Sales and Customer Success.
What you’ll do
 Improve processes and workflows: Map how teams work and streamline lead routing, opportunity management, renewals and handovers, making ownership and next steps clear.
 Document and enable change: Create clear Confluence documentation and deliver training so new processes are easy to follow and changes stick.
 Bring structure to AI initiatives: Maintain a searchable catalog of proven AI use cases, build practical AI skills connected to tools such as Salesforce and Confluence, and set lightweight standards for readiness, adoption and ongoing review.
 Own data quality and reporting: Improve data accuracy across Salesforce, Pardot (Account Engagement), Apollo, ZoomInfo and connected platforms; establish shared metric definitions and keep dashboards consistent.
 Partner with Finance: Help align commissions, bookings, ARR, contract and renewal data, reconciling CRM and finance records and addressing gaps.
 Support revenue teams and their tools: Act as a trusted partner and first-line support for revenue leaders and reps, administer and improve relevant tools, and turn requests into clear priorities.
 Drive continuous improvement: Identify recurring issues and bottlenecks, address root causes, implement solutions and measure their impact.
Job requirements
 What will help you thrive 
You don’t need to match a rigid checklist, but you should be hands-on, structured, and comfortable operating where process, data, tools, and people meet.
You’ll thrive if you bring:
RevOps foundation: 2–5 years in revenue operations, sales operations, or business analysis—ideally in a B2B SaaS environment.
Hands-on Salesforce or HubSpot administration (reports, flows, validation rules) an Admin certification is a plus.
AI-native working style: Daily, practical use of AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, similar), with examples of something you built (workflows, automations, skills), not just prompts.
Strong analytical thinking: You can turn messy data into a clear insight and a recommendation that leaders can act on.
Documentation and enablement mindset: You document what you build and can explain it simply to non-technical colleagues.
Confident prioritization: You can juggle competing requests, make trade-offs visible, and say “no” with a clear rationale.
Communication skills: Fluent written and spoken English.
 Life at AIMMS: The Good Stuff 
 You’ll join a company where deep technology meets real-world impact—and where people genuinely care about what they build and how they work together. 
 Impact & environment 
 A role with high ownership in a fast-evolving Scale-up 
 A product-led SaaS company with strong technical foundations 
 A collaborative, international team with short lines and high trust 
 Hybrid working from our Haarlem office 
 Reward & benefits 
 💰 Competitive salary. 
 🧓 Fully paid pension. 
 🌍 Hybrid work 
 🌴 30 vacation days to properly recharge. 
 🧠 A culture that prioritizes continuous learning and skill development through coaching and training. 
 ✈️ ‘Short-term remote friendly’ the freedom to occasionally work from abroad, in alignment with the team. 
 If you’re ready to bring clarity, structure, and impact to our commercial team, apply now — we can’t wait to meet you. 
——————
 AIMMS: Who We Are (and why it matters) 
It all started in 1989, when we saw a huge untapped potential for mathematical optimization. Since then, AIMMS has touched many aspects of people’s daily lives—from the electricity delivered to our homes and the distribution of vaccines to emission-reduction policymaking. Today, as a product-led SaaS company, we support industries worldwide—from logistics to sustainability—enabling smarter, faster, and greener choices. 
 How AIMMS made impact: 
 Remember the urgency of COVID? Our technology helped Dutch hospitals predict where ICU beds and staff would run short, and decide in minutes how to spread patients so no region was overwhelmed. That’s how we turn complex data into life-saving decisions – and the kind of impact you can have here.

description:
About Kinaxis
About Kinaxis
Are you looking to join an innovative, market-leading company where you can truly elevate your career? At Kinaxis we are serious about culture, we are serious about technology, we are serious about customers, and we are serious about not taking ourselves too seriously. Our powerful, AI infused platform provides full transparency and visibility across end-to-end supply chains, enabling our customers to make faster, better decisions. Location
 This is a remote/hybrid position. You can work from home and be located anywhere in Canada. Please note if you are located in Ottawa, ON we work a hybrid schedule where you will work from our headquarters 3 days per week.

 The Regional Sales Operations Manager partners with Sales Leadership to drive pipeline execution, forecast discipline, and operational excellence across assigned North America territories.
