title: Head of Revenue Enablement
description:
Hi, I'm Romain - SVP Global Sales at hx.
I joined hx six months ago because I saw a rare mix of things: a deeply talented team, a product that is genuinely changing how insurers make decisions, and the ambition to build something category-defining in one of the world's most important industries.
The commercial opportunity in front of us is huge, but it is also complex. We sell into a market where credibility matters, where our customers are actuaries, underwriters and senior insurance leaders, and where AI needs to create real business value, not just a better story.
That is why we are hiring our first Head of Revenue Enablement. This person will help us build the operating rhythm, onboarding, materials and enablement programmes that make our global Revenue team sharper, more consistent and more credible in the field.
 A note on level: we're open on seniority for this hire. What matters most is finding the right person to build this function from scratch, not matching a specific title. If your experience sits closer to a senior enablement lead than a Head, we still want to hear from you, see the companion Revenue Enablement Lead posting for a version calibrated closer to that level.
This is not a role where you inherit a finished playbook, and it is not a role that comes with a team or budget to build one out immediately. It is a role for someone who wants to build the first version properly, hands-on, working closely with Revenue leadership, and help shape how hx sells as we continue to scale.
 About Hyperexponential (hx)
 At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry, which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.
Until now, insurers have been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision, helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.
Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally, already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.
What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do, from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.
What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure, it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.
If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.
 About The Team
 hx's commercial engine is scaling rapidly, and Revenue Enablement sits at the heart of making that scale sustainable. Today, enablement happens across pockets of the organisation, Revenue leadership, RevOps, Sales Ops, Product Marketing, and Marketing, but there's no single owner, no operating cadence, and no clear system for turning commercial strategy into repeatable field execution.
This is where you come in. You'll be building hx's first dedicated Revenue Enablement function from scratch, working in close partnership with Romain and the wider commercial leadership team. Your mission is to close the gap between intent and execution: improving how our sellers are trained, equipped, motivated, and held to a consistent operating rhythm that drives revenue.
You'll take an AI-first approach to how enablement gets built at hx. That means using AI tools to accelerate content creation, calibrate messaging against live deal data, and build feedback loops faster than a traditional enablement function could, not just producing more content, but producing a smarter, faster system.
In this role, you'll treat enablement as a system, not a content library. You'll bring structure and pace to a high-performing sales organisation, staying close to the customer, the field, and the behaviours that actually move deals forward. This is a builder role for someone who thrives in ambiguity and sees the opportunity to shape how a world-class commercial team operates, hands-on, not from a distance.
 Check out our Sales and Partnerships Candidate Hub for a behind the scenes look at the team you would be joining!
 What you'll be doing
Build hx's first Revenue enablement operating model, defining clear scope, ownership, intake processes, prioritisation frameworks, and success metrics that make enablement predictable and aligned to commercial priorities.
Create and execute the 2026 Revenue enablement roadmap, translating commercial OKRs into a focused programme of training, content, and rhythms that improve seller effectiveness and execution discipline.
Drive measurable improvements in seller behaviour, designing enablement programmes that strengthen qualification, discovery, deal progression, sales process adherence, Salesforce hygiene, and forecasting accuracy.
Strengthen customer-centric selling by equipping the sales team with better customer insight, references, case studies, proof points, and value messaging that make sellers more credible and commercially sharp in every conversation.
Partner closely with Marketing, Product Marketing, and ABM to ensure sellers can confidently use targeted messaging, launch materials, competitive positioning, and customer stories in the field.
Design scalable onboarding and continuous learning programmes with clear curriculum, measurable ramp indicators, manager reinforcement, and defined productivity milestones for commercial hires.
Use AI tools directly and hands-on to build, iterate, and scale enablement assets and programmes rather than relying solely on manual content production.
What you'll need to have done
Built or significantly scaled Revenue enablement in a B2B SaaS, enterprise software, or complex commercial environment, demonstrating that enablement is about changing seller behaviour, not just producing training content.
Designed and implemented enablement operating models that include intake, governance, stakeholder alignment, measurement, and repeatable cadences across Revenue, Marketing, Product Marketing, and Operations teams.
Delivered programmes that measurably improved seller effectiveness, such as better discovery execution, increased win rates, faster ramp times, improved Salesforce adoption, or stronger commercial discipline in live deals.
Partnered cross-functionally with senior commercial leaders, earning trust through pragmatic judgement, clear prioritisation, and demonstrable revenue impact rather than relying on formal authority.
Created structured onboarding and ongoing learning programmes that shortened time-to-productivity for new hires, with clear curriculum, reinforcement mechanisms, and measurable outcomes.
Used customer insight, market context, references, and proof points to improve how sellers engage with prospects, demonstrating commercial credibility and customer-centricity in enablement design.
Been comfortable building alone, without a team, at least in the first phase of the role.
You're unlikely to thrive here if
Your experience is mainly in content production, LMS administration, or training delivery without building the operating system and structure around enablement.
You need an existing playbook to follow, or see enablement as separate from sales execution, commercial strategy, customer insight, and cross-functional operating cadence.
You're a strategist who struggles with hands-on delivery, or someone who prefers working in isolation rather than collaborating closely with Revenue leadership, Marketing, RevOps, and frontline sellers.
You're looking for a role with a team and budget to build out from day one.
If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energized, hx may not be the place where you will do your best work. We are building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.
 Compensation
 At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process, our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations, and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.
Equity: We offer equity across all roles at hx, making it a significant component of total compensation. Your Talent Partner will be able to share more details about this.
 Benefits
 £5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.
25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).
Company pension scheme via Penfold.
Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life.
Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.
Private healthcare insurance through AXA.
Income protection and Life Insurance.
Cycle to Work Scheme.
Additional perks
Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).
Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.
Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.
Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.
Interview process
Initial call with our Talent team to kick things off.
Manager interview with our SVP of Sales.
Skills assessment: 60-minute working session where you'll present your diagnosis of the enablement opportunity at hx, a proposed 6-month enablement plan, your operating model for intake and prioritisation, and one example enablement programme designed to improve seller behaviour in practice.
Values interview + Meet the CEO
We offer!
Our commitment to Diversity
hxer's are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.
Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.
If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.
Next steps
If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.
For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.
 Please note that background checks will be conducted as part of the hiring process to ensure compliance with our governance policies. We handle all background checks sensitively and in full compliance with relevant regulations. All applicant data will be processed in accordance with data protection regulations and our privacy policy.

title: Aptitude Software - GTM Sales Enablement Manager
description:
GTM Sales Enablement Manager - Fynapse
 Team: Fynapse GTM
 Reports to: Global Head of Sales Engineering
 Location: London
 Travel: Regular international travel expected across our US, UK & Australia sales offices
 Level: Individual contributor
 Why this role exists
 Fynapse is a Finance ERP built around a Super Ledger. Selling it well means being fluent in three things at once: what the platform actually does, why a CFO or Group Controller would fund it, and how the conversation changes between a bank tracing a group balance back to source for its regulator, an insurer consolidating across dozens of legal entities, a telco drowning in billing volume, and a PE-backed SaaS business preparing for IPO.
We already have people who do this exceptionally well. The opportunity is to make what they know something the whole team owns as we scale new logo, migration of our existing enterprise base, and, in time, a partner ecosystem.
 This is a product and industry enablement role rather than a sales methodology one ; we already have a sales process. What we need is someone who can teach people to sell this product, to these buyers, in these industries, and keep that current as the platform evolves.
This is a new role: the programme, the tooling and the standard are all yours to build. You will be measured on ramp time and certification coverage, not on sessions delivered or assets published.
 What You'll Own
 GTM onboarding: product and industry ramp
Own the product and industry onboarding journey for every new GTM hire: AEs, BDRs, Sales Engineers & Account Managers.
Design role-specific paths. For example, a BDR needs the qualification filter and the trigger events; a Sales Engineer needs platform architecture and the demo narrative. Same content spine, different depth.
Build in verification, not just delivery. A new AE should be certified to run a first meeting unsupervised, and we should know how long this takes to be effective.
Coach the team to reduce the time to first qualified opportunity.
 The core curriculum - value, buyers and business case
Teach the value propositions and keep the language consistent: headline positioning, the deployment models, how to run discovery, how to quantify need, how the architecture creates the value, and how our approach to AI differs.
Teach the buyer map: CFO, Group Financial Controller, Finance Transformation Director, Chief Accounting Officer, Finance Systems Manager, CIO, PE Operating Partner: understand each intimately, what they value, and how to position for it.
Teach business case construction: close cycle cost, headcount avoidance, cost of inaction, uptick in revenue. The team should be able to co-build a quantified case with a prospect, not present a generic ROI deck.
Teach the triggers and how to spot them in research, so the team qualifies on compelling event rather than on interest.
Teach industry context to a credible level in our priority verticals: Banking, Insurance, Payments, SaaS, Telcos; with working knowledge of the other adjacent sectors too.
Adapt the curriculum for regional reality. North America, UK & Ireland and Australia are priority markets, and they do not sell the same way regulators, competitive set and sector priorities all differ. The core narrative stays consistent; worked examples, reference customers and compliance drivers should be relevant to the team in the room.
 Migration of the existing base
 This is a priority, not a side project. Our long-standing enterprise clients on our established finance products match almost exactly the profile we sell Fynapse into warm, well-qualified, trusted relationships that need a fundamentally different conversation from net new.
Build and own the enablement for the migration conversation: why now, what changes, what the client gains, how the risk is managed, how it is sequenced.
Equip account teams to run that conversation with sponsors who have known us for years, and to handle "we're happy as we are" without damaging a relationship we value.
Build the expansion playbook; explain what else a client can benefit from once migrated.
Work with Account Management so the commercial narrative and the delivery reality match.
 Maintaining the standard
Create certification on industry narratives, demo storylines, business case creation, objection handling, and competitive positioning.
Coach in the flow of work, call reviews, deal debriefs, live calls, pre-meeting prep. Not an annual training event.
Diagnose rather than assume. Use call recordings, win/loss, stage conversion and pipeline quality to find where the team is weak, then fix that.
Refresh the standard whenever the product, the competitive set or the market shifts.
 Build the function
Be pragmatic about tooling. You'll shape what we use, we don’t want to create more admin for our teams. Get real value out of what we already have and be resourceful, including with AI.
Make knowledge findable at the point of need. Someone in pre-call prep at 4pm should be able to self-serve in two minutes.
 Autonomy and guardrails
 You have full latitude over how we enable: curriculum design, certification model, onboarding structure, cadence, how success is measured, what gets built and what gets deleted, and how we use the tooling available to us. Nobody here has a fixed view on any of it.
The exception is core positioning, headline messaging, how we frame the deployment models, approved language on what is live versus roadmap, and how we talk about competitors. That is set with Product and Product Marketing. You will have a strong voice in shaping it and we expect you to challenge it, but you don't own it.
Everything else is yours to define.
 How You'll Work
 We want a practitioner, not a preacher; treated as part of the deal team, someone AEs pull into prep calls because it makes the meeting better.
Co-create. Build the playbook with the top performers, not for them. Much of the job is extracting what already works and making it teachable.
Curate. A short, current, trusted set of material beats a large library nobody opens. Deleting is part of the job.
 Across three regions. Our sales teams sit in the US, UK and Australia, so this must work without you in the room. Design enablement that holds up, self-serve material, recorded modules, certification that runs without you. Travel is non-negotiable; people learn best in person, so we like roleplays, scenarios and hot seat exercises.
 Where this role grows
 Two things to grow into once the internal foundation is solid:
Externally facing. In front of prospects and clients - running value or industry sessions, supporting complex deals, presenting at client and industry events.
Partner and ecosystem enablement. As the partner motion matures, build the version of the curriculum that works for advisory, implementation and reseller partners who need to position and qualify Fynapse, and know when to bring us in.
 Success
 First 90 days
Fluent enough in Fynapse to run the product narrative and a first meeting unaided.
A baseline assessment of team capability, with gaps named and evidenced from pipeline and call data.
An onboarding path defined for one GTM role and run with an employee.
 By 12 months
Onboarding live across all GTM roles, with certification and a measurable reduction in ramp time.
Migration enablement built and in the hands of account teams.
A feedback loop into Product and Product Marketing that people actively use.
Job requirements
 Essential
 Who you are
You have sold finance software into our target industries: banking and financial services, alongside insurance, technology and SaaS, telecommunications, or comparable regulated, high-volume environments.
Existing finance and accounting knowledge. You can hold an unaided conversation with a Group Financial Controller about month-end close, reconciliation, subledger-to-GL flow, revenue recognition and audit lineage, and teach it to someone who can't.
You have carried a number or owned customer outcomes directly: as an account manager, net new seller, sales engineer or pre-sales consultant, or in a client-facing consulting role where you were accountable for the outcome. You can talk about deals you won, deals you lost and why.
Experience migrating clients from an established platform onto a newer one and enabling others to have that conversation.
Can translate a technical platform into a buyer-relevant narrative and pitch it at the right altitude for a CFO versus a Finance Systems Manager.
Facilitation and coaching skill across a range of go-to-market functions.
Pipeline-literate and data-driven. You go into call recordings, win/loss and stage conversion yourself to find where the team is weak - and you can show the number moved after you fixed it.
Comfort with ambiguity, and the discipline to re-teach something a month after you taught it.
Experience enabling distributed teams across time zones, and a track record of making things stick without being in the room.
 Desirable
Qualified or part-qualified accountant (ACA / ACCA / CIMA / CPA), or equivalent practical depth.
Direct experience with ERP, subledger, accounting engine, revenue recognition or financial close software.
Awareness of the accounting standards that drive our clients' reporting, across both IFRS and US GAAP.
Experience enabling partner or channel ecosystems, including advisory and systems integrator relationships.

In 2021, Great Place To Work® was acquired by UKG (Ultimate Kronos Group.) As a leading global provider of HCM, payroll, HR service delivery, and workforce management solutions, UKG believes organizations succeed when they focus on their people. While Great Place To Work® will continue operating independently within the UKG family, our research and insights will help UKG differentiate its best-in-class HR, talent, and workforce management technology, and together we'll support every workplace to become great. UKG has 15,000 employees around the globe and is known for its inclusive and supportive workplace culture and best-in-class rewards and benefits.
Both UKG and Great Place To Work® are leading the change on what it means to be a Great Place To Work® for all, and we are proud to be Certified™ great workplaces!
 About the Position 
We are looking for a Senior Sales Operations Analyst to build and run the operating discipline that enables Sales to execute consistently and scale effectively. This role sits at the intersection of sales strategy, planning, execution, technology, and analytics.
As our new-logo sales motion evolves from primarily inbound to a more structured outbound model, this role will partner with Sales leadership to shape how we plan, prioritize, and execute. You will own the operating cadence, processes, and systems that keep teams aligned, maintain pipeline and forecast discipline, and enable sellers to focus on the opportunities that matter most.
This is a senior individual-contributor role for someone who can take ambiguous business challenges, apply strong analytical and operational judgment, and turn them into practical solutions. You will bring a point of view, challenge existing approaches, and actively shape how we operate, informed by data, technical feasibility, and what will most effectively improve seller productivity and revenue performance. Success requires someone equally comfortable advising Sales leadership, working with frontline managers, and rolling up their sleeves to solve complex operational problems.
 Key Responsibilities 
Partner with Sales Leadership to establish and run a consistent quarterly operating cadence: planning, business reviews, forecast reviews, deal inspections, and key execution milestones.
Establish consistent operating processes and expectations across teams and segments, ensuring leaders and sellers have the information and accountability needed to act.
Proactively identify execution gaps, competing priorities, and operational friction, recommending improvements that keep teams focused on pipeline progression and revenue attainment.
Strengthen forecast accuracy and pipeline health through consistent opportunity management standards, qualification criteria, stage governance, and data quality.
Participate in forecast and pipeline reviews, bringing independent analysis, identifying risks, and reinforcing sales process discipline with frontline managers.
Develop reporting and leading indicators for pipeline creation, coverage, conversion, deal progression, and seller performance, translating findings into actionable recommendations.
Partner with Sales Leadership to develop capacity, quota, territory, and account coverage recommendations, modeling scenarios informed by performance, market opportunity, and business priorities.
Develop account segmentation, scoring, prioritization, and territory strategies that improve market coverage, balance seller portfolios, and identify whitespace opportunities.
Manage account assignment, ownership, recycling, and coverage processes across Salesforce and related systems, ensuring accurate data and consistent execution.
Partner with Demand Generation, Events, and Sales Leadership to translate targeted GTM programs into executable seller workflows, advising on audience selection, prioritization, and operational approach.
Build and improve account distribution, engagement processes, and standardized seller workflows, including Gong Engage, to support consistent outbound execution.
Work directly with sellers and managers to identify friction, improve adoption, and develop solutions that reduce administrative work and increase selling time.
Serve as a recognized operational expert across Salesforce, Gong, 6sense, Unify, and related GTM technologies, understanding how they connect to support Sales execution.
Identify, design, and implement automation, AI, and technology improvements that increase seller productivity and operational efficiency, evaluated against cost and business impact.
Lead cross-functional process improvements with Revenue Systems & Architecture, from technical requirements and integration through adoption and scalable execution.
 Success In This Role Looks Like 
Operating discipline: Sales operates against a consistent quarterly rhythm with clear milestones, effective reviews, and reliable follow-through. Leaders have visibility into pipeline health, deal progression, and forecast risks, supported by consistent processes and trustworthy data.
Sales coverage and execution: Territories, account assignments, and seller priorities are aligned to market opportunity and business objectives, with clear ownership and minimal operational friction.
Seller productivity: Sellers and managers spend less time on systems and administrative tasks, and more time engaging customers and advancing opportunities.
Business impact: Operational improvements contribute measurably to pipeline generation, forecast accuracy, seller productivity, and revenue attainment.
Strategic partnership and innovation: Sales leadership has a proactive partner who challenges assumptions, brings practical solutions, and continuously improves how the organization operates.
 Required Qualifications 
5+ years of experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Sales Analytics, or a comparable GTM operations role.
Hands-on experience with sales forecasting, pipeline management, territory and account operations, and recurring operating cadences including forecast reviews, business reviews, and planning cycles.
Depth of expertise in Sales Operations, with working knowledge of related disciplines including Finance, Revenue Systems, Marketing Operations, and GTM analytics.
Strong analytical, data-reconciliation, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work with complex data, build models, and surface actionable insights.
Strong working knowledge of Salesforce, including opportunity management, reporting, dashboards, account ownership, and core CRM workflows.
Demonstrated ability to evaluate complex business problems, challenge existing approaches, develop practical solutions, and lead cross-functional initiatives from requirements through adoption.
Ability to influence stakeholders, communicate complex concepts, and work effectively with senior Sales leaders and frontline managers.
Comfortable operating independently in ambiguous or evolving environments, with guidance needed only in the most complex situations.
Comfortable operating independently in ambiguous or evolving environments with strong attention to detail and sound business judgment. Guidance needed only in the most complex situations.
Track record of proactively identifying and evaluating new techniques, technologies, and approaches to improve Marketing effectiveness.
 Preferred Qualifications 
Experience with Gong/Gong Engage and account-based or outbound platforms such as 6sense or Unify.
Experience with account segmentation, market coverage, account prioritization, scoring, and whitespace analysis.
Experience developing and maintaining opportunity management standards, qualification criteria, and sales process governance.
Experience building or applying AI-powered tools, automation, or connected workflows that improve seller productivity and decision-making.
Experience supporting a transition from inbound to structured outbound, including operationalizing GTM programs with Demand Generation or Marketing Operations.
Experience modernizing fragmented workflows, addressing operational technology debt, or integrating data across sales systems.

 The pay range for this position is $94,000 to $113,975 . The actual base pay offered may vary depending on skills, experience, job-related knowledge and work location. In addition to base pay, employees may be eligible to participate in a performance-based bonus plan and to receive restricted stock unit awards as part of total compensation. Make Your Mark: 
With very limited direction, the Customer Success Manager 3 (CSM3) delivers post-sales efforts to their assigned customers via a consultative Customer Success program strategy specifically associated with BlackLine onboarded customers. This program strategy encompasses the activities, resources, and relationships necessary to optimize customers' adoption of subscribed licenses and products, prevent attrition and churn, and continually enhance customer health and satisfaction. The CSM3 uses their immense expertise in the Company's platform and products as well as their domain expertise to provide best practice deliverables. These deliverables include coaching, Business Reviews, Customer Success Reviews, Success Planning that aligns to the customer corporate goals and objectives and are required to ensure the customer is receiving the value expected from their BlackLine subscription and moving through their customer journey. Due to their extensive accounting industry knowledge as well as their BlackLine knowledge, the CSM 3 is able to effectively provide guidance to clients on how to best adopt BL tools considering the entire finance transformation client journey. title: Head of Customer Success
description:
About Us 
At Colossyan, we help modern teams create, manage, and scale training and enablement content with AI.
Leading organisations such as Paramount, Ericsson, Continental AG, Cisco, Johnson & Johnson, and UPS use Colossyan to transform knowledge into engaging, scalable training and enablement experiences. By combining AI-powered video and authoring with intuitive design, teams can turn existing knowledge into structured, interactive content and deliver it across global organisations efficiently. To date, more than 1 million videos have been created using Colossyan, and we’ve been recognised as a G2 Leader across multiple product categories.
We’re also proud to have received the Red Dot Design Award for product design.
Colossyan enables teams to:
- Transform documents, presentations, and prompts into structured training content
- Create AI-powered learning experiences with avatars, narration, and visual storytelling
- Build interactive training programs with modules, media and assessments to drive engagement
- Translate and localise training into 100+ languages instantly
- Keep knowledge up to date by quickly editing and maintaining training content as information evolves
- Measure effectiveness with analytics and insights
Behind the product is a fast-growing, international team of 70+ people united by a passion for technology and its potential to help organisations scale knowledge more effectively. We foster a culture of collaboration, curiosity, and continuous learning, and we’re committed to supporting the personal and professional growth of every team member.
Our mission is to democratise organisational knowledge and make it easy for teams to create, update, and scale training and enablement across the entire company.
To learn more about our product features, visit colossyan.com .
Why this role exists
Our customers are global enterprises, and the next phase of our growth comes as much from keeping and growing them as from winning new logos. We're looking for a Head of Customer Success to own that outcome: retention, expansion and the customer experience behind both. This is a player-coach role. Roughly 70% of your time is hands-on with our most strategic accounts; roughly 30% is building and leading the team. If you want to run the function and still be the person in the renewal call, this is for you.
What you will own
 Retention. Own gross and net revenue retention across the customer base. Carry a book of our most strategic enterprise accounts yourself, run their renewals and expansions, and set the standard for how every account is managed.
 Playbooks. Design and run the retention playbooks: the renewal cycle, early-warning signals (adoption, champion change, procurement, competition), executive sponsorship, and value proof through ROI stories and our newer products (Learn, Cora and our knowledge-transfer agent).
 Expansion. Build the CS-sourced expansion motion with Sales: seats, new teams and new products inside existing customers, with clear triggers, plays and hand-offs.
 Operating system. Be the business owner of our AI-native customer success platform: health scoring, risk and expansion signals, forecasting, and a weekly view of the book for the executive team.
 Team. Lead and coach Customer Success Managers, hire another for the team, and design how our next stage of Enterprise growth is covered, from high-touch enterprise accounts to a digital-led long tail.
 Voice of the customer. Bring what customers need back to Product and Marketing, and turn customer outcomes into stories the whole company can use.
Who you are
 Must haves 
7+ years in Customer Success or post-sales at a B2B SaaS company, including time leading a team or running a function as a player-coach.
Experience at a seed, Series A or Series B startup: you have built or scaled a CS function with limited resources and know what good looks like at this stage.
A track record of improving retention and driving expansion on enterprise accounts, with the renewals, negotiations and executive relationships to show for it.
Hands-on and commercial: comfortable owning a number, running a difficult renewal yourself and writing the playbook afterwards.
Data-led and AI-enabled: you build health scores and forecasts you'd defend to a board, and you use a modern CS platform as an operating system, not a reporting tool.
A clear, direct communicator who can present to executives, customers and the team.
Driven and diligent, with a strong attention to detail: this is a critical role, with potential to grow into a senior leadership role in the company.
Based in London and happy to be in the office three days a week.
 Nice to have 
Experience selling to or serving L&D, HR or enablement buyers.
Experience with AI products, or with helping customers adopt new product lines.
Experience with partner- or reseller-sourced customers.
Experience adopting AI native customer success platform.
 What we offer: 
 Stock options: We want everyone to feel motivated to do their best work, which is why we’re all owners.
 Remote work: Enjoy extra flexibility with one full week of remote work per quarter.
 Free lunch Thursdays and breakfast Tuesdays: Build team connections over complimentary weekly breakfast and lunches.
 Great office location: Work from our centrally-located, pet-friendly office designed for comfort and team collaboration.
 Birthday time off: Celebrate your birthday with an additional paid day off, if it falls on a weekday, separate from your regular vacation allowance.
 Flexible annual leave: Enjoy 25 days of annual leave with the unique option to convert the 8 bank holidays into working days and boost your annual leave allowance to 33 days. Choose what works best for you.
 Private healthcare: Access private healthcare through Bupa, including talk therapy and physiotherapy. We understand that everyone does their best work when they’re happy and healthy.
 Retirement planning: We offer matched salary sacrifice pension with Smart Pension.
 Cutting-edge AI technology: Be at the forefront of AI innovation, working directly with state-of-the-art AI technologies that form the core of our product.
 Impact: As a rapidly expanding Series A startup, your contributions will have an immediate impact on our global development!
At Colossyan, we believe that diversity drives innovation and inclusion fosters a sense of belonging. We are committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels valued, respected, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. 
We actively seek to build a diverse team and encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds and beliefs to apply to our open positions.
We strongly encourage individuals from underrepresented and/or marginalised identities to apply. If you need any accommodations for your interview, please email recruitment@colossyan.com
hard_gaps: Time leading a team or running a CS function
Built or scaled CS at seed/Series A/B startup
flags: title band: director_plus -- check the JD for actual scope and comp
CSM in UK-London at a non-standout company
no pay stated in the ad or the feed, verify vs floor
A 70-person Series A startup may not hold a UK sponsor licence; confirm before applying.
Head of CS is a CS leadership track rather than a RevOps pivot, though platform ownership and forecasting add ops depth.
Enterprise training-content product overlaps closely with NAVEX compliance-training renewals and usage reconciliation, a real talking point.
verdict: Strong post-sale content fit, but no people leadership or startup tenure; both are stated must-haves at a small, sponsorship-uncertain Series A.

title: Sales Operations Manager
description:
Job Description 
 Job Title: 
 Sales Operations Manager
 Posting Start Date: 
 27/10/2026
 Job Description: 
 Sales Operations Manager 
 Location: London / Hybrid
 Reports to: Senior Sales Operations Manager
 Employment type: Full-time
 About the role 
As Sales Operations Manager, you'll help run the systems, processes, and analytics that power how Bell Integration sells. Working closely with the Senior Sales Operations Manager, you'll own key workstreams, from CRM administration to pipeline reporting and forecasting support, and help the sales team close more deals and scale efficiently. You'll also partner with Sales, Marketing, Finance, and Customer Success to solve problems and turn data into decisions.
 What you'll do 
 Process and systems 
Administer day-to-day CRM operations (Salesforce), including configuration, workflows, user management, and troubleshooting
Support integrations and the broader sales tech stack, partnering with the Senior Sales Ops Manager on tool evaluation and rollout
Identify process gaps from lead handoff through closed-won and renewal, and implement improvements
Document processes and drive adoption across the sales team
 Forecasting and analytics 
Support the weekly, monthly, and quarterly forecasting cadence by preparing data, validating pipeline accuracy, and flagging inconsistencies
Build and maintain dashboards and reports on pipeline health, conversion rates, win/loss, and rep productivity
Deliver clear insights and recommendations to Sales leadership, with guidance from the Senior Sales Ops Manager
 Planning and performance 
Support annual and quarterly planning, including territory analysis, quota modelling, and capacity planning
Assist with commission calculations and comp plan administration in partnership with Finance
Track performance against targets and surface risks and opportunities early
 Cross-functional partnership 
Partner with Sales Enablement on onboarding, training materials, and playbooks
Work with Marketing on lead routing and scoring, and with Finance on bookings
Act as a point of contact for sales team questions on systems, data, and process
 What we're looking for 
 Required 
5 years in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, or a related analytical role, ideally in B2B, IT reseller, systems integrator, MSP, or distributor, with an understanding of vendor-led and multi-product sales.
Hands-on experience with Salesforce, including reporting, workflows, and automation
Strong analytical skills and comfort with data (advanced Excel/Sheets; SQL or BI tools such as Tableau, Looker, or Power BI a plus)
Experience supporting forecasting processes and building pipeline and performance reports
Clear communicator who can explain data and recommendations to sales leaders and cross-functional partners
Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams and take direction as well as initiative
 Nice to have 
Exposure to territory planning, quota setting, or comp plan design
Salesforce Administrator certification
 Why Join Bell Integration? 
A collaborative, fast-paced environment where you can make an impact.
Exposure to strategic decision-making across the business.
Opportunities for personal growth and career development, including exposure to digital, automation, and AI-enabled ways of working.
Competitive salary, bonus, and benefits package.
 Apply now
hard_gaps: 5 years in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations or related analytical role
flags: no pay stated in the ad or the feed, verify vs floor
Day-to-day Salesforce administration is core duty; candidate has cert but no production org admin time.
IT reseller/systems integrator context prefers vendor-led multi-product sales experience, not SaaS post-sale.
Reports into a Senior Sales Ops Manager with support-heavy duties, so a mid-level band may sit near the £70k visa floor.
Mid-size IT services firm; sponsor licence status unconfirmed and should be checked on the UK register.
verdict: Genuine Sales Ops pivot role in London, but a support-level, reseller-context position with likely tight comp versus the sponsorship floor.

title: Senior Revenue Operations Manager, EMEA
description:
The world of payment processing is rapidly evolving, and businesses are looking for loyal and strategic partners, to help them grow.
 Meet Nuvei , Nuvei is the global fintech building the infrastructure for every payment, everywhere. Its modular, flexible, and scalable technology enables leading companies to accept next-generation payments, offer all payout options, and benefit from card issuing, banking, risk, and fraud management services. Connecting businesses to their customers in more than 200 markets, with local acquiring in 52 markets, 150 currencies, and over 720 alternative payment methods, Nuvei provides the technology and insights for customers and partners to succeed locally and globally through one integration.
At Nuvei, we live our core values, and we thrive on solving complex problems. We're dedicated to continually improving our product and providing relentless customer service. We are always looking for exceptional talent to join us on the journey!
 Your Mission
 We are looking for a seasoned Senior Revenue Operations Manager to join our fast-growing EMEA Revenue Operations team. Reporting to our Head of Revenue Operations EMEA you support the development and implementation of regional revenue growth and go-to-market initiatives, as well as long-range strategic plans for our Enterprise business.
 Key Responsibilities
Commercial Performance: Lead deep-dive analysis of revenue, customer, and sales performance data to uncover trends, diagnose issues, and generate strategic insights for leadership decision-making
Develop materials and business cases that drive Strategic Growth Initiatives to accelerate revenue growth and increase transacting customers across key segments and markets
Cross-Functional Leadership: serve as a strategic partner to Sales, Marketing, Product, and Finance to align on goals, share insights, and ensure end-to-end execution of revenue strategy
Support annual and quarterly planning processes by providing structure, analytical rigor and insight-backed recommendations
Pipeline Management & Forecasting: Lead and execute sales pipeline management and forecasting processes to improve forecast accuracy, accelerate pipeline velocity and drive business outcomes
Market & Competitor Analysis: monitor and report on the FinTech ecosystem, tracking competitor pricing motions, market trends, and shifts in card network (Visa/Mastercard etc) and alternative payment method (APM) costs
Analysis of payment economics (Interchange, Scheme Fees, Processing Costs) to identify margin leakage, recommend pricing adjustments, routing optimizations to drive commercial growth across EMEA 
Partner with cross functional teams to design, implement, and iterate on sales processes that support strategies for our core payment gateway, acquiring services, and SaaS products
Develop presentations and materials for senior leadership to effectively convey the team's initiatives
 Requirements
7+ years of experience and proven track record of success in revenue operations, revenue strategy, pricing, Go-to-Market or related roles within the Fintech or payments industries
Strong analytical skills with experience in financial modelling, data analysis, and market research
AI-native, with a strong understanding of how to apply AI tools and automation to improve decision-making, productivity and business outcomes
Excellent oral and written communication skills, including the ability to translate complex information into clear, audience-appropriate messages
Strong leadership and communication skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams
Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, adapt to shifting priorities, maintain attention to detail, and deliver on time
Ability to work independently to strict timelines while collaborating effectively with a diverse team of professionals
Comfortable wearing multiple hats, navigating ambiguity and taking on responsibility beyond the traditional scope of Revenue Operations when needed
Experience working in a global or multi-regional environment is preferred
Professional fluency in English required
 Benefits
Private Healthcare
10% Pension
25 days annual leave
30% ruling

title: GTM Growth Lead
description:
Who we are
Validere is the enterprise intelligence platform for the energy industry. Our all-in-one platform empowers energy companies to make smarter decisions by streamlining operations with integrated data, automation, and predictive insights.
Over 50 of the world’s leading energy companies rely on Validere’s technology and multidisciplinary experts to improve their operations and navigate complex compliance requirements with clarity and ease. The company has offices in Toronto and Calgary.
The Role
Validere is hiring a GTM Growth Lead to create more high-quality opportunities for our enterprise Sales team and build better ways to pursue them.
This is a senior individual contributor role. You will find promising growth opportunities, design ways to pursue them, personally get the first version into market, give Sales a usable motion, measure what happens, and repeat what works.
This role is focused on enterprise accounts and Sales opportunities rather than high-volume lead generation. Success is measured by the quality of conversations, opportunities, and pipeline created.
We're looking for someone who finds opportunities we haven't told them to find.
You might notice the same problem coming up across several Sales conversations, develop a campaign hypothesis around it, build the target audience and initial messaging, create or repurpose the content needed to support the motion, launch it with Sales, and determine whether the signal is strong enough to scale.
This isn't a role for someone who stops at strategy or hands execution to someone else. The first version should be something you can launch, not a plan for other people to pick up.
You'll have access to HubSpot, Apollo, and modern automation and AI tools to help execute and scale your work. We expect you to be comfortable working directly in the tools, but this is not simply a marketing operations or RevOps role.
What You Will Do
Find and prioritize opportunities
Look across accounts, audiences, existing relationships, events, market signals, and emerging themes for commercial opportunities Sales is not already pursuing. 
Use GTM, campaign, account, and Sales data to identify patterns, gaps, and opportunities worth investigating. 
Guide which conferences, associations, roundtables, and other industry events are worth the investment, based on the target accounts, buyers, themes, and commercial opportunities they bring together. 
Build targeted pre- and post-event motions that help Sales know who to meet, why to engage them, and how to turn event conversations and insights into follow-up opportunities. 
Identify new stakeholders, business units, use cases, or reasons to engage inside enterprise relationships we already have. 
When the same pattern shows up across Sales conversations, events, data, or accounts, bring it forward as something to test. 
Design and run the motion
Turn an opportunity into a clear hypothesis: who it is for, why now, what we will say, and what Sales will do when someone engages. 
Build target audiences and lead-generation motions, write the initial outbound or campaign, and identify the content, offer, or proof needed to give Sales a reason to engage. 
Work with Marketing to develop or repurpose the content, landing pages, customer proof, and other materials needed to get a motion in-market. 
Personally launch the first version with Sales and iterate from real responses. 
An experiment should be ready to run, not a slide describing something we could try.
Give Sales a motion they can use
Turn what works into a practical play: who to pursue, why now, what to say, what content or proof to use, and what to do next. 
Put the play into practice with Sales and improve it based on real conversations. 
Learn and repeat
Decide what success looks like before a motion launches and make sure we can measure it. 
Analyze performance across audiences, messages, channels, conversations, opportunities, and pipeline to understand what is, and isn't, working. 
Build a consistent experimentation process that records hypotheses, results, learnings, and next actions, and share those learnings with the broader GTM team. 
Improve what shows promise, stop what does not, and turn the motions that work into plays that Sales can run again. 
What you bring to the team
5+ years of experience building and executing enterprise B2B growth, outbound, account-based, or GTM programs. 
A track record of taking a GTM idea through execution and measurement, including work you personally built and launched. 
Experience creating conversations and opportunities inside defined target accounts and complex buying groups. 
Experience developing outbound campaigns, messaging, and sales plays for an enterprise sales team. 
Ability to define a hypothesis, establish meaningful success criteria, interpret results, and decide what to try next. 
Comfort working with GTM and campaign data to identify opportunities, evaluate performance, and turn results into clear decisions. 
Working knowledge of HubSpot or another CRM and marketing automation platform. 
Hands-on experience with Apollo or similar sales intelligence, prospecting, enrichment, and lead-generation platforms, and the ability to use them to build targeted audiences and execute outbound motions. 
You can turn an idea into credible messaging without waiting for someone else to write it. 
Strong commercial judgment and curiosity, you naturally look for patterns, opportunities, and things the team hasn't tried yet. 
Experience in enterprise software, energy, industrial technology, environmental software, or another complex B2B market is an asset.
Above all, we're looking for a doer. You're senior enough to recognize an opportunity and decide what we should try, and hands-on enough to build the first version yourself. You don't need a large team, a perfect brief, or every answer before you start.
What we offer
Competitive compensation
Stock options (at Validere, we're all owners)
Generous time-off with parental/family leave
Quarterly Employee Wellbeing Days
Hybrid work environment: 1 day per week work-from-home
Professional development budget to master your craft
Comprehensive health and dental benefits
Great Place to Work Certified
An inclusive, ego-free environment where diversity of people and thought is valued
Opportunity to impact the trajectory of a fast-growing tech company
Our shared values
Deliver the highest value
Remove friction
More scalable, everyday
Be fair & transparent
Validere is an equal employment opportunity employer. We welcome and encourage applications from everyone regardless of race, colour, religion, gender, sexual orientation, age, or disability status. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the interview process and beyond. We are committed to providing an inclusive, open, and diverse work environment.

However, all candidates are thoroughly reviewed and advanced by our dedicated internal recruitment team, ensuring a personalized and attentive hiring process. It’s important to note that we do not employ additional AI tools in this process; our evaluation is entirely manual, focusing on the unique qualifications and experiences of each candidate.

title: Head of Revenue Operations
description:
Job Description
 Role: Head of RevOps
 Reports to: Chief Revenue Officer
 Office: London
 The Organisation
 Efekta provides the world's leading AI-powered learning technology. Our mission is to help everyone learn faster and go further by making personal tutoring affordable and accessible. AI Personalized Learning that works alongside human teachers in schools, universities, and global companies. With an AI-driven curriculum, personal AI tutor, and AI teaching assistant, we deliver proven results at scale.
Recently added to the TIME 100 Most Innovative Companies list, we have extremely ambitious growth plans and are looking for highly talented, motivated people to help fuel them. A career with us offers the scale of a global organization with the pace, purpose, and energy of a fastgrowing business. We look for thinkers and doers who are excited to help us shape the future of education.
 The Opportunity
 As Head of RevOps you'll own the commercial operating system for Efekta; how we forecast, how we measure pipeline health, how we run the deal desk, and how we make sure the data we rely on is trustworthy. You'll report to the CRO, have one direct report (Bid Manager), and work closely with regional sales leads across multiple markets.
This is a builder role. There is no mature playbook to inherit. If you've spent your career
optimising systems that already exist, this probably isn't the right fit. If you're energised by designing from scratch in a fast-moving environment, it might be exactly right.
 What You’ll Own
Forecasting; own the methodology, the cadences, and the accuracy. Make the pipeline honest.
Pipeline health; track stage-to-stage conversion, identify where deals stall, and turn that into insight the CRO and regional leads can act on.
CRM governance; own Salesforce as the system of record. Set the data standards, run the hygiene audits, make it trustworthy.
Deal desk; structure and review complex, non-standard deals efficiently. Own turnaround time.
Ramp & productivity; define what good looks like for each sales role, set ramp benchmarks, and track time-to-productivity for new hires.
Commercial rhythm; design and run the weekly, monthly, and quarterly cadences that keep the business aligned.
Bid Manager; lead and develop your one direct report, keeping bid quality high and the sales team focused on relationships. 
 How We’ll Measure Success
Forecast accuracy
Stage-to-stage conversion rates
CRM data hygiene %
Deal desk turnaround time
Ramp to productivity
 What We’re Looking For
5–10 years in Revenue or Sales Operations — ideally some of that in a startup or scale-up where you had to build, not just run.
You've owned forecasting methodology end-to-end, not just produced the report.
Comfortable in Salesforce — you can build what you need without waiting for a BI team.
Experience with complex deal structures is a plus — tenders, government procurement, long sales cycles.
Credible enough with senior salespeople that they actually adopt the standards you set.
Direct, clear communicator — you'll be in the room with the CRO regularly. 
 Who You Are
 You have strong opinions about how a sales organisation should operate. You're comfortable with ambiguity and don't need a perfect brief before you start. You spot when data doesn't add up and you say so. You build things that last.
 Why work at Efekta
A balance of autonomy and support to develop and follow your own strategy.
A start up fast paced environment with real potential to create transformative impact in schools and universities around the world if we succeed.
Surrounded by passionate, talented international teammates who are experts in education, technology and growth and who believe nothing is impossible.
A chance to spend time in other offices and with teams around the world.

title: Director, Revenue Operations (B2B SaaS)
description:
WHY STOREFORCE
StoreForce helps retailers connect decisions, execution, and performance across their stores. We work with complex, well-known retailers around the world, and we have meaningful room to grow both through new clients and within the clients that already trust us. This role will sit close to the work, have real access to leadership, and materially shape how our sales organization scales.
OVERVIEW
 Make the right sales behaviors repeatable, visible, and durable. 
StoreForce has strong sales leadership, meaningful opportunity inside our existing client base, and a growing set of plays for winning new business. What we need now is someone who can turn those ideas into consistent execution across the team.
Reporting to the Chief Revenue Officer (CRO), the Director of Revenue Operations will build the operating rhythm that makes good ideas stick. This person will bring rigor to account planning, pipeline management, forecasting, expansion, and follow-through. They will know what matters commercially, make it visible, and work with the team until it becomes how we operate every week.
This is not a traditional Salesforce administrator role nor a second sales leader. The CRO will set sales strategy, coach the team, and lead our most important pursuits. The Director of Revenue Operations will translate that direction into clear actions, useful inspection, and sustained execution so the CRO and sellers can spend more time coaching, selling, and closing.
This role is fully remote with moderate national and international travel required.
THE PERSON WE’RE LOOKING FOR
You are a commercially minded operator who enjoys helping a talented team become more consistent. You can move comfortably between the detail of a late account plan and the larger question of where growth is coming from. You are direct without being heavy-handed, analytical without hiding behind the data, and persistent without creating unnecessary process.
You make things happen. When a direction is agreed, you create the structure and follow-through needed to carry it all the way into the field.
You know what good enterprise SaaS selling looks like. You can distinguish a meaningful commercial signal from activity that merely looks busy.
You can hold experienced people accountable without relying on hierarchy. Your credibility comes from judgment, preparation, consistency, and a willingness to help.
You build with the team, not around it. You listen, ask plainspoken questions, and improve the system as you learn.
You are comfortable in a growing, evolving company where not every answer or process already exists.
You care about outcomes more than ownership lines and bring a low-ego, sleeves-rolled-up approach to cross-functional work.
RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Execution and Operating Cadence
Translate sales strategy and priorities into a manageable set of actions, owners, milestones, and measures.
Run the recurring cadence for pipeline, forecast, deal progression, and account-plan review in close partnership with the CRO.
Reinforce the agreed revenue KPIs through the weekly operating cadence, ensuring the team understands what is being measured, why it matters, and what actions are required when performance is off track. Follow through with persistence and good judgment. Help the team understand why the work matters and remove obstacles where you can. When commitments are missed repeatedly, name it plainly and hold the line. The job is durable execution, not activity that looks busy.
Spot when a play or process is not working, diagnose why, and improve it rather than adding bureaucracy.
2. Account Planning and Expansion
Set a practical standard for strong account plans and coach the team toward it.
Build repeatable land-and-expand plays across sister brands, regions, and StoreForce products.
Keep expansion opportunities moving from analysis to action, with clear ownership and measurable progress.
3. Pipeline, Forecasting, and Insight
Create a shared, fact-based view of pipeline health, deal risk, forecast, conversion, velocity, and win/loss patterns.
Own the revenue KPI framework, including the leading and lagging indicators used to measure pipeline creation, pipeline coverage, forecast accuracy, conversion, deal velocity, win/loss, expansion, productivity, and attainment. Ensure definitions are clear, reporting is trusted, and metrics are used to drive action rather than simply describe performance.
Ask the next useful question when the data exposes a gap. Turn reporting into decisions and actions, not another set of dashboards.
Partner with the CRO on coverage strategy, territory design, and capacity planning to ensure resources are aligned with market opportunity and growth objectives.
Partner with Finance on quota setting, incentive design and compensation modeling that reinforces desired commercial behaviors and supports the annual go-to-market objectives.
4. Process, Enablement, and Systems
Document the few processes and playbooks that genuinely help the team execute, then drive their adoption.
Reinforce new sales approaches through coaching, inspection, and feedback until they become durable field behavior.
Work with our existing Salesforce and analytics resources to define what the systems need to deliver. You should be fluent enough to ask for the right things, but you will not be expected to serve as the hands-on Salesforce administrator.
Partner closely with Sales, Marketing, Client Success, Finance, and Product where the sales motion crosses functional lines.
WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
 In the first 12 to 18 months, this leader will: 
Establish and drive adoption of AI-enabled workflows across account planning, opportunity management, prospect research, enhance deal inspection and forecasting, creating measurable productivity improvements for the sales team
Establish a simple, dependable weekly operating cadence for pipeline, deal progression, account plans, and commitments. Expectations are clear, follow-up is consistent, and agreed actions do not disappear between meetings.
Within the first 90 days, baseline the numbers that matter (forecast accuracy, deal-cycle time, win rate, and account-plan coverage), and set clear targets against them with the CRO, so that “better” has a definition both of you agree on.
Establish a clear revenue scorecard and KPI framework that leadership trusts and the sales team uses consistently to inspect performance, identify risk, and drive action.
Raise the quality of account planning across the team. Our most important clients and prospects have practical plans with clear objectives, relationships, next steps, owners, and dates.
Turn white-space analysis into an active expansion motion across brands, banners, geographies, and products. Opportunities are prioritized, assigned, progressed, and measured.
Improve confidence in the forecast by creating stronger pipeline discipline, clearer inspection, and more reliable inputs. Risks and gaps surface early enough for the team to act.
Operationalize our sales plays, including value and ROI communication, so they show up consistently from the first conversation through proof of value, QBRs, expansion, and renewal.
Build useful visibility into performance by segment and region, helping leadership decide where to focus and where different motions may be needed.
Clarify the right approach to smaller, faster-moving opportunities that sit below our traditional enterprise ICP, then help stand up the motion if the opportunity warrants it.
Create leverage for the CRO. Sales leadership spends less time chasing updates and policing process, and more time coaching the team, shaping strategy, and closing important business.
KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS (KPIs)
Salesforce CRM adoption and data quality/completeness rate across the sales team;
Sales process compliance: percentage of deals and activities following StoreForce-defined processes;
Timeliness and accuracy of sales forecasting;
On-time delivery of weekly, monthly, and quarterly sales performance reports to the CRO and stakeholders;
Number of identified process gaps converted into documented, implemented, and adopted processes;
Pipeline velocity, conversion rates, win/loss ratios, and average sales cycle length.
QUALIFICATIONS
Competencies Required:
Accountability – Holds themselves and others to a high standard; proactively identifies issues, follows through on commitments, and ensures nothing falls through the cracks.
Influence & Assertiveness – Comfortable driving accountability across peers and senior team members; knows how to push for results without direct authority and does so with professionalism and persistence.
Analytical Thinking – Digests complex data from multiple sources; identifies patterns, gaps, and opportunities; translates data into clear, actionable insights for decision-makers.
Communication – Strong oral and written communication skills; able to present complex data and recommendations clearly to both frontline team members and senior executives.
Leadership – Demonstrated ability to coach, train, and develop others; creates clarity, sets expectations, and builds a culture of operational excellence.
Process Orientation – Natural inclination to bring structure and repeatability to ambiguous or unstructured environments; thrives on building systems that scale.
Agility – Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, evolving environment; maintains focus and drives outcomes despite competing demands and shifting priorities.

title: Head of Revenue Operations & Strategy
description:

 At Birdie, we’re reimagining care for older adults. We’re building the technology that powers the future of home healthcare, empowering care teams with tools to deliver better, more dignified care, and enabling older people to thrive in their own homes for longer. Our all-in-one solution powers millions of care visits every month, equipping care providers with the tools they need to deliver exceptional, efficient care.
 We’re not here to tinker at the edges. We’re here to radically transform a broken system.
 That’s why we’ve built an all-in-one platform that supported over 60 million care visits and enabled care for 116,000 individuals in 2025, and we continue to grow our impact.  Your mission is to redesign how Birdie’s commercial teams work. You’ll use AI to give our sales, customer success and SDR teams more leverage, so more care providers choose Birdie, stay with us and grow with us. You’re technical enough to direct and challenge systems and data work, without needing to do it all yourself.

You care more about outcomes than process, and you like working at pace.
You want your work to improve how older people are cared for.

 🌈 What You’ll Get From Us
 We believe people do their best work when they’re supported, trusted and inspired. Here’s how we build a world-class employee experience:

A deeply human, radically transparent culture

 Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.

 About This Role

title: Sales Enablement Program Manager
description:
Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together.
So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff. Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place. Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale.
Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. We’re building a significant, meaningful, and lasting business, and we are helping sellers worldwide do the same.
 The Role 
We’re looking for a proactive and highly organized Sales Enablement Program Manager to help drive clarity, consistency, and continuous learning across Block’s global sales and Account Management teams. You’ll play a critical role in operationalizing our everboarding strategy—ongoing education beyond onboarding. This role requires a strong blend of content operations, learning science, stakeholder management, and sales context awareness.
 You Will 
Support ongoing learning initiatives by helping to plan, build, facilitate, and maintain scalable sales enablement content beyond onboarding.
Curate and maintain centralized knowledge resources, partnering with subject matter experts (SMEs) across Product, Marketing, and Sales to ensure accuracy and consistency.
Help operationalize the everboarding strategy, coordinating timelines, deliverables, and stakeholder communications.

Manage internal communications related to enablement, such as newsletters, training calendars, training decks, and update broadcasts to reduce noise and increase clarity.
Collect feedback and track program impact, using data to assess adoption, knowledge retention, and performance improvements.
Support regional Canada enablement needs, ensuring content is localized and relevant for diverse sales teams across markets.

 You Have 
4+ years of experience in Sales Enablement, Sales, or Account Management.
Strong understanding of adult learning theories and experience applying them to training design, content delivery, or knowledge-sharing systems.
Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with an ability to influence and collaborate across functions and levels.
Proven ability to prioritize effectively, manage competing demands, and maintain clarity under ambiguity.

Exposure to coaching methodologies such as GROW to support learner development and behavior change.
