title: Head of Business Operations
description:
Take over founder-led operations and build the systems that help us grow.
 You might be a consultant who moved into a startup, a founder’s associate already running important parts of a business, or an operator who has started building software and automations yourself.
You enjoy understanding how a business works, finding what slows it down, and making it work better. You can turn an unclear problem into a practical plan, bring people with you, and build the first solution.
We are looking for someone ready to take that ability further: own our operations function, lead a small team, and join the company’s leadership team.
 About Us
 Platform Engineering Masters is the company behind platformengineering.org and PlatformCon. We bring together engineers, technology leaders and vendors through our community, conferences, education and Weave Intelligence.
As the business grows, the systems behind it need to grow too: how we deliver for customers, run events, produce content, understand performance and share information across teams.
Our co-founder, Christoph currently leads operations. You will work closely with him during the handover, then take responsibility for running and developing the function independently. You will report to Luca, our Managing Director.
 The challenge
 We have a working business, an existing operations team and plenty already being built. We also have manual handovers, disconnected information and processes that depend too much on particular people.
Your job is to decide what needs attention, understand the business problem behind each request, and lead the work through to a solution people actually use.
Some of the questions you will tackle:
How do we turn a customer commitment into a reliable delivery process across sales, content and events?
How do we give teams trustworthy information about what is working and where to focus?
How do we make recurring work, such as publishing a webinar or delivering a sponsored asset, easy to run consistently?
Which problems need custom software, which need better use of existing tools, and which simply need a clearer process?
How do we keep improving our systems without making the business dependent on their original builders?
 What you will own
 The operations roadmap. Work directly with Sales, Growth, Content and Events to understand their needs. Prioritize by business impact, challenge requests where necessary, and make trade-offs explicit, including when requests come from founders.
 A small, growing team. You will manage our existing revenue operations and systems engineering specialists from the start, and help recruit and develop additional content/design and growth operations capacity.
 Hands-on delivery. Prototype, write code, connect systems and build automations yourself when that is the fastest way to make progress. Give your team clear direction and space to own delivery.
 Systems that last. Make sure critical workflows have clear ownership, useful documentation and sensible standards for reliability, access and maintenance.
 Adoption and results. Work with business teams until the solution is part of their everyday work. Judge success by better delivery, useful information and time saved.
Your remit is the operational systems supporting the business. Functional leaders own their commercial, editorial and event outcomes; you work with them to make those outcomes easier to achieve.
 What You Will Bring
Structured problem-solving and strong communication. You can understand an internal customer’s needs, question assumptions and explain a recommendation clearly. Consulting or similar client-facing experience would be useful. 
Evidence that you build. You have used code, APIs, automation or AI tools to solve real problems. You can walk us through what you built, why you chose that approach and what happened when people used it. 
Commercial judgment. You connect operational improvements to revenue, delivery quality, cost or capacity. 
Ownership in an ambiguous environment. You can make progress without a complete brief and follow through when implementation gets difficult. 
Readiness to lead. You can set priorities, give useful feedback and hold a small team accountable while staying close to the work. 
Curiosity about technology and the business. You learn unfamiliar tools and domains quickly and care about the quality of the result. 
Experience managing processes in a startup would be valuable. You do not need to have held a Head of Operations title or worked in every area this role touches. We care more about your judgment, learning speed and track record than a particular CRM certification or tool stack.
 What Success Looks Like
 In your first months, you will establish clear priorities with the team, take ownership of the most important systems and deliver improvements that business teams can see and use.
Over time, routine work will run with fewer manual interventions, teams will have better information, and the founders will be able to step out of day-to-day operations with confidence.
 Why join
 You will inherit a real team, work directly with leadership and have the mandate to shape an important part of a growing business. This is an opportunity to move from solving individual problems to owning the function that solves them.
 Interested?
 Send us your CV or profile and a short example of something you improved or built. Tell us what the problem was, what you personally did and what changed. If you have any questions, please contact james@platformengineering.org

title: Sales Operations Manager, Channel
description:
Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely.
We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.
 Summary:
 We are currently seeking a Channel Sales Operations Manager to join our Revenue Operations team. This role is available to applicants based in either the United States or Canada.
 What your team does:
 Revenue Operations has one job: to drive growth by accelerating our revenue-generating and revenue-retaining teams. We directly support Sales, Marketing, Channel, Customer Enablement, Customer Support and Payments by providing insights, reducing friction, and enabling teams to be innovative and self-sufficient.
 Who you are:
 Clio’s partner ecosystem is becoming a primary growth lever — the way we break into hard markets, extend into new geographies, and absorb the businesses we acquire. Today, it runs on processes that were never designed for its current scale.
We are hiring a Channel Sales Operations Manager to own the operating model behind it. This is a net-new role, and it is deliberately senior: we want someone who arrives as the subject matter expert and owner of channel operations at Clio, not someone who needs the function defined for them first. You will own Clio’s global partner channel operationally — reseller and referral segments, all law firm segments, every region we operate in. Your first mandate is concrete: map what actually happens today, name the gaps costing our partner account managers time and revenue, and lead the business implementation of our new partner platform. From there, you own the operating model those processes run on.
You will be working on the Sales Operations team in the Revenue Operations department, reporting to the Manager, Technical Sales Operations, with deep cross-functional partnerships across Channel, Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Finance, and Legal. The role is also genuinely ambiguous — our operations org is scaling fast, and work will often arrive undefined, contested between teams, or both. The people who thrive here have a strong "figure it out" instinct: they sit in the messiness long enough to find the right frame instead of the fast answer, and they are comfortable naming a problem nobody has named yet.
 What you'll be doing:
 Lead the partner platform implementation
Own the business implementation of a new Partner Relationship platform, Clio’s new AI-driven partner platform — requirements, configuration, data model, partner journeys, migration, and adoption.
Own the platform roadmap after launch, including where Salesforce remains the system of record
Drive down partner-side friction as a measured outcome — including partner portal lead conversion, which takes roughly 15 minutes today
 Own the channel operating model
Map and document Clio’s channel processes end to end, including the scenarios undocumented today: l, referral and reseller partner motions
Identify and close the operational gaps slowing down partner account managers, and build the mechanisms that keep those gaps from re-forming
Own partner-attributed pipeline architecture in Salesforce, ensuring accurate sourced vs. influenced vs. co-sell categorization
Own the channel measurement architecture — partner-sourced MRR, activation rates, deal registration volume, co-sell conversion, and contribution by tier — defining what good looks like, not just reporting the number
Own partner program tier mechanics, channel routing and territory logic, rules of engagement, and the enablement material that supports them
Serve as escalation and decision point for partner attribution and credit disputes
 Bring channel operations into strategy, not just execution
Serve as the accountable channel operations voice in annual planning, QBRs, and GTM launches
Bring operational feasibility into partner program and incentive design before the program is committed, rather than after
Support partner pipeline inspection and forecast roll-ups with Channel Sales leadership, and own the partner performance narrative leadership plans against
 How Success Is Measured
 Performance is measured through OKRs, with an initial focus on adoption and successful implementation of the new partner platform, partner-sourced conversion rates, and the stickiness and retention of partner-sourced accounts.
 What you bring:
4+ years of relevant experience, with a substantial portion in channel or partner operations specifically — this is not a general sales operations role, and general sales ops experience alone will not translate
Hands-on Salesforce experience, including channel-relevant objects and relationships (Partner, Opportunity splits, lead source attribution) and reporting
Demonstrated ownership of channel program mechanics: deal registration, partner tiering, co-sell motions, referral fee structures, and margin / discount governance
Experience standing up or materially re-platforming a PRM tool or partner portal — an implementation, not administration of one someone else built
Proven ability to operate in ambiguity: taking an undefined, cross-functional problem and producing a defensible operating model without waiting for it to be scoped
Influence without authority across functions with competing incentives — including getting other teams to reprioritize by framing business cost, and stating a tradeoff and choosing what not to do, publicly
Fluent use of AI tooling to streamline workflows, generate insights, and scale operational processes — raising both their own ceiling and their stakeholders’
 Strongly Preferred
Experience operating a partner channel across multiple regions, or during a market entry or M&A integration
High proficiency in Google Sheets or Excel for channel performance modeling, and with BI tools for partner contribution and attribution reporting
Experience with the broader sales and channel tech stack: SalesLoft, ChiliPiper, Gong, ZoomInfo
Salesforce Admin certification
 What you will find here:
 Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture.
 Some highlights of our Total Rewards program include: 
Competitive, equitable salary with top-tier health benefits, dental, and vision insurance 
Hybrid work environment, with expectation for local Clions (Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Dublin and Sydney) to be in office minimum twice per week. 
Flexible time off policy, with an encouraged 20 days off per year.
EAP benefits for you and household members, including counseling and online resources
401k matching and Child Education Savings
Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgement at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years
The expected salary range for this role is $130,600 to $195,800 USD. Initial placement within the range is informed by geographic region, experience, and skillset, with room to progress as impact and tenure grow. Final offer amounts will vary based on candidate profile.

 Our team shows up as their authentic selves, and are united by our mission. We are dedicated to diversity, equity and inclusion. We pride ourselves in building and fostering an environment where our teams feel included, valued, and enabled to do the best work of their careers, wherever they choose to log in from. title: Head of Revenue Operations
description:
About H 
H Company is a European frontier AI lab building computer-use agents: Holo models, HoloTab, HoloDesktop and the CU Agent API. We're turning frontier research into powerful enterprise tools, and building the operating system behind that growth.
 The role 
You'll build and run the revenue engine for sales, partnerships, forward deployed and marketing. You'll own how we forecast, how pipeline moves, how deals get priced, and what data we use to decide. You’ll report to the COO and work closely with GTM leads and partners across the business. This is a builder role: much of it doesn't exist yet.
 What you'll own 
 Revenue architecture: Design the end-to-end GTM process, from lead through to renewal, across self-serve (API) and enterprise motions.

You'll also help shape a function that's still being built: a RevOps team that already works AI-natively, with the tooling and the mandate to use it, not just permission to ask. It's a category-leading vertical-SaaS environment with real technical depth in the systems you'd be running.
You will be responsible for:
 Salesforce Administration 
Declarative configuration: flows, validation rules, page layouts, permission sets, profiles, reports, and dashboards. 
User and license management, security review, and the field-level hygiene that keeps Salesforce trustworthy as the system of record. 
Triage and close out the standing data-quality and config backlog (duplicate records, broken flows, permission gaps, stale automation), work currently split between the Director and an external agency. 
Partner with the Director on architectural decisions such as object-model changes and taxonomy rebuilds, and own the build, not just the ticket queue.
 Marketing & GTM Tooling 
Administer the martech stack RevOps is responsible for: HubSpot (workflows, lead scoring, campaign operations), Chili Piper (lead routing), Propensity (ABM), Fathom, RocketLane, CLM/quoting tools, and the sales-engagement and cadence tooling inside Salesforce. 
Keep every tool's integration back to Salesforce clean. Salesforce is the hub, so nothing you administer should create a parallel data store.
Support tool evaluation and pilots: set up trials, define what “pass” looks like, and carry a pilot into permanent operation once it earns its place in the stack. 
 Data & Reporting Infrastructure 
Own the connective tissue between Salesforce, the marketing stack, and the reporting layer: keeping syncs, exports, and integrations running, and diagnosing them fast with the analytics engineer when they break. 
Build, maintain, and simplify the Salesforce reports, dashboards, and light data pipelines RevOps and its stakeholders depend on day to day, and support the shift to our “source of truth” cloud data-lake reporting system as we build it out in 2027. 
Work alongside the data/analytics function on schema and warehouse questions without owning deep analytics engineering. This is the operational admin seat, not the data-architect seat. 
 AI-Native Systems Work 
Use Claude and Claude Code as a standard part of how you build and maintain configuration: SFDX metadata changes, bulk data fixes, scripted QA, and automation that a point-and-click admin workflow would make too slow or too manual to attempt. 
Bring judgment about what to automate and what not to. AI makes bad changes cheap to ship, so config changes still get scoped, tested, and reviewed like engineering work, not shipped straight to production. 
What we want from you:
2 to 4 years of hands-on Salesforce administration (Sales Cloud). Salesforce Administrator certification preferred, not required.
Hands-on, shippable experience with at least one AI coding/automation tool (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, or similar) as a real part of your workflow today. This is a must-have, not a nice-to-have, and you can point to something you've actually shipped with one.
Experience administering at least one marketing automation or sales-engagement platform (HubSpot, Marketo, Salesloft, Pardot, or similar).
Comfortable writing basic SQL for data checks and light scripting for automation.
You've administered Salesforce for real users in production, not a sandbox project, and you know the line between what's safe to build declaratively and what needs escalation.
You default to fixing the data and the configuration, not building a report on top of the problem.
You're comfortable inheriting and prioritizing your own backlog; this role starts with significant standing technical debt, not a clean system.
You ask "does this write back to Salesforce cleanly?" before you ask "does this tool look nice?"
Bonus: exposure to a CPQ/quoting tool, a contract lifecycle management (CLM) tool, or a data warehouse/BI layer.
What you will get from us:

A group RRSP employer contribution up to 5%;
A group insurance for you and your family as well as an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and telemedicine;
A $750 wellness allowance per year;

In-office snacks, including fresh fruit baskets, coffee, beverages, and free drinks.

title: Sales Operations Analyst
description:
Job title: Sales Operations Associate 
 Location: Remote (U.S.) — Utah preferred 
 Type: Full-time 
 Compensation: $ 85,000–$100,000 base salary (DOE) plus a target annual bonus of 15%. Total target compensation ranges from approximately $98,000–$115,000+, based on experience and performance. 
 About Avari 
 Avari is a fast-growing short-term rental property management company, operating in partnership with Casago across Florida's Gulf Coast, Alabama, Utah, Nevada, Oregon, and the Lake Tahoe region of California. As we continue to expand through strategic acquisitions and new market growth, we help homeowners maximize the value of their vacation rental investments through exceptional management and proven returns. This role plays a key part in strengthening our market expansion, sales outreach, and revenue operations as we scale nationwide.
 About the role 
As a Sales Operations Associate with Avari Management, this role sits at the intersection of data and the field. You'll mine market-level data to surface homeowner-acquisition opportunities in our priority markets, translate those insights into clear messaging and collateral for our reps, and provide the sales operations backbone — quota tracking, payouts, and forecasting support — that keeps the team running.
In short: you turn "here's what the data says" into "here's exactly what our reps should say and send," and you keep the numbers behind the sales team honest and current. You're happiest with a lot of surface area, moving fast, and a mix of analysis, communication, and operations in a single week.v
 What you'll do 
 Market intelligence & analysis 
Mine internal and third-party data (CRM, data warehouse, STR market data, property/ownership records) to identify high-opportunity markets, owner segments, and competitive dynamics.
Build repeatable market profiles covering owner density, competitor presence, pricing, seasonality, and regulatory considerations.
Partner with RevOps on enrichment workflows so the data feeding the field stays accurate and current.
 Messaging & collateral 
Translate market insights into clear value propositions tailored by market and owner segment.
Create rep-ready collateral: one-pagers, outreach/email templates, call scripts, market briefs, and objection-handling guides.
Keep the content library organized so reps can find and use what they need.
 Sales enablement & adoption 
Equip BD/sales reps with the market playbooks, messaging, and collateral they need to win owners in each region.
Onboard and train reps on positioning, tooling, and plays, and drive real adoption — not just published assets.
Run feedback loops with reps to learn what's landing in-market and refine accordingly.
 Sales operations support 
Track quota attainment across the sales team and calculate commission/payouts accurately and on time.
Support forecasting and pipeline reporting, including operating the team's pipeline-weighting and projected-revenue reporting.
Maintain CRM hygiene and build reporting that connects rep activity and enablement to pipeline and owner signings.
 What you'll bring 
 Required 
3–4 years in sales/revenue operations, sales enablement, analytics, growth, or another data-forward GTM role.
 Strong with data — you pull, analyze, and interpret it without hand-holding. Fluent in spreadsheets and CRM, and quick to pick up SQL or BI tools.
 Tech-native — you learn new tools fast and instinctively look for ways to automate and streamline.
 Communicate insights well — you turn a dataset into a clear, persuasive narrative and into material a rep can actually use.
 High energy and pace — you thrive with lots of moving parts, ambiguity, and a fast tempo, and you take ownership without waiting to be told.
Comfort with numbers behind a sales team: quota, commissions/payouts, and forecasting mechanics (or a clear aptitude to ramp quickly).
 Preferred 
Experience in proptech, real estate, hospitality, marketplaces, franchise/multi-location, or other geographically segmented go-to-market models.
HubSpot and/or data-warehouse (e.g., Snowflake) experience.
Familiarity with prospecting/enrichment tooling (e.g., Clay) and STR or local-market data sources.
Exposure to owner-, SMB-, or B2B2C-acquisition motions.
 What success looks like 
 First 90 days: market profiles for the top [3–5] priority markets, a first rep-facing playbook in market, and clean, reliable quota/attainment reporting the team trusts.
 First 6–12 months: measurable rep adoption of collateral, demonstrable conversion lift in enabled markets, and a repeatable "market → messaging → enablement" motion — with sales ops reporting running like clockwork.
 Compensation & benefits 
Base salary range: $85,000 – $100,000, depending on experience.
Performance bonus: 15% target annual bonus (bringing target total compensation to approximately $98,000–$115,000+, depending on base salary and performance).
Health, dental, vision, 401(k) match, unlimited PTO & remote-first culture.
Professional development and career growth opportunities

title: Strategy & Business Operations Manager, Wolt Drive
description:
About Wolt
 At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we’re building the delivery of (almost) everything and you’ll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.
Working at Wolt isn’t always easy, but it’s definitely exciting. Here you’ll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You’ll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you’re a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.
 About The Role
 Wolt is on a growth journey as part of the DoorDash family, together with Deliveroo. Drive is our delivery-as-a-service business: we let merchants offer fast, reliable delivery in their own channels (their webshop, app or ordering system), powered by the Wolt and Deliveroo courier networks. We're now bringing Drive across Wolt and Deliveroo countries together into one EMEA business , with one team and a clear ambition: grow fast and build a business that stands on its own feet.
A growing share of that scaling comes from outside restaurants: grocers, retailers, pharmacies and other eComm players who want on-demand and same-day delivery for their own customers. Their needs can be very different from restaurants: bigger baskets, scheduled and batched deliveries, larger and heavier items, longer distances and more complex integrations. This brings us to you, our next Manager, Strategy & Operations for Grocery & Retail Drive.
You'll own this segment across EMEA, from strategy and planning to pricing, product requirements and performance. You'll work hand in hand with our regional commercial teams, who own the partner relationships, and with Product, Logistics, Finance and our Marketplace grocery & retail teams. You'll join the Drive EMEA Strategy & Operations team and report to the Director of Strategy & Operations, Drive EMEA.
 What You'll Be Doing
Own the Grocery & Retail strategy and annual plan for Drive EMEA: where we play, which partners we go after, and the growth and profitability we commit to.
Set the commercial framework for the segment, including pricing guidelines, deal economics and investment cases for our largest partnerships, together with the regional commercial leads.
Act as the voice of grocery and retail partners towards Product and Logistics, turning commercial needs such as scheduled delivery or large and heavy items into sized, prioritized requirements.
Run performance management for the segment: track growth, unit economics and service levels for our biggest partners, spot what's off and drive the fix with the teams involved.
Shape how Drive works with our Marketplace grocery & retail teams, so partners get one joined-up offer from us.
Turn wins into playbooks that country teams can reuse, from the first pitch to launch and scale-up.
 Our humble expectations
5+ years of experience in strategy & operations, business development, commercial roles or management consulting, with a track record of owning outcomes, not just recommendations.
Strong commercial and analytical skills: you can build a deal P&L or a segment plan from scratch, and defend it in front of a partner's leadership or our own.
Proven ability to get things done across a matrix organization without direct authority, working with regional teams, Product, Logistics and Finance.
You use AI tools (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) in your daily work, for example in analysis, planning and ways of working, and look for new ways to apply them to elevate you - whilst maintaining strong judgement that comes from personal understanding complex systems
Structured thinking and clear, concise communication in English, both written and spoken.
Willingness to travel occasionally across our EMEA markets.
 Seen as a strong advantage:
Background in retail, grocery, e-commerce, logistics or on-demand delivery, either in-house or advising companies in these sectors.
Experience with B2B platform or delivery-as-a-service businesses.
 Why you'll love it
🚀 Global and growing fast: Be part of a fast-moving business at the moment it's being built, across two of Europe's best-known delivery brands
🛒 A segment to own: Work with some of the biggest grocery and retail brands in Europe, and see what you write end up on the product roadmap
🤩 Ride of a lifetime: Accelerate your career with direct access to DoorDash's global Drive experience and room to grow as the segment scales
💪 Instant impact: Take ownership and make a difference
💙 Big hearts and small egos: Surround yourself with smart, friendly people
 Next steps
 If you are excited about working in a high-growth environment, taking ownership, and being part of an extremely ambitious team, then click below to apply, make sure to add your CV in English and get the conversation going! We will be reviewing applications on a rolling basis.
Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion
We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.
 Beware of recruitment scams: DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about our legitimate recruiting process at Recruitment Scam Awareness - DoorDash .

title: Sales Operations Lead
description:
At FintechOS, we are looking for a Sales Operations Lead who wants to build, influence, and leave a visible mark. You will shape the processes, data, technology, and commercial rhythms behind our global enterprise sales organisation, creating an environment where the commercial team can focus, execute consistently, and thrive.
This is not a CRM administration role. You will have the mandate to challenge what is not working, simplify how we operate, and turn HubSpot into a genuine performance enabler. Your impact will be visible in seller productivity, pipeline quality, forecast confidence, and our ability to scale.
Why this role is worth your next move
• Build, do not simply maintain: shape the sales operating model and HubSpot environment for our next stage of growth.
• Influence at the right level: partner with senior commercial leaders on forecasting, planning, performance, and go-to-market decisions.
• Own outcomes end to end: identify the problem, design the solution, lead adoption, and measure the commercial impact.
• Solve meaningful complexity: enable enterprise sales into banks, insurers, and other highly regulated organisations.
The impact you will make
 Build the sales operating system: Create scalable processes and cadences that help sellers prioritise the right accounts, progress complex opportunities, and execute consistently.
 Make HubSpot work for sellers: Own CRM architecture, pipeline design, workflows, automation, integrations, reporting, data governance, and adoption.
 Increase seller productivity: Remove unnecessary administration, automate repetitive work, and return more time to customer-facing activity.
 Own the revenue execution cadence: Run pipeline inspection, deal reviews, forecast cadence, and the shared sales scoreboard, turning each into clear decisions, actions, and accountability.
 Turn data into decisions: Give sellers, managers, and leaders clear insight into priorities, risks, performance, and growth opportunities.
 Enable complex deals: Improve pricing, approvals, contracting, and cross-functional coordination across long enterprise sales cycles.
 Shape commercial planning: Partner with Sales Leadership and Finance on territories, quotas, capacity, coverage, and performance management.
 Lead meaningful change: Take operational improvements from idea through implementation, enablement, adoption, and measurable impact.
What you will bring
8+ years in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, or Commercial Operations, ideally within enterprise B2B SaaS.
Advanced HubSpot experience across CRM architecture, pipeline design, automation, reporting, integrations, data governance, and user adoption.
Experience supporting long, high-value sales cycles involving multiple decision-makers, procurement, legal, security, and executive stakeholders.
Hands-on ownership of forecasting, pipeline governance, territory planning, quota setting, or capacity planning.
Strong knowledge of ARR, ACV, bookings, pipeline coverage, win rate, sales velocity, and quota attainment.
Strong analytical and modelling skills using Excel or Google Sheets, plus Power BI, Tableau, Looker, or similar tools.
A track record of simplifying sales processes and improving seller productivity without sacrificing commercial discipline.
Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, and change leadership skills, with the confidence to challenge constructively.
Great to have
Experience in fintech, banking technology, insurance technology, payments, or another regulated industry.
Familiarity with MEDDPICC, MEDDIC, Challenger, or another enterprise sales methodology.
Experience with Gong, Outreach, ZoomInfo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Clari, or similar platforms.
Experience improving deal-desk, pricing, compensation, or partner-led sales processes.
You will know you are making an impact when
Sellers know where to focus and how to move opportunities forward.
HubSpot is valued as a selling tool, not treated as an administrative obligation.
Pipeline and forecast conversations are consistent, focused, and actionable.
Managers have the insight they need to coach effectively.
Commercial approvals and internal handoffs are faster and more predictable.
The sales operating model scales confidently with the business.
Who we are
FintechOS is a global fintech enablement company on a mission to make financial innovation accessible to every business. Our platform helps banks, insurers, and other financial institutions launch and scale financial products faster, bringing new solutions to market in as little as 12 weeks.
You will join an international team solving complex commercial and technology challenges in one of the world’s largest and most highly regulated industries. We value ownership, curiosity, collaboration, inclusion, and constructive challenge.

Power BI, Tableau, Looker or similar BI tools

title: Principal Customer Success Manager
description:
Your role at Dynatrace 
As a Principal Customer Success Manager, you will be responsible for preserving and growing subscription renewals for our largest and most complicated enterprise customers. You will accomplish this by driving adoption and consumption within your book of business and will educate your customers on Dynatrace’s platform and service offerings. You will demonstrate value and focus on growing relationships by acting as their champion within Dynatrace.
As a trusted advisor both within your customer teams and IAT, the Principal CSM is responsible for and looked upon to ensure that customers are achieving their business outcomes and realizing value from their investment. You will highlight wins and be able to tie the customers pain points, compliance needs and desired outcomes successfully to our platform capabilities and services offerings. You will also plan and develop short- and long-term strategies via success planning and provide thought leadership and mentoring to others. Additionally, the Principal Customer Success Manager partners with both Marketing and Sales to publish customer case studies, add to our referenceable customer list and drives the closing of new business with Sales in the field. Our goal is to provide our customers with software intelligence that will accelerate their digital transformation. As a Lead Senior Customer Success Manager, you will be at the heart of that journey.
Role & Responsibilities
Accelerate customers adoption and consumption of the Dynatrace platform and service portfolio through relationship management, success planning, and documenting value events/realization
Own renewal strategy and subsequent on time renewal of subscription(s) as well as the identification of customer goals, KPIs and their associated milestones for comprehensive success planning
Build Dynatrace brand awareness and loyalty and expand into other business units within your customer base
Conduct regular proactive calls and account review meetings; maintain an accurate record of discussions, success plans, and action items in our CRM
Work with management team to ensure that critical issues are documented and escalated in an expeditious manner for resolution
Defend against the competition and be able to compare/contrast our platform with the competition
Collaborate on account activities with the Integrated Account Team (IAT) spanning sales and post-sales teams and if appropriate, engagement, process analysis and operational improvement efforts
Identify strategic, new business growth opportunities and/or white space
Leverage relationships to aid in the building of reference accounts/contacts
Act as customer advocate and liaison to become a trusted advisor by providing business and account oversight to ensure exceptional customer experience
Possess industry or vertical experience to leverage across your book of business and properly articulate and apply Dynatrace platform value across multiple industries or verticals
Engage directly with various customers and/or partner stakeholders, from technical professionals to senior executives, driving consumption, adoption and real business transformation with your Customer Success Engineers and IAT
Leverages data and analysis to inform the customer and/or IAT on important account decisions, while tracking and driving deployment, adoption, growth and measure of Dynatrace value across business units and/or geographies
Travel as required to support your book of business
 What will help you succeed 
 Qualifications 
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience
15+ years relevant experience in customer success, account management, or similar field managing large and complex customers possessing an expert level understanding and implementation of customer success best practices
A strong business acumen and commercial outlook with a great conceptual understanding of IT operations processes and best practices
Be able to quickly develop strong relationships with users/commercial partners/internal communities as well as customer executives to drive, deliver and document successful business outcomes delivered from the Dynatrace platform
Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills and comfortable with fast-paced, dynamic environments associated with high-growth companies
Experience in the Observability marketplace with an understanding of where Dynatrace is positioned and our key strengths as they pertain to our competition
Highly motivated, energetic and committed to getting results
Proven expertise working with the executive level in client environments, as well as with procurement and business owners
Prior experience partnering with Product/R&D organizations and successfully championing customer platform requirements
Technical understanding of cloud concepts and application performance monitoring technologies, and specific experience and use cases for AWS, GCP and Azure cloud platforms
Demonstrable past experience partnering with senior customer/partner stakeholders to develop strategies resulting in significant outcomes and impact to the respective parties
Understanding of Internet, web and mobile applications; knowledge of HTTP, HTML, JavaScript etc.
 Why you will love being a Dynatracer 
Dynatrace is a leader in unified observability and security.
We provide a culture of excellence with competitive compensation packages designed to recognize and reward performance.
Our employees work with the largest cloud providers, including AWS, Microsoft, and Google Cloud, and other leading partners worldwide to create strategic alliances.
You'll get to work at the forefront of innovation with Dynatrace Intelligence—the industry's first agentic operations system. Bringing together deterministic and agentic AI, it helps teams understand what's happening, why it matters, and what to do next— automatically.
Over 50% of the Fortune 100 companies are current customers of Dynatrace.
 Compensation and Rewards 
The targeted base pay range for this role is $150K to $180K. When determining your salary, we consider your skills, experience, education, work location and internal equity.
 Equal Employment Opportunity 
All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.
We offer competitive compensation, company-sponsored premium benefits, medical, dental, vacation/holidays, company matching 401(k) Plan, etc. Dynatrace is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, color, gender identity, religion, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, physical abilities, age, sexual orientation, creed, disability status, veteran status, pregnancy, genetic status, or any other characteristic protected by law. If your disability makes it difficult for you to use this site, please contact careers@dynatrace.com . Dynatrace participates in E-Verify, participant information in English and Spanish. Right to work information in English and Spanish. EEO is the Law . To be considered for this position, please upload your resume/CV.
Benefits and work-life perks
We offer best-in-class core rewards, including paid time off, financial security benefits, retirement savings plans, and health insurance. Beyond that, you’ll get other benefits and work-life perks designed to make your ride with us even more rewarding.
Mental health support

About Dynatrace

title: Senior Revenue Operations Manager
description:
Location: Dublin ideally or London
 Working style: Hybrid 2 days on site
 Reports to: Chief Revenue Officer, with a close working line into Finance
 About Kota
 Kota is reimagining insurance and retirement benefits for the modern workforce. Through our two flagship products - Kota Platform, the first fully integrated benefits platform, and Kota Embed, our embedded insurance solution - we're making benefits more accessible, valued, and global.
Today we power benefits for tens of thousands of employees at Europe's most forward-thinking companies, including Carwow, Tines, Zoe, and Remote. Founded in 2022, we've raised more than €20M from EQT Ventures, Eurazeo, Northzone, and Frontline, along with founders and executives from Workday, Remote, Personio, OpenAI, and more. We're now ~100 people and scaling fast.
 The Role
 We're hiring our first Senior Revenue Operations Manager to build the operating system behind Kota's revenue - the data model, the plan, the forecast and the rhythm that runs the business.
Kota sells two ways. Embed puts our insurance inside the world's largest EOR, payroll and HR platforms. Platform sells direct SaaS to People teams. Each has its own motion, partners, contracts and economics, across multiple products and countries. Our revenue is multi-product, ramps on go-live and renews on insurer cycles - a far richer model than a standard SaaS funnel.
The business has outgrown the systems that got us here. Today we need one view of the pipeline, contracted ARR and live revenue across both business lines, and a planning process that ties targets, headcount and investment back to it. This is a builder role: part strategy, part operator, part systems architect. You'll sit in the CRO's team, partner closely with Finance, and be the person the exec team and board rely on for the numbers.
This is not a CRM admin role. You'll decide what we build, own the answer and then make it run.
 What You'll Do
 First 90 days
Build one revenue truth. Design the data model for a multi-product brokerage: parent accounts with product-line opportunities, each carrying its own value, go-live date, renewal date and commission.
Stand up the forecast. One forecast across Embed and Platform, with three distinct views: pipeline, contracted ARR, and live, ramping revenue driven by go-live dates.
Pressure-test the 2027 plan. It’ll be signed off before you start. Rebuild the model underneath it, bottoms-up by business line, partner, product and market, so we know which assumptions it rests on and where it breaks. Own the re-forecast from there.
Fix the funnel definitions. Stages that match how we actually sell - technical evaluation, quoting, contracting, go-live - with clean source attribution from first touch to signed and live.
 Ongoing
Planning and targets. Own the annual and quarterly planning cycle from 2028: targets, quotas, territories, capacity and headcount models across Sales, Account Management and Partnerships. Land the plan before headcount planning, so the plan drives the hiring, not the reverse.
Compensation. Design and administer commission and incentive plans, including MBO structures for roles that build as well as close. Run payouts with Finance.
Operating rhythm. Run the weekly forecast call, monthly business reviews and the board and investor revenue pack.
Partner and renewal economics. Model partner rate cards, revenue share, attach and renewals. Track unit economics (CAC, payback, NRR) by channel.
Systems and tooling. Own the GTM stack (HubSpot today) and the BI layer above it. Decide what we build, buy or replace as we scale.
Strategy. Run deep-dives the exec team needs: market prioritisation, pricing, new segments and channels. Turn analysis into decisions.
Build the team. Hire and lead a small Rev Ops and analytics team as the business grows.
 What We're Looking For
8+ years across Rev Ops, sales strategy & operations, or GTM strategy, with at least 3 leading the function in a high-growth B2B or fintech business.
A strategist who builds. You've designed a revenue operating model from the ground up - data model, forecast, planning, comp - not inherited one.
Strong commercial finance. You can build a three-statement-aware revenue model, a partner rate card or a comp plan from a blank sheet. A background in corporate finance, consulting or investing is a plus.
Planning at scale. You've run annual planning end to end: targets, territories, quotas, capacity and headcount, signed off at exec and board level.
Systems fluency. Deep in HubSpot or Salesforce, comfortable with a BI layer (Looker or similar) and SQL, and clear on when to build, buy or replace.
Complexity is your comfort zone. Multi-product, multi-country, partner-led or usage-based revenue. Insurance, payments or embedded finance experience is a strong plus.
Credibility in the room. You turn data into a recommendation, and you're trusted by the CRO, CFO and board to hold the number.
Owner's mindset. You'll start as a team of one and do the work yourself before you build a team around it.
 Our Values
Have Integrity. We care deeply about our why and it won't jeopardise our how.
Care Deeply. Our products are our story; we look at the details and go the extra mile to delight customers.
Own Your Ship. Ask why, do the work, get the data, solve the problem, be an owner.
Raise the Bar. We continuously push past good enough. Expect more, move faster, and never stop raising your and the team's standards.
Play to Win. We exist because we decided to say no to the norm - now we do this every day.
 Kota Benefits
Health insurance via Kota
Workplace pension with matched contributions up to 5% via Kota
WFH stipend to support your home office
25 days of paid time off
Annual company-wide offsite plus a dedicated team offsite
Attractive stock options

 Show less
 Seniority level
 Mid-Senior level
 Employment type
 Full-time
 Industries
 Financial Services

Design and administer commission and incentive plans

title: Senior Manager, Sales Strategy & Operations — International & Channel
description:
Who are we?
 Smarsh empowers its customers to manage risk and unleash intelligence in their digital communications. Our growing community of over 6500 organizations in regulated industries counts on Smarsh every day to help them spot compliance, legal or reputational risks in 80+ communication channels before those risks become regulatory fines or headlines. Relentless innovation has fueled our journey to consistent leadership recognition from analysts like Gartner and Forrester, and our sustained, aggressive growth has landed Smarsh in the annual Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing American companies since 2008.
Smarsh is looking for a Senior Manager of Sales Strategy & Operations to own Sales Ops for our International and Channel segments — two of our most complex, nascent, and highest-growth-opportunity segments. You'll own the full Sales Ops stack end to end, and you'll do it with a team: two direct reports from day one, with room to grow as these segments scale.
This role requires real autonomy. You'll partner with the VP of Channel Sales (US-based) and the VP of International Sales (UK-based), which means operating comfortably across time zones and building trust with a US-based leadership culture while representing the realities of international and partner-led selling. The ideal candidate is as comfortable setting multi-quarter strategy as they are rolling up their sleeves to build, fix and analyze.
 How will you contribute?
 Sales strategy & planning
Own annual and in-year planning for International and Channel: territory and partner coverage design, account/partner segmentation, quota setting, and capacity planning.
Translate segment strategy into operating plans and priorities in close partnership with the VP of Channel Sales and VP of International Sales.
Navigate the added complexity of these segments — multi-region/currency dynamics for International, and co-sell, deal registration, and partner incentive structures for Channel.
 Forecasting, pipeline & revenue cadence
Run forecasting and pipeline management for both segments, including the added layer of partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline.
Build and maintain the operating rhythm — pipeline reviews, forecast reviews, QBRs — adapted to work across US and London time zones.
Partner with Deal Desk, Finance, and Commissions on deal structuring, channel incentive design, and quota attainment for your segments.
 Reporting, analytics & business reviews
Build the reporting and dashboards that give both VPs a trusted, real-time view of pipeline, forecast, and partner/channel performance.
Use cohort, funnel, and partner-productivity analysis to explain what's driving — or blocking — growth in these nascent segments, and recommend what to do about it.
Own the analytics behind monthly and quarterly business reviews for International and Channel.
 Cross-functional & systems partnership
Partner with Enterprise Applications to translate International and Channel Ops needs (e.g., partner portals, multi-currency reporting, deal registration workflows) into systems requirements and roadmap priorities.
Build strong working relationships with Finance, Legal, and Marketing on the cross-border and partner-specific considerations these segments carry.
Represent International and Channel needs in global Sales Ops forums, influencing shared processes and tooling without owning them outright.
 AI & process innovation
Bring an AI-first mindset to two segments that are still establishing their operating model — this is a chance to build the right processes from the start rather than retrofit them.
Identify where AI and automation can improve forecast accuracy, partner/deal hygiene, and seller and partner productivity.
 Team leadership
Hire, coach, and develop a team (and grow it over time) across International and Channel Ops.
Set clear priorities, operating standards, and growth paths for your team.
 What will you bring?
 Required Qualifications
7+ years of experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, or a closely related GTM function, ideally in B2B SaaS, including 3+ years as a people manager.
Experience supporting international and/or channel/partner sales motions, including the added complexity of multi-region or partner-led selling.
Deep, hands-on experience with Salesforce or a comparable CRM, including reporting and dashboard build.
Strong analytical skills — comfortable building models and pipeline/forecast analysis independently.
Demonstrated ability to operate autonomously and partner effectively with US-based stakeholders and time zones.
Experience partnering with VP-level stakeholders and driving alignment without direct authority.
 Preferred Qualifications
Experience designing channel/partner incentive structures or deal registration processes.
Experience with multi-currency or cross-border reporting and compliance considerations.
Background in management consulting or investment banking, particularly with an MBA.
 What do we offer?
Private Health Insurance
Enhanced Assistance Program
Employee Dental Plan
Group Life Assurance (GLA)
Wellness Reimbursement
Pension employer match
Internet Allowance
 About Our Culture
 Smarsh hires lifelong learners with a passion for innovating with purpose, humility and humor. Collaboration is at the heart of everything we do. We work closely with the most popular communications platforms and the world’s leading cloud infrastructure platforms. We use the latest in AI/ML technology to help our customers break new ground at scale. We are a global organization that values diversity, and we believe that providing opportunities for everyone to be their authentic self is key to our success. Smarsh leadership, culture, and commitment to developing our people have all garnered Comparably.com Best Places to Work Awards. Come join us and find out what the best work of your career looks like.

title: GTM Analyst
description:
We're Civica and we deliver outcome focused value solutions that help deliver critical services for citizens all around the world. Civica works from local to central government, to education, to health and care, over 5,000 public bodies across the globe use our solutions to help provide critical services to over 100 million citizens.
Our aspiration is to be a GovTech champion everywhere we work around the globe, supporting the needs of citizens and those that serve them every day. Building on 21 years of continuous growth and success, we're at a pivotal point on our journey to realise that aspiration. 
 Why you'll love this opportunity as GTM Analyst with us 
Our Go-To-Market (GTM) Analytics team plays a critical role in helping Civica make smarter, data-led commercial decisions. As we continue to grow, having clear visibility of sales performance, trends and the effectiveness of our compensation plans is increasingly important. 
We're looking for a highly analytical and commercially minded GTM Analyst to join the team. This role will partner closely with our Sales and GTM leadership teams, using data to provide meaningful insights that support performance, planning and growth. 
A key focus of the role will be supporting the design, modelling and ongoing analysis of internal and external market data. You'll analyse GTM performance against targets, identify trends and patterns, model different scenarios, and help leaders understand what the data is telling us and where action may be needed. 
You'll also take ownership of key GTM dashboards and reporting, bringing together data and provide insights from across the business to provide a clear view of performance. Beyond regular reporting, you'll dig deeper into the numbers, delivering ad-hoc analysis that helps answer important commercial questions and supports better decision-making. 
 What you will do be to be successful in this role 
Performance & trend analysis - Identifying trends, patterns and opportunities within GTM data and translating them into clear, actionable commercial insights. 
Dashboarding & reporting - Owning and developing key dashboards and reporting that give Sales and GTM leaders a clear view of performance. 
Commercial insight - Going beyond reporting the numbers to explain what they mean, what is driving performance and where there may be opportunities or risks. 
Data interrogation - Carrying out ad-hoc analysis to answer commercial questions around sales performance, productivity, targets, compensation and wider GTM effectiveness. 
Business partnering - Working closely with Sales, Finance and GTM stakeholders to understand their data needs and provide insight that supports decision-making. 
Data quality & consistency - Helping ensure the data underpinning GTM reporting and compensation analysis is accurate, reliable and trusted.
 Requirements 
We're looking for someone who genuinely enjoys getting into the detail of the data, but who can also step back and understand the wider commercial picture. 
You'll ideally bring: 
Strong analytical and numerical skills, with confidence working with large and complex datasets. 
Experience analysing sales performance, commission, incentives or compensation plans. 
Strong Excel skills, including modelling and scenario analysis. 
Experience creating dashboards and turning complex data into meaningful insights for stakeholders. 
A commercially curious mindset. You don't just report what happened, you want to understand why it happened. 
Strong attention to detail, particularly when working with targets, compensation and performance data. 
Confidence working with senior stakeholders and communicating analytical findings in a clear, straightforward way. 
The ability to work at pace and balance recurring reporting with ad-hoc commercial analysis.
 We Want You to Bring Your Whole Self to Work 
 There is no such thing as the perfect candidate, so if you think you have what it takes but don't necessarily meet every single point on the list above, please still get in touch. We'd love to have a chat and see if you could be a great fit.
 Why You'll Love Working with Us 
 As a company, we're passionate about what we do and the citizens we serve. If you, too, want to champion the use of technology in public services to improve outcomes for citizens and public sector organizations, then Civica is the right place for you. We will help you unlock the best version of yourself, achieve career growth, and make a real difference to people and communities.
 We know that when our people are happy, they work better and have greater job satisfaction. Here's what you can expect:

At Civica, we are committed to building an inclusive and diverse workplace where everyone feels valued and supported. We believe that a variety of perspectives drives innovation and excellence, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds, cultures, and experiences.

title: Revenue Operations Manager
description:
Get to Know Us 
Kafene is revolutionizing the lease-to-own space. We’re the point-of-sale powerhouse making flexible lease-to-own accessible to everyone—prime and non-prime customers alike. Our secret weapon? Cutting-edge AI and machine learning that analyzes 20,000+ data inputs in real-time, empowering retailers across furniture, appliances, electronics, tires, and durable goods to say “yes” to more customers.
The numbers tell our story: over $500 million in originations and counting. But we’re just getting started.
Our 175-person team spans NYC headquarters, Wilmington, and remote talent across the globe—all united by a culture that thrives on collaboration, innovation, and genuine support. We don’t just talk about great workplace culture; we deliver it. That’s why Built In named us a Startup to Watch and Forbes recognized us as one of the Best Startup Employers.
Ready to be part of the fintech revolution? Join us.
Every merchant on Kafene’s platform can grow, stall, or slip away. The right treatment, promotion, or incentive at the right moment changes which way it goes. Your job is to make those programs happen, on time and with proof they worked.
As Manager, Revenue Operations, you’ll own the programs Kafene uses to grow, retain, and improve the performance of its merchant base: merchant treatments, experiments, promotions, and sales incentives. You’ll run each one end to end, from intake and setup through launch, tracking, and results. This is an execution-first role with real ownership; you’ll turn decisions from Revenue, Risk, and leadership into programs that go live on time, run cleanly in our systems, and produce outcomes we can measure.
You’ll work alongside a second Revenue Operations Manager and our Revenue Operations specialists, partnering daily with Business Development, Account Management, Marketing, Merchant Risk, Product, and Analytics. This is a hands-on role without direct reports.
 What You’ll Do 
Keep merchant treatments moving. Own day-to-day operation of the Retention Machine, Kafene’s merchant treatment program, and execute the RevOps-owned treatments flagged in Merchant Health Reviews, taking each from intake to completion in HubSpot and Jira with clear ownership and on-time turnaround.
Run experiments that settle questions. Partner with Analytics and Product to define success metrics, sample sizes, and measurement windows for merchant experiments, then turn readouts into clear recommendations for sales and leadership.
Launch promotions cleanly. Plan and execute merchant promotions from eligibility and terms through system configuration, launch, and measurement, and keep a single source of truth for every active, upcoming, and past promotion.
Make incentives airtight. Administer merchant incentive programs, including spiffs and rebates, owning eligibility tracking, payout calculations, approvals, and audit-ready documentation in partnership with Finance and sales leadership.
Build for scale. Create repeatable processes, SOPs, and dashboards that show program status, turnaround, and impact, and partner with Product and Risk to automate manual workflows so programs grow without added headcount.
Be the RevOps partner sales counts on. Serve as the go-to contact for Account Management and sales leadership, communicating proactively on launches, changes, and results.
 What You’ll Bring 
5+ years in revenue operations, sales operations, or a closely related operations role.
Hands-on experience executing promotions, pricing changes, or A/B experiments in a B2B or fintech environment, ideally alongside an analytics team.
Advanced HubSpot skills across tickets, pipelines, workflows, properties, and reporting, plus working proficiency in Google Sheets or Excel.
Sound judgment on edge cases that fall outside standard process, and the confidence to make the call or escalate it.
A clear, proactive communication style with sales leaders and cross-functional partners, and the organization to run many programs in parallel without dropping details.
Strong plus: experience in lease-to-own, point-of-sale, or payments; familiarity with merchant risk concepts like approval rates and merchant scoring; or experience with Jira, Confluence, and Sigma or another BI tool.
Likely backgrounds: RevOps or sales ops at a B2B fintech, payments, or POS company; merchant or partner operations at a marketplace or embedded finance platform; promotions or incentive operations inside a high-volume B2B sales org.
 Compensation and Benefits 
Base Salary: $130,000–$150,000
Healthcare: We prioritize your well-being by covering 80% of medical, dental, and vision insurance costs, including coverage for your spouse, children, and other dependents.
Retirement Benefits: Begin planning for your future from day one with our 401k plan.
Paid Time Off: We understand the importance of work-life balance. That’s why we offer flexible paid time off days starting from day one of your employment.
We’re building a team as diverse as the customers we serve. Kafene is proud to be an equal-opportunity employer, and we mean it. We welcome qualified applicants of every race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, veteran status, and all other legally protected characteristics.
Need accommodation during the application process? We’ve got you. If you’re applying for a U.S. position and require reasonable accommodation at any stage, reach out to careers@kafene.com with details about your request and contact information. We’re here to help make the process work for you.
Note: This email address is specifically for accommodation requests and will only respond to those inquiries.

title: Head of Customer Success
description:
About Dyad 
Dyad's mission is to improve the delivery and efficiency of healthcare.
We are building a platform to model and manage the flow of information within healthcare organisations, improving outcomes for patients, payers, and healthcare providers. We believe data handling in current healthcare systems is needlessly complex and disconnected, leading to isolated and inefficient decision making. To showcase how this technology can advance the delivery of healthcare and improve lives, we build and deploy products for healthcare providers and payers into the UK and US markets.
Dyad is a fast-growing, Series A-funded health tech company with a team of more than 70 people. We are expanding quickly as we grow from primary care into NHS secondary care and new international markets. We are passionate about technology and its applications in worthwhile ventures. New joiners will have a significant impact on the direction of the company, as well as our culture.
Our products
Dyad's Platform: Dyad's products are founded upon our Semantic AI platform, which enables payers and providers to access cutting-edge AI capabilities for their own use cases and applications. Our partners either use the platform APIs directly or work with us to develop applications for their use cases. For more information, please see our Platform page.
Primary care operations: Dyad develops a suite of products for healthcare operations, including:
BetterLetter, our AI tool helping practices decrease their admin burden in processing clinical letters. We use this to reduce staff time spent identifying codes to be applied to the record as well as suggesting follow-up tasks and workflow optimisations. BetterLetter helps providers save time, save cost, improve performance under audit and build staffing resilience.
 The role 
As Head of Customer Success at Dyad, you will shape how GP practices and PCN groups experience BetterLetter, making sure every customer gets lasting value from the product and grows with us. As we expand, the role will increasingly focus on growing revenue within our customer base and building the team to support new markets..
You will lead a small Customer Success team: a CS Team Lead and two Customer Success Executives, with further support from our Principal Clinical Practice Specialist. The team takes every practice from contract signature through onboarding, then into a structured account review lifecycle. You will set the standards for that lifecycle, coach the team to deliver it, and personally lead the conversations that matter most: our largest accounts, and practices at risk of not realising the full benefits of AI-assisted coding.
You will lead on keeping and growing revenue across our customer base. That means understanding what each practice and PCN needs, spotting opportunities to extend the value they get from BetterLetter, and acting early when a customer needs extra support. You will work closely with Product, Engineering, Commercial and Customer Operations so that customers stay, succeed and expand with us.
This is a senior role in a fast-growing company. BetterLetter is scaling quickly, with a strong pipeline of PCN and federation opportunities and SystmOne practices coming on stream. Our first contracts in new markets are also expected next year. You will build a Customer Success function ready for new markets and a larger, more diverse customer base.
Reporting to: VP Business Operations/VP Customer Operations
Direct reports: CS Team Lead and two Customer Success Executives.
This is a full-time position, which can be offered on a hybrid or remote basis.
Core responsibilities
 Customer success and growth: Partner with BetterLetter’s customers (GP practices and PCNs) to ensure they realise ongoing value, drive high adoption across internal teams, and foster long-term customer advocacy.
 Strategic accounts: Lead quarterly business reviews and annual account plans for our largest practices and PCN groups. Build senior relationships with practice partners, PCN clinical directors and federation leads, and identify expansion opportunities for the Commercial team.
 Customer lifecycle and operations: Oversee onboarding (with practices live within one month of contract) and the account review lifecycle that follows.
 At-risk accounts: Own every practice rated red, at any point in its lifecycle. Put a retention plan in place within 2 working days, lead difficult conversations with practices, and bring in clinical, product and AI expertise to resolve the underlying issue.
 Retention and net churn: Own the company target of net churn. Produce a monthly churn forecast, report gross and net churn to the leadership team, and maintain a single, reliable record of churned and paused practices.
 Re-engagement: Oversee the pipeline of paused practices run by the CS Team Lead, and agree with Sales how practices move between paused re-engagement and churned win-back.
 Complaint handling: Own the customer complaints procedure, built with our Regulatory team to align with our quality management system and ISO 27001. Make sure every complaint is logged, resolved within target and analysed for root causes.
 Team leadership: Line manage, coach and develop the Customer Success team. Set and review individual objectives quarterly, maintain cover across every role, and contribute to hiring as the team grows.
 Customer insight : Turn what the team hears from practices into clear, prioritised insight for Product and AI teams, and make sure practices hear back about the changes made in response.
 Cross-team collaboration: Work closely with Commercial, Product, Engineering, Customer Operations, Regulatory and Clinical colleagues to give practices a smooth journey from contract through to long-term success.Ensure cover in place for every role.
 Our hiring process 
Introductory screening interview (30 minutes).
Interviews with members of the Customer Success and Support team & at least one member of the Senior Management Team.
Final interview and offer.
 Requirements 
Credibility with GP practices is essential for this role. Practice managers, partners and PCN leaders need to trust that you understand how general practice works from the inside, so first-hand primary care experience (or equivalent) is our most important requirement.
Must-have:
Substantial first-hand experience in or of UK primary care. People who have worked as practice managers, operations or business managers, PCN managers, or primary care transformation leads strongly preferred. You understand how GP practices and PCNs work, who makes decisions, and the pressures practice teams face day to day.
Strong people management skills with a track record of building inclusive, high-performing teams.
Significant experience in customer success, account management or a comparable customer-facing role, including at least two years leading a team.
A track record of owning retention or churn targets and improving them.
Confidence leading difficult conversations with senior stakeholders, such as practice partners and PCN clinical directors.
Experience designing customer processes, such as onboarding, account reviews, health scoring or complaints handling.
Comfortable working with data to track customer health, forecast churn and report to a leadership team.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex topics clearly to clinical and non-clinical audiences.
A proactive, organised and customer-focused approach, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced startup environment.
Nice-to-have:
Experience in health tech, particularly products used by GP practices.
Familiarity with UK primary care clinical systems such as EMIS, SystmOne or Docman.
Background in clinical coding or primary care administration (for example SNOMED, QOF/IIF).
Experience with customer success platforms and CRM tools, such as Custify, HubSpot or Airtable.
Experience of complaints handling within a regulated or quality-managed environment, such as ISO 13485 or ISO 27001.
Experience building or scaling a Customer Success function in a growing company.
 Benefits 
Competitive Salary
Company Pension
25 days of paid annual leave (pro-rata)
A fun and flexible hybrid working environment
Access to our Employee Assistance Programme - Health Assured
A modern, dog-friendly office located near Chancery Lane with free drinks
hard_gaps: At least two years leading a team
Track record building high-performing teams
Understanding of how GP practices work

CSM in UK-London at a non-standout company
no pay stated in the ad or the feed, verify vs floor
Series A, 70-person health tech; sponsor licence status unknown, and the Skilled Worker floor may strain a startup Head of CS budget.
Role centres on people management and owning the CS operating rhythm, which Tom has never held.
NHS primary-care customer base (GP practices, PCNs) is a domain far from his GRC/legal enterprise SaaS background.
verdict: Head of CS at a small NHS health-tech startup demands team leadership Tom lacks and doesn't advance the RevOps pivot; skip.

The Revenue Operations team at Euna Solutions is hiring a Revenue Operations Analyst to own the reporting, forecasting, and compensation numbers that go-to-market leaders use to run the business: bookings and attainment, win rates, pipeline health, retention, and the commission payouts calculated against them. Own standing sales and Customer Success reporting: bookings versus plan, win rates, deal cycle trends, pipeline coverage, GRR, NRR, and churn, cut by segment, team, vertical, and solution
Answer the follow-up question behind every number: what changed, for whom, and what the gap is worth

title: Sales Operations Lead
description:
At FintechOS, we are looking for a Sales Operations Lead who wants to build, influence, and leave a visible mark. You will shape the processes, data, technology, and commercial rhythms behind our global enterprise sales organisation, creating an environment where the commercial team can focus, execute consistently, and thrive.
This is not a CRM administration role. You will have the mandate to challenge what is not working, simplify how we operate, and turn HubSpot into a genuine performance enabler. Your impact will be visible in seller productivity, pipeline quality, forecast confidence, and our ability to scale.
 Why this role is worth your next move 
• Build, do not simply maintain: shape the sales operating model and HubSpot environment for our next stage of growth.
• Influence at the right level: partner with senior commercial leaders on forecasting, planning, performance, and go-to-market decisions.
• Own outcomes end to end: identify the problem, design the solution, lead adoption, and measure the commercial impact.
• Solve meaningful complexity: enable enterprise sales into banks, insurers, and other highly regulated organisations.
The impact you will make
 Build the sales operating system: Create scalable processes and cadences that help sellers prioritise the right accounts, progress complex opportunities, and execute consistently.
 Make HubSpot work for sellers: Own CRM architecture, pipeline design, workflows, automation, integrations, reporting, data governance, and adoption.
 Increase seller productivity: Remove unnecessary administration, automate repetitive work, and return more time to customer-facing activity.
 Own the revenue execution cadence: Run pipeline inspection, deal reviews, forecast cadence, and the shared sales scoreboard, turning each into clear decisions, actions, and accountability.
 Turn data into decisions: Give sellers, managers, and leaders clear insight into priorities, risks, performance, and growth opportunities.
 Enable complex deals: Improve pricing, approvals, contracting, and cross-functional coordination across long enterprise sales cycles.
 Shape commercial planning: Partner with Sales Leadership and Finance on territories, quotas, capacity, coverage, and performance management.
 Lead meaningful change: Take operational improvements from idea through implementation, enablement, adoption, and measurable impact.
What you will bring
8+ years in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, or Commercial Operations, ideally within enterprise B2B SaaS.
Advanced HubSpot experience across CRM architecture, pipeline design, automation, reporting, integrations, data governance, and user adoption.
Experience supporting long, high-value sales cycles involving multiple decision-makers, procurement, legal, security, and executive stakeholders.
Hands-on ownership of forecasting, pipeline governance, territory planning, quota setting, or capacity planning.
Strong knowledge of ARR, ACV, bookings, pipeline coverage, win rate, sales velocity, and quota attainment.
Strong analytical and modelling skills using Excel or Google Sheets, plus Power BI, Tableau, Looker, or similar tools.
A track record of simplifying sales processes and improving seller productivity without sacrificing commercial discipline.
Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, and change leadership skills, with the confidence to challenge constructively.
Great to have
Experience in fintech, banking technology, insurance technology, payments, or another regulated industry.
Familiarity with MEDDPICC, MEDDIC, Challenger, or another enterprise sales methodology.
Experience with Gong, Outreach, ZoomInfo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Clari, or similar platforms.
Experience improving deal-desk, pricing, compensation, or partner-led sales processes.
You will know you are making an impact when
Sellers know where to focus and how to move opportunities forward.
HubSpot is valued as a selling tool, not treated as an administrative obligation.
Pipeline and forecast conversations are consistent, focused, and actionable.
Managers have the insight they need to coach effectively.
Commercial approvals and internal handoffs are faster and more predictable.
The sales operating model scales confidently with the business.
Who we are
FintechOS is a global fintech enablement company on a mission to make financial innovation accessible to every business. Our platform helps banks, insurers, and other financial institutions launch and scale financial products faster, bringing new solutions to market in as little as 12 weeks.
You will join an international team solving complex commercial and technology challenges in one of the world’s largest and most highly regulated industries. We value ownership, curiosity, collaboration, inclusion, and constructive challenge.
