Our Intelligent Network Operations platform delivers and enables AI-driven agentic ops at scale, automating and simplifying how companies manage, secure, and optimize their networks.
But what makes us different is how we work: we believe great work happens in an environment where you're trusted, heard, and supported. With teams globally, we're building a workplace culture that values collaboration and integrity as much as innovation. If you're looking to advance your career with a company that invests in its people, this is it.
As Manager of our Pooled Customer Success team, you will lead a team of 4 to 7 Customer Success Managers who share collective ownership of a large portfolio of customers. Your mandate is to build a high performing team that delivers consistent, measurable value across many accounts without the a named one to one relationship.
This is a different discipline from named account management. Success here comes from designing repeatable plays, prioritizing the right customers at the right moment, maintaining clean account context so any CSM can pick up any customer, and holding the team to response and follow through standards that protect retention at volume.
You are both an operator and a hands on coach. You build the coverage system, you improve it every quarter, and you develop CSMs who can move quickly, diagnose accurately, and create value in a compressed number of touchpoints.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Team Leadership & Talent Development 
- Lead, coach, and develop a team of 4 to 7 pooled CSMs supporting a shared customer portfolio.
- Manage workload distribution, queue coverage, and capacity across the team so no customer segment goes unattended.
- Conduct regular portfolio reviews, renewal and risk reviews, and performance check ins.
- Coach CSMs on rapid discovery, efficient customer conversations, and getting to value in fewer, higher quality interactions.
- Build a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
- Hire, onboard, and develop CSM talent suited to a fast moving, high volume environment.
- Driving Measurable Customer Value at Scale
- Operationalize our Customer Value Framework through standardized plays rather than bespoke plans.
- Ensure every customer in the pool receives defined lifecycle coverage, including onboarding confirmation, adoption checkpoints, and a structured pre renewal review.
- Establish clear value milestones and outcome criteria that apply consistently across the portfolio.
- Ensure product adoption is connected to tangible business results in every customer facing interaction.
- Monitor portfolio health signals and direct team effort toward the accounts where intervention changes the outcome.
 Retention, Expansion & Growth Alignment 
- Own retention performance for the pooled portfolio, including renewal readiness and early risk detection.
- Partner closely with Renewals and Sales leadership on renewal strategy and expansion routing.
- Ensure CSMs surface new use cases, new stakeholders, and expansion signals and hand them off cleanly.
- Influence retention strategy through data driven insights and repeatable risk mitigation plays.
- Operational Excellence & Scalability
- Define and enforce the operating rhythm for the pool, including coverage standards, response expectations, escalation paths, and handoff protocols.
- Ensure documentation discipline so that account context lives in the system, not in individual memory, and any CSM can serve any customer.
- Ensure CRM and CS tooling reflect accurate account health, engagement history, and renewal status.
- Use metrics such as coverage rate, time to first response, adoption, health scores, renewal rates, and expansion ARR to drive performance conversations.
- Identify automation and process improvements that increase capacity without increasing headcount.
- Cross Functional Leadership
- Serve as the voice of a large and diverse customer population internally while balancing business priorities.
- Partner with Support, Product, Professional Services, Renewals, and Sales to improve the customer journey for customers who do not have a dedicated resource.
- Surface systemic risks, adoption blockers, and product feedback trends to senior leadership, using the volume of the pool as an early warning system for the broader base.
- Contribute to strategic planning for the broader Customer Success organization.
 What You Bring 
- 5+ years of experience in B2B SaaS, including:
- 3+ years in Customer Success or account management
- 2+ years managing or leading CSM teams
- Experience operating a pooled, shared, or scaled coverage model, or a demonstrated ability to build one.
- Strong understanding of renewal strategy, retention management, and risk identification at volume.
- Proven ability to design and improve repeatable plays, playbooks, and operating standards.
- Comfort managing through systems and data rather than through individual account relationships.
- Strong analytical mindset, with the ability to translate portfolio signals into prioritized team action.
- A leadership style grounded in transparency, ownership, and high standards.

title: Revenue Enablement Manager
description:
This posting reflects a current, actively recruited opening at Float. All applications are being reviewed on a rolling basis. 
 About Float 
Float is on a mission to simplify finance for Canadian businesses, empowering them to eliminate complexity and unlock new opportunities. Through our innovative platform, Float enables businesses to streamline financial operations and optimize cash flow, so they can focus on what matters most: growth.
As one of Canada’s fastest growing companies and top-rated startups in 2025 , 2024 and 2023 , Float is customer-obsessed, passionate and entrepreneurial, with a team that includes leaders from Uber, Stripe, Shopify, Top Hat, Ada, Doordash, Snowflake, and Wealthsimple.
 Our Product 
Float is Canada’s intelligent financial operating system, combining modern financial services and software to help businesses spend, save, and grow. Trusted by more than 10,000 Canadian companies, Float provides high-limit corporate cards, automated expense management, next-day bill payments, high-yield accounts, and industry-leading support, all built in Canada, for Canada. Float recently announced our $85 million Series C , and is backed by world-class investors, including Inovia Capital, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, OMERS Ventures, and Silicon Valley Bank.
 About the Team 
Float is building a category defining Canadian fintech at the scale of the country's biggest banks. We operate on a consumption based revenue model, Cards TPV, not seats or contracts, which means our GTM teams win by driving real product usage, every month, compounding. We're in a defining competitive window, and we move with urgency, ownership, and an aggressive bias toward rebuilding how we work with AI.
 About the Role 
Float is hiring a dedicated Revenue Enablement Manager to own enablement for every customer facing team: BDRs, AEs, the Customer Activation team, and Customer Success. This is a senior individual contributor role, no direct reports, full ownership of the function. You'll report to the Head of GTM Strategy & Operations and work in close partnership with Sales, Customer Success, Product Marketing, and Product leadership.
You'll own the full loop: building content and learning pathways, embedding our SPICED sales methodology into how reps actually sell, standing up scorecards and reinforcement mechanisms (e.g., in Gong and with front line managers), and measuring the impact of these efforts. You'll also lead messaging and readiness for major product launches (partnering with PMM/Product for inputs), and skill building initiatives like discovery call quality, competitive positioning, and QBRs. 
Within your first 60 days, you'll also lead an evaluation of our LMS and make a recommendation on whether to keep, replace, or restructure it. This is your platform to build on, so you own the call.
 What you'll own 
 Enablement strategy and programs across BDR, AE, CAM, and CS: content, onboarding, learning pathways, and ongoing skill development
 Methodology reinforcement : embedding SPICED (and evaluating where frameworks like MEDDPICC or Challenger add value) into real rep behaviour, not just a deck
 Measurement and reinforcement infrastructure : scorecards, call scoring rubrics (e.g., in Gong or using other AI-forward tools), and a clear read on whether enablement is changing outcomes
 Product launch and messaging enablement : partnering with Product, Product Marketing, and Sales/CS leadership to prep customer facing teams ahead of key launches
 Tooling : operate day-to-day across Gong, Salesforce, Unify, Notion, and HubSpot; lead a first 60 days evaluation of our LMS
 Change management : driving adoption of new programs, tools, and skills across teams that are being asked to move fast
 What you'll bring 
5+ years owning or leading Sales/Revenue Enablement programs at a SaaS company; FinTech or consumption based revenue model experience is a bonus
Proven experience building and overseeing adult learning programs end-to-end, both the instructional design and the reinforcement/measurement of impact. This is a hard requirement: we're looking for someone who's done both halves, not just built content.
Working knowledge of a modern sales methodology (SPICED, MEDDPICC, or Challenger); we run SPICED today
Comfort operating in Gong and Salesforce day to day; LMS platform experience (WorkRamp or equivalent)
Prior quota carrying sales experience is a plus, not a requirement. That said, you'll need to earn credibility with a sales floor that moves fast and expects direct, practical coaching
A track record of using AI to create leverage in your own function: drafting content faster, mining call data for patterns, surfacing the highest priority gaps, not just adopting a tool because it exists
 How we work 
Float operates with high urgency and high ownership. You'll be expected to move fast, say the direct thing early, and treat AI as core to how you build and scale your own function. This role exists because enablement work at Float needs someone who can own it, not administer it.
 About You 
Here's what sets you up for success at Float:
 You Put Customers First, Always. You care deeply about delivering meaningful value. Whether you're building internal systems or customer-facing features, you're always thinking about how to make life better for our users.
 You Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, step up to challenges, and seek solutions proactively, doing what's best for the business, not just your role.
 You Think Big and Move Fast. You're energised by building from 0 to 1. You're not afraid to challenge the status quo, experiment quickly, and learn as you go.
 You Constantly Learn and Grow. You're hungry to improve your craft and open to feedback. You bring a growth mindset to everything you do.
 You Raise the Bar. You care about doing things well and efficiently. You balance speed with rigour and always look for ways to improve how we work.
 You Win as a Team. You're a generous collaborator who values communication, context, and shared wins. You lift others up and help make the team stronger.
 Why You Should Join 
Work at one of Canada's fastest-growing fintech companies
Make a real impact in a high-autonomy, high-growth role
Collaborate with an ambitious and supportive team
Competitive compensation, equity options, and benefits
Hybrid work model – we are based in Toronto with in-office days for connection and collaboration
Enjoy catered team lunches every Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday
Bring your pup to our dog-friendly office
Thrive in a high-trust, high-performance culture where your work truly matters
 In Short 
At Float, you’ll thrive if you’re bold, curious, and eager to make a real impact. We're building something special and having a lot of fun along the way. If you’re excited to build, grow, and win together, we’d love to meet you. 
 We’re committed to building a workplace that’s welcoming and accessible for everyone. If you need any accommodations during the hiring process or once you join Float, just let us know! You can reach out to Vic ( victoria@floatfinancial.com ), and we’ll work with you to make sure you have what you need to succeed. 
 AI Use in Our Hiring Process 
We use technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), to support parts of our hiring process. This may include AI-assisted scheduling and candidate communications, and AI-generated interview notes, guides or summaries to help our team focus on the conversation. All hiring decisions are made by humans.

title: Senior Manager, Sales Enablement and Strategy
description:
About Metergy Solutions Inc. (“Metergy”)
 Metergy has the energy, rapid growth and excitement of a startup, together with a rock-solid, recession-proof business that has a 45 year track record. We’re a technology company that drives huge carbon emission reductions. This is a once-in-a-career opportunity.
As one of North America’s most experienced submetering providers, Metergy has brought turnkey solutions to clients for over 45 years. Metergy supplies, installs and remotely reads meters to measure individual suite consumption of electricity, water, gas, and thermal energy in multi-residential and commercial buildings, and bills and collects for the cost of commodities and administrative charges for the services provided. The business model allows for long-term recurring revenue through an innovative Submetering as a Service (SaaS) model. Submetering is proven to reduce in-suite energy consumption by 40%, driving decarbonization efforts for Metergy’s clients. This performance has enabled Metergy to issue green bonds and obtain green financing.
Positioned as the #1 submeter provider in the New York and Canadian markets, and one of the largest in North America, Metergy has more than 900,000 contracted meters, issues over 4M utility bills annually and has over 500 team members. Metergy is a portfolio company of Brookfield Infrastructure Partners. Brookfield is one of the world’s largest investors, owners and operators of infrastructure assets across the utilities, transport, energy, data and sustainable resources sectors. This sponsorship provides Metergy with access to large-scale capital, infrastructure investment expertise and global reach.
 Our Mission
 Provide building owners and occupants with accurate and reliable utility consumption data through market-leading expertise in turnkey submetering and billing, while fostering a workplace with inspired team members empowered to do more good.
At Metergy, we don’t just believe in our people; we champion them. When individuals feel valued, supported, and inspired to grow, incredible things happen. That’s why we’re thrilled to be recognized as a Great Place to Work for the third consecutive year ! This achievement reflects our unwavering commitment to building a workplace that’s respectful, inclusive, and high-performing.
Come be part of a team that leads with passion , thrives on positivity , and delivers with precision . We’re proud of who we are and even prouder of where we’re headed.
 Metergy office location is in Markham but will be moving to North York toward the end of 2026!
 The Role
 The Senior Manager, Sales Strategy & Enablement is a strategic and hands-on leader responsible for strengthening how Metergy plans, manages and executes sales across Canada and the United States.
Reporting to the Vice President, Sales Enablement, this role owns core sales operations processes, including forecasting, pipeline governance, performance reporting and sales systems business requirements. The role also advances MEDDICC adoption, seller effectiveness, pricing insights and targeted pipeline development.
Working closely with Sales, Marketing, Finance, Operations and Client Success, the successful candidate will turn data into action, improve commercial workflows and build visibility from opportunity creation through contracted meters and revenue activation. Leadership is exercised through process ownership and cross-functional influence, with sales leaders retaining accountability for sales results and forecast commitments.
 Responsibilities:
 Sales forecasting and performance management:
Own the sales forecasting process, including forecast definitions, submission cadence, consolidation and accuracy reporting; partner with sales leaders to identify deal risks, timing changes and gaps against targets. 
Coordinate pipeline reviews, monthly performance reviews and quarterly business reviews, providing actionable insights and tracking agreed actions with accountable owners.

That's the engine. And we're looking for the person who runs it.

Backed by more than five decades of ACIC pharmaceutical industry experience, we support sterilization and contamination control, cleanrooms, formulation and pure-fluid systems, radiopharmaceutical production and radiation shielding (including hot cells and automated processing and dispensing), freeze drying, filling, labelling and inspection, as well as packaging, vacuum processing and automation – helping pharmaceutical manufacturers, healthcare institutions and research organizations enhance efficiency, ensure compliance and accelerate success.

Every step follows ACIC's newly revised CRM BD & SALES Workflow Process in Salesforce. You are its guardian. Discipline is how we win.

ServiceNow is formalizing Exclusive Networks as its authorized distributor for EMEA, extending our two-tier channel model into the European Union and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Partner with Legal, Finance, Tax, and Trade Compliance to resolve jurisdiction-specific questions before they become program issues.
 Stakeholder management

title: Customer Success Lead (SMB)
description:
2 Berkeley Street, Toronto, Ontario, Canada, M5A 4J6
full-time . January 13, 2026
Description
At Chexy, we’re reshaping the way money moves—making payments smarter, faster, and more rewarding.
We started by being the first in Canada to let people pay their biggest and most painful bills with credit cards and earn rewards on money they had to spend anyway. Now, we’re on a much bigger mission: to build a super app that acts as your co-pilot for all your money—helping you get more value from every dollar you spend.
As a high-growth fintech startup, we’re at the forefront of payments innovation, and we’re looking for hungry, ambitious people to help us scale. If you thrive in a fast-moving, high-energy environment and want to be part of something big, we’d love to work with you.
**About this role**
We’re looking for an experienced, relationship-driven Customer Success Lead (SMB) to own the end-to-end experience for our Small & Medium Business (SMB) customers. In this role you will provide high-touch, high-quality support and success for our SMB customers—primarily via email and Intercom — while building the SMB customer success “program” (playbooks, workflows, and standards) so the experience is consistent as we grow. You will partner closely with our Growth/Sales team to ensure new SMB clients are onboarded smoothly and set up for long-term success.
**What You’ll Do**
**SMB Customer Ownership & Relationship Management**
* Own a portfolio of SMB customers as their primary post-sale point of contact.
* Build trusted relationships with SMB decision-makers and operators through proactive communication, check-ins, and thoughtful follow-through.
* Ensure customers have a consistently excellent experience across onboarding, payments/operations, and ongoing support.
**SMB Onboarding (Partnering with Growth/Sales)**
* Work closely with Growth/Sales to ensure a clean handoff and a strong “first 30 days” experience for every new SMB client.
* Run onboarding kickoffs, collect requirements, align on timelines, and set expectations.
* Coordinate internally to unblock onboarding (product, engineering, operations, risk/fraud, etc.) and drive customers to first value quickly.
* Maintain/iterate an SMB onboarding checklist and standard onboarding communications.
**High-Touch SMB Support & Escalations**
* Respond to SMB inquiries via email and our CX platform (encouraging fast, high-quality resolutions).
* Troubleshoot issues end-to-end: clarify needs, identify root causes, coordinate fixes, and close the loop.
* Handle escalations with calm urgency—keeping customers informed while mobilizing internal teams.
**Build the SMB Customer Success Program (Process + Quality)**
* Design and document SMB-specific success workflows and standards (SOPs, macros, templates, SLAs, escalation paths).
* Create/maintain customer-facing and internal documentation: help articles, FAQs, onboarding guides, playbooks.
* Identify recurring SMB issues and drive continuous improvement through better process, automation, and product feedback.
* Improve how our chatbot-first CX operation supports SMBs (e.g., routing rules, escalation triggers, internal handoff protocols).
**What We’re Looking For**
* 3+ years of experience in Customer Success, Account Management, Implementation, or high-touch Support serving SMB customers (fintech/payments or SaaS experience is a plus).
* Proven ability to manage customer relationships with excellent written communication (email is a core channel for this role).
* Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills—you can navigate ambiguity, investigate issues, and coordinate cross-functionally.
* Process-minded and organized: you enjoy building playbooks, improving workflows, and making things repeatable.
* Comfortable working closely with a Growth/Sales team to deliver a great onboarding experience and smooth handoffs (without being responsible for upsells).
* Tech-savvy: comfortable learning tools quickly and working in platforms like Intercom (or similar), Notion, Slack, and Google Suite.
* This role is fully in-office 5 days a week .
**Nice to Have**
* Experience at an early-stage or fast-growing startup
* Experience at a fintech or a B2C SaaS company
* Familiarity with payment products (card issuing, money transfers, credit, etc.)

title: Director of GTM Data, Processes, and AI Enablement
description:
MaintainX is a leading mobile-first work execution platform for industrial and frontline teams. More than 13,000 customers , including Duracell, McDonald's, Shell, DHL and Volvo, use MaintainX to cut unplanned downtime and run better operations, across 13.9 million managed assets and 79.5 million completed work orders.
 In August 2026 MaintainX became part of Autodesk, joining Autodesk Operations Solutions , the organization unifying Autodesk's operations platform alongside Tandem, FlexSim and Fusion Operations. Autodesk's strategy is to converge design, make and operate into one continuous lifecycle: design an asset, build it, run it, then feed what you learn running it back into the next design. Autodesk had design and make. Operate is the phase that tells you what actually happened, and it is ours.
 The Role
 MaintainX (part of Autodesk) is hiring a Director of GTM Data, Processes, and AI Enablement to own critical foundations of our GTM teams, including:
Customer and prospect data within our CRM;
Core CRM processes that enable selling across GTM teams (e.g., opportunity workflows, territory assignment processes); and
Our internal GenAI and automation efforts driving efficiency, effectiveness, and productivity of our GTM teams
This role also owns the integration of the MaintainX GTM teams into Autodesk GTM systems, processes, and GTM motions, for the core functional areas of the role – a key area of focus for the next 6 to 18 months.
The role sits in the broader MaintainX Revenue Strategy and Operations team and leads a small team of data quality analysts, but we expect this role to drive the majority of its impact through others outside of their direct team. Across all functional areas, this role will be working with, influencing, and directing the work of senior stakeholders, front-line managers, and ICs across Marketing, Rev Ops, Enablement, and GTM Engineering. We need someone with deep functional expertise that knows best practices and has rapid pattern recognition for solutions to GTM issues, who is technical enough to be credible with engineers, and is practical enough to be trusted by sellers to get work done.
 What You'll Do
 Own CRM data quality and governance
Set the strategy, standards, and governance for leads, contacts, accounts, and account hierarchies. That includes parent/child structures, holding companies, franchises, PE portfolios, and multi-site customers.
Move data quality from cleanup to prevention. Put in intake controls, matching and dedupe rules, and enrichment precedence, and track them on a data quality scorecard with targets.
Show leadership what data gaps cost in revenue, and make GTM data ready for AI use cases.
Lead the team doing this work, including writing requirements for GTM Systems to implement.
Develop deduplication strategies and processes to manage a dual CRM environment across MaintainX and Autodesk
 Drive core CRM-based processes and workflows
Own CRM territory management developing the processes and systems requirements to implement the territory design and strategy defined by GTM leadership and Rev Ops teams.
Own our rules of engagement: account ownership, crediting, and conflict resolution across segments, regions, and teams – including both MaintainX selling in isolation and coordination between MaintainX and Autodesk sellers
Own optimization of CRM processes and workflows for end user teams, including building an understanding of current processes, identifying points of improvement, working with GTM systems and Rev Ops teams to define business requirements
Collaborate with Rev Ops, Enablement, and GTM systems teams to ensure field teams know how to use our systems and processes as they change, through release communications, training, and documentation.
 Lead the GTM AI program for field teams
Run out GenAI and automation program for GTM field teams end to end: intake, prioritization and resource allocation across GTM and Engineering, operating cadences, solution evaluation, executive readouts, field enablement.
Lead discovery with Sales leaders to find the highest-value automation and agent opportunities. Align leadership and our GTM engineering team on one prioritized roadmap.
Own business requirements, build-vs-buy recommendations, and testing for centrally built solutions. Partner with Engineering to build and launch them.
Set the standards for how teams build their own solutions: knowledge base governance, a quality bar, and a path for scaling proven team-built tools across the org.
Own rollout with Enablement and measure adoption and ROI. The measure is workflows changed, not trainings delivered.
 Lead integration efforts for MaintainX GTM into Autodesk
Own the GTM integration plan, governance and coordination across the workstreams, including: systems and data, account mapping and ownership, territories, sales process alignment, rules of engagement for joint selling, and enablement.
Coordinate stakeholders across both organizations. Run the cadence, track risks and dependencies, and escalate decisions.
Be accountable for integration outcomes, not just coordination.
 About You
10+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or GTM strategy at a B2B SaaS company, including 3+ years leading people.
Deep expertise in core sales processes, territory design, and rules of engagement.
Strong command of the CRM data model: Salesforce objects, account hierarchies, matching, and enrichment. You define and specify; you don't need to configure.
Hands-on experience bringing AI into GTM workflows (LLMs, agents, workflow automation), with results you can measure. Fluent enough to work credibly with engineers.
A track record of leading large cross-functional programs through influence, including with VP and C-level leaders.
M&A or GTM integration experience is strongly preferred.
Clear writing and speaking. You can make complex tradeoffs understandable to sellers, engineers, and executives.
 Our mission is to keep the physical world running. Factories, fleets, hospitals and campuses stay up because the people who maintain them have tools worth using. That is what we build.
 Compensation and benefits. Base pay is one part of the package. Depending on the role, compensation may also include commission, an annual bonus and equity. Benefits differ by country. For roles in the United States, Autodesk’s benefits are described at benefits.autodesk.com. For roles in Canada and other countries, the plan differs on health coverage, retirement and leave, and your recruiter will walk you through it.
 Belonging. We take pride in a culture where everyone can thrive. More at autodesk.com/company/global-belonging. More on where this is going: Autodesk CEO Andrew Anagnost on building the future of connected operations, and AOS SVP Stephen Hooper on welcoming MaintainX to Autodesk.

title: Director Strategic Revenue Operations
description:
Context & Impact: 
As Lansweeper continues to mature its Revenue Operations function, this position takes on broader strategic ownership across forecasting, GTM planning, deal operations, commissions, and AI-native transformation of the RevOps engine. 
As Director Strategic Revenue Operations, you are the person who tells leadership whether we are on track, explains why when we are not, and turns that into recommendations they can act on. Reporting to the COO and working closely with the CRO and CCO, you own the full funnel view from lead to closed won — and you help define what an AI-native revenue organization looks like at Lansweeper. 
Your near-term goals: establish a forecast process leadership can plan against, build one version of the truth across Marketing, Sales and Customer Success, and progressively rebuild how RevOps works when agents and automation are available. 
 Challenge: 
The main challenges you'll face are: 
 Forecast predictability. Leadership needs a forecast it can plan against, with accuracy measured and improving cycle over cycle across segments, regions and categories. 
 One version of the truth. Marketing, Sales and Customer Success each have their own view. You build the single funnel view all of them recognize as theirs — and you own the definitions that make it add up. 
 An AI-native RevOps function. Not bolting AI onto today's processes, but asking what forecasting, analysis, planning and deal operations look like when agents do much of the work — and holding the business case from hypothesis to realized value. 
 Authority without a reporting line. The systems, data and AI teams you depend on do not report to you. You get there with a business case and standards people accept. 
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Forecasting 
Set the forecast process, methodology, stage and category definitions and the tooling behind them — Sales leadership runs the forecast calls; you build the machine that makes their call reliable. 
Measure forecast accuracy every cycle by segment, region and category, report it alongside actuals, and drive it up. 
Challenge the roll-up, surface the risk and upside the number is hiding, and flag early where coverage does not support the commit. 
 Performance & Insight — Lead to Closed Won 
Own the golden set of sales and marketing reports reaching the CRO, CEO and board, and the definitions that make the full funnel add up: lead and MQL criteria, stage conversion, attribution and handoffs between Marketing, Sales and Customer Success. 
Partner with Marketing on spend, pipeline contribution, funnel velocity and conversion by source and segment. 
Set the operating rhythm: forecast, pipeline, monthly business and quarterly GTM reviews, with clear decisions, owners and follow-up. 
 Annual Planning 
Drive the annual GTM planning cycle with the CRO, CCO, COO, Finance and the data team, translating the growth ambition into segment, territory, quota and capacity models. 
Set the pipeline, coverage and marketing investment assumptions behind the plan, and run the quarterly re-forecast and in-year reallocation. 
 Sales Operations, Deal Desk & Pricing 
Run GTM sales operations as a service to the sales teams: deal structuring, data quality, account and lead assignment, territory and quota administration. 
Build and operate a real deal desk with standards, approval paths and turnaround commitments — quality enforced up front rather than corrected afterwards. 
Set pricing operations: discount governance, approval thresholds, price book maintenance and rollout of pricing and packaging changes. 
 Commissions 
Own commission plan design with the CRO, CCO and Finance, and the system behind it: mechanics, quota logic, accelerators, payout rules, and the accuracy and auditability of the payout cycle. 
Run rollout, seller queries and disputes against clear service levels. 
 GTM Data & Systems 
Establish GTM data quality and master data as a permanent capability, not a clean-up project, and enforce the data contract with the teams that own the systems. 
Translate GTM needs into a prioritized, business-cased demand list for GTM Apps, CRM, Data and Quote-to-Cash leaders. 
 AI 
Rebuild how Strategic RevOps works when agents and automation are available: forecasting and pipeline inspection, revenue and root-cause analysis, planning and scenario modelling, deal operations, data quality monitoring and recurring reporting. 
Identify where AI moves a number — and say plainly where it does not. Set the business priorities for GTM AI Labs and hold the business case from hypothesis to realized value. 
 Leadership 
Lead and grow the Strategic RevOps team (2 direct reports, 9 indirect); operate as a trusted counterpart to the leadership team with the standing to challenge the plan and the numbers. 
Lead through influence across the systems, data and AI teams your outcomes depend on. 
 Hard Skills: 
5+ years in Revenue Operations, including several years as Senior Director level in a fast-paced B2B SaaS scale-up. 
Built a forecast process, methodology and tooling for a multi-segment, multi-region organisation, with demonstrable improvement in accuracy. 
Owned annual GTM planning, territory, quota and capacity modelling at the same scale. 
Led a sales operations function including sales process design, deal desk, pricing operations and GTM data governance. 
Fluent in full-funnel analytics: conversion, attribution, velocity and marketing spend efficiency — able to hold that conversation with a Marketing leader. 
Hands-on with commission plan design and a commission system (Xactly, CaptivateIQ, Spiff, Everstage or similar); deep experience in CRM (Salesforce preferred) and BI tooling. 
Demonstrated, hands-on AI experience in a RevOps or GTM setting: concrete examples of AI-powered workflows, analyses or agents you have led or embedded, ideally with measurable impact. You don't need to have engineered them yourself, but you do need to have made them stick. 
 Soft Skills: 
Equally credible in a leadership debate and inside a dataset — able to hold a strategic conversation with a CRO, CFO and a data engineer on the same day. 
Able to drive outcomes through teams that do not report to you — influence, business case, standards. 
Clear, direct communicator who can translate complex analysis into decisions and follow-up. 
 AI Specific Skills: 
Lansweeper is an AI-native company. AI fluency is a hard requirement in this role — on three levels at once. 
 Personal. AI is part of your daily work for analysis, modelling, research and communication, and you evaluate what it produces critically. 
 Functional. You make Strategic RevOps progressively AI-native, redesigning workflows and building the team's ability to work alongside agents — from forecasting and pipeline inspection to deal operations and recurring reporting. 
 Business. You prioritise GTM AI opportunities on measurable commercial impact, work with GTM AI Labs, Data and Systems to scale the strongest, and hold the business case from hypothesis to realised value. 
We believe AI multiplies strong Revenue Operations expertise. It does not substitute for it. 
 Team Info: 
You'll join the RevOps team, working closely with the CRO, CCO, COO, Finance, GTM AI Labs, Data and GTM Apps leadership. 
Team size: 2 direct reports, 9 indirect, based across Belgium and the United States. 
This role reports to the COO. 
 Our Offer: 
 Salary: 
€113,000 – €183,467gross (EUR, Belgium, based on full-time employment) 
 Belgium 
Meal vouchers (€10/day), ecocheques (€250/year), vacation payout in June, and a 13th month in December. 
Time off — 20 days holiday + 12 ADV days + 12 public holidays. 
Health & protection — Full hospitalization and outpatient insurance, life insurance, disability coverage, and mental health support. 
Pension — Employer-paid pension plan included. 
Work setup — Hybrid working with full telework equipment and a monthly home working allowance. 
Extra — Flexible Income Plan to shape part of your package once a year. Company car or mobility budget included from a certain level. 
 United States 
• Comprehensive package (including paid holidays, medical, etc).
 About Lansweeper: 
Lansweeper is the AI Cyber Asset Intelligence platform helping IT and Security teams gain full visibility, reduce cyber risk, and scale automation with confidence. 
In today's complex IT, OT, cloud, and IoT environments, fragmented asset data slows decisions and increases risk. We transform raw asset data into a continuously validated, trusted source of truth — so teams can move faster and act with certainty. 
With Lansweeper, organizations can: 
 See – Truly complete visibility across hybrid environments 
 Know – Enriched asset intelligence with lifecycle and risk context 
 Act – Automate workflows, coordinate remediation, and enforce policy at scale 
From universal asset discovery to AI-powered intelligence, we provide the shared foundation modern IT Operations, Cybersecurity, and Digital Transformation teams rely on. 
 Our culture: 
We're built on four core values: 
 One Team – United across boundaries 
 We Care – Customers and people at the center 
 We Grow – Learning, sharing, improving 
 We Deliver – Focusing on what truly matters 
 Pay Transparency: 
At Lansweeper, every role is assigned to a level defined by three things: the expertise it requires, the complexity it involves, and the scope of impact it carries. 
Each level maps to a salary band based on salary benchmarks from the Software/SaaS industry of your country, so your pay reflects what the market pays for comparable roles. 
The gross salary range for this role is €113,000 – €183,467 (EUR, Belgium) (based on full-time employment). 
Where you land within that range depends on the expertise you bring, the complexity you have navigated, the scope of impact you have owned, and your track record of delivering results in comparable roles — the same criteria applied consistently to every candidate. 
We welcome applicants of all backgrounds, regardless of gender, religion, ethnic origin, age, sexual orientation, or disability. 
 AI Usage during Hiring Process: 
We use AI to support and not replace during the hiring process. HR decisions are made by our talent acquisition team. You can request more info at any time via recruitment@lansweeper.com

GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. An overview of this role
As a Customer Success Architect, you’ll be a strategic advisor to some of GitLab’s most important customers, helping them connect our DevSecOps platform to their business goals and realize meaningful, long-term outcomes. You’ll partner closely with customers after the sale to turn pre-sales command plans into concrete success plans, guide them along the customer journey, and drive hands-on enablement, adoption, utilization, and maturity. Reporting into a Senior Manager within our North America Customer Success organization, you’ll own a book of customers, act as their primary GitLab liaison for questions and escalations, and coordinate with Product Management, Engineering, Sales, Professional Services, and Support so customers can navigate complex technical and organizational challenges with confidence.
You’ll use your understanding of Git, software development lifecycles, and continuous integration, continuous deployment, and DevSecOps practices to help customers adopt best practices and stay current with new GitLab capabilities. In your first year, success looks like building strong, consultative relationships with key stakeholders, increasing adoption of the GitLab platform, and strengthening retention, growth, and customer satisfaction across your portfolio.
What you’ll do
Partner with customers to translate pre-sales command plans and desired business outcomes into actionable objectives and clear success criteria.
Guide customers on how to best use the GitLab platform, including common DevSecOps best practices, Git workflows, CI/CD, and adoption patterns.
Own a book of customers and drive adoption, retention, expansion, and overall satisfaction through ongoing strategic and technical engagement.
Build and maintain Customer Success Plans, define critical goals and key performance indicators, and track progress with customers over time.
Act as the primary GitLab liaison for assigned accounts, coordinating responses to questions, issues, and escalations across Support, Product Management, Sales, and Professional Services.
Provide hands-on technical enablement and onboarding, including education on new GitLab features, releases, and relevant use cases.
Program manage account escalations, ensuring root causes are understood, follow-up actions are owned, and stakeholders are informed.
Collaborate with Services and other internal teams to identify and recommend training, enablement, and maturity opportunities aligned to customer needs.
What you’ll bring
Practical understanding of Git, common branching strategies, and modern software development lifecycles.
Working knowledge of continuous integration, continuous deployment, and DevSecOps practices.
Experience partnering with customers to define business outcomes and translate them into actionable success plans, key goals, and measures.
Background in customer success, post-sales, or professional services roles focused on adoption, retention, and satisfaction.
Ability to manage a portfolio of customers, including handling escalations and coordinating across Support, Product Management, Sales, and Professional Services.
Strong communication, presentation, and organizational skills, with attention to detail and analytical thinking.
Experience planning and managing projects or initiatives in technical environments, including identifying training and enablement needs.
Alignment with GitLab’s values and interest in applying transferable skills from related roles or industries, with flexibility to travel as needed according to company policy.
About the team
We are part of GitLab’s Customer Success organization. Our mission is to help customers align the GitLab platform with their business objectives through hands-on technical enablement, driving adoption, utilization, and DevSecOps maturity while building strong, consultative relationships. As Customer Success Architects, we act as trusted advisors and key liaisons between customers and the broader GitLab ecosystem, collaborating closely with Product Management, Engineering, Sales, Support, and Professional Services to address questions, guide roadmaps, and navigate escalations. We work in an all-remote, asynchronous way, coordinating across time zones to support a focused set of strategic accounts and ensure long-term customer success.

title: Strategy & Operations Manager (Revenue)
description:
(On-site - reports to the VP, Sales)
About Clutch
We’re on a mission to reinvent the way people buy, sell, and own cars.
Clutch is Canada’s largest online used car retailer, delivering a seamless, hassle-free car buying and selling experience to drivers everywhere. Customers can browse hundreds of cars from the comfort of their home, get the right one delivered to their door, and enjoy peace of mind with our 10-Day Money-Back Guarantee... and that’s just the beginning.
Named two years in a row to the Globe & Mail’s list of the Top Growing Companies in Canada and also awarded spots on Deloitte’s Technology Fast 50TM and Fast 500TM lists, we’re looking to add curious, hard-working, and driven individuals to our growing team.
Headquartered in Toronto, Clutch was founded in 2017 and currently services Ontario, British Columbia, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, and Prince Edward Island. Clutch is backed by a number of world-class investors, including D1 Capital, Altos Ventures, BMO Capital Partners, Canaan, Real Ventures, and others. To learn more, visit clutch.ca.
About the role
We’re looking for a smart, resourceful, and analytically strong individual to join our Revenue team as Strategy and Operations Manager (Revenue). This role is an exceptional opportunity for someone early in their career 1-5 years post-grad who’s hungry to drive impact across a high-growth sales organization - working side by side with our VP of Sales on strategic initiatives, performance insights, and cross-functional projects that unlock growth.
What You’ll Do
Project-Based Execution
Lead and execute small to medium-sized strategic projects that drive incremental improvement across the sales team—ranging from process optimization to frontline tools to performance analysis.
Take ownership of project scoping, planning, execution, and results measurement—working across disciplines to see initiatives through end-to-end.
Ruthlessly prioritize initiatives that move the needle and align with broader revenue goals.
Work Cross-Functionally to Drive Change
Collaborate with Sales, Product, Marketing, Customer Experience, and Engineering to remove friction in the sales process and bring structure to ambiguity.
Be equally comfortable building a business case in Excel, presenting findings to the VP Sales, or jumping into a call with a distressed customer to understand root causes.
Translate complex problems into actionable insights—and ensure action happens.
Data-Driven Insights & Sales Strategy
Dive deep into sales and funnel data to uncover insights and opportunities. You’ll be expected to bring a strong analytical toolkit and be an 8+/10 when it comes to working with data.
Support forecasting, territory planning, performance dashboards, and root cause analysis to inform sales leadership decision-making.
Develop simple, clear, and persuasive recommendations backed by data and common sense.
Self-Learning & Experimentation
Take initiative to self-learn new tools, frameworks, and strategies—whether it’s mastering ChatGPT, learning how to write SQL, or figuring out how a new system works with minimal handholding.
Be proactive in experimenting with new ideas, rapidly testing assumptions, and applying learnings in real-time.
Develop comfort navigating ambiguity and unfamiliar territory—you’ll regularly tackle challenges that don’t come with a playbook.
What We’re Looking For
1-5 years of experience in management consulting, investment banking, sales strategy, business operations, or a high-performing startup environment.
8+/10 with data: Strong proficiency with Excel/Sheets required; experience with SQL, BI tools (e.g., Looker, Tableau)
Proven ability to lead structured projects and think strategically, while also rolling up your sleeves to get things done.
Comfortable with ambiguity and change—able to thrive in a fast-paced, ever-evolving environment.
Intellectually curious, fast learner, and someone who brings strong judgment and common sense to every conversation.
Strong communication and collaboration skills—you’re just as comfortable with execs as you are with frontline staff or developers.
Gritty, humble, and high-agency: you take initiative, own problems, and don’t wait to be told what to do.
Nice to Have
A genuine interest in Clutch’s industry—automotive, marketplaces, consumer tech, or the future of retail.
Passion for building things from the ground up and a desire to grow into a leadership role in the future.
Why Clutch
Partner directly with the VP Sales on initiatives that materially impact top-line performance.
Solve meaningful problems, fast: You’ll be in the room where decisions happen and have the chance to influence direction across the business.
Build your career: Whether your goal is GM, Product, Strategy, or Ops—this role sets a strong foundation for growth.

Working closely with our sales teams and leaders, and with Product, you'll turn our roadmap into revenue, with a particular focus on growing our financial services product line.
At Treatwell we don't just sell software: we help Europe's best salons and spas digitalise their business, grow their revenue and improve the experience they offer their clients.
You'll be the strategic owner of go-to-market for Treatwell across Europe. With a strong commercial mindset and a highly collaborative approach, you'll define how we position, price, package and launch our products, and partner with Sales to turn them into real, measurable revenue.
 You Will Be Responsible For
Commercial go-to-market strategy: Own and lead Treatwell's European go-to-market strategy, defining target segments, positioning, pricing, packaging and commercial priorities, with a clear focus on revenue growth.
Financial services revenue: Own and lead projects that drive revenue for the financial services product line, from payments to new financial solutions, setting clear targets and taking accountability for results.
Sales partnership: Work closely with our sales teams and sales leaders across markets to shape commercial plans and targets, and turn go-to-market strategy into pipeline, deals and revenue.
Sales enablement & playbooks: Build scalable playbooks, pricing guidance, sales narratives and training that help local market teams sell our products and drive adoption on the ground.
Product launches: Partner with Product to bring new products and features to market, from validation and pilots through to full European rollout, bringing the commercial and customer perspective into the roadmap.
Product-led growth: Alongside our sales teams, build in-app and self-serve sales motions that help adoption and revenue scale efficiently.
Cross-functional leadership: Partner with Product, Supply, Finance, Operations, Legal and local market teams to embed payments into acquisition, onboarding, account management and retention.
Strategy into execution: Translate strategy into clear execution plans with owners, timelines and KPIs, proactively removing blockers and driving accountability across teams that don't report directly into the role.
Commercial performance & optimisation: Track and drive adoption, revenue and margin across markets, using data and customer insight to optimise pricing, packaging and the sales funnel.
Stripe partnership: Manage Treatwell's strategic partnership with Stripe, acting as the senior commercial point of contact and aligning joint go-to-market plans and growth priorities.
 About You
Proven experience in go-to-market, commercial strategy or sales strategy roles within a fast-growing digital or tech company (marketplaces, SaaS, delivery, fintech or similar)
Strong commercial focus, with a track record of owning revenue targets and driving measurable growth
Multi-market experience is a must: you've worked closely with sales teams and sales leadership across multiple markets

Over 95,000 partner salons

At Treatwell we don't just sell software: we help Europe's best salons and spas digitalise their business, grow their revenue and improve the experience they offer their clients.
You'll be the strategic owner of go-to-market for Treatwell across Europe. With a strong commercial mindset and a highly collaborative approach, you'll define how we position, price, package and launch our products, and partner with Sales to turn them into real, measurable revenue.
 You Will Be Responsible For

Commercial performance & optimisation: Track and drive adoption, revenue and margin across markets, using data and customer insight to optimise pricing, packaging and the sales funnel.
Stripe partnership: Manage Treatwell's strategic partnership with Stripe, acting as the senior commercial point of contact and aligning joint go-to-market plans and growth priorities.
 About You
Proven experience in go-to-market, commercial strategy or sales strategy roles within a fast-growing digital or tech company (marketplaces, SaaS, delivery, fintech or similar)
Strong commercial focus, with a track record of owning revenue targets and driving measurable growth

 About Treatwell
 We're a team of 800+ people working every day to transform the beauty industry across Europe. We've built the leading salon management software, connected to Europe's number one marketplace, helping thousands of professionals run and grow their business.
 The Numbers Speak For Themselves
Over 95,000 partner salons

And the best is yet to come. If you want to join an international, innovative and fast-growing company where your work has a real, visible impact... join us!

title: Head of Strategy & Business Operations
description:
Position: Head of Strategy & Business Operations
 Department: B2B and DaaS (JEFB & JETGo)
 Reporting to: Director of B2B, DaaS and Strategic Partnerships
 Location: London
 Hybrid role: 3 days a week from our London office & 2 days working from home
Ready for a challenge?
Then Just Eat Takeaway.com might be the place for you. We’re a leading global online delivery platform, and our vision is to empower everyday convenience.
Whether it’s a Friday-night feast, a post-gym poke bowl, or grabbing some groceries, our tech platform connects tens of millions of customers with hundreds of thousands of restaurant, grocery and convenience partners across the globe.
 About This Role
 Just Eat for Business (Corporate food ordering) and Just Eat Go (Delivery as a Service) are two of our biggest growth opportunities, and both sit under the same Director at JustEat Takeaway.com.
JEFB is expanding in London and into new cities, while DaaS is turning our delivery network into a service other businesses can rely on.
As Head of Strategy and Business Operations, you'll help set and execute the strategy for both businesses, acting as chief of staff to the Director of B2B and DaaS.
You'll bring together strategic planning, OKR setting and cross-functional delivery, and be the link between Commercial and Product & Technology.
You'll put customers at the centre of every decision, work as one team with Marketing, Commercial and Commercial Ops, and help the global team shape a clear future for B2B. You will be expected to join client/partner meetings where relevant to contribute your expertise.
These are some of the key components to the position:
Lead the strategy – help the Director set and execute the strategy for B2B and DaaS, turning business objectives into clear priorities and measurable plans.
Aim high – set, track, and review OKRs, holding teams accountable for delivery while supporting each other to succeed.
Be the Director's right hand – run the operating rhythm, prepare decisions and follow up on actions across the leadership team.
Own the numbers – monitor business performance and recommend interventions to hit targets, and support the commercial ops team with annual planning and budget submissions.
Break down silos – act as the link between Commercial and P&T, turning commercial insight and customer feedback into clear product priorities.
Grow DaaS – build a deep understanding of the industry, competitors and customer needs, working very closely with the Commercial Head of DaaS. 
Step into our customers' shoes – solve client problems with P&T and Operations, turning them into repeatable, scalable offerings and helping new customers onboard well.
Show up for our partners – attend major customer QBRs with strategic context and commercial credibility to protect and grow key partnerships.
Grow B2B – drive profitable growth in London and lead strategic planning for new cities, including market selection, launch approach and operating model.
Think global – work with the global team to shape a coherent B2B strategy, making sure UK priorities fit and UK needs are represented.
AI - we are striving to be an AI first company - this person should be helping to make that the case within B2B and DaaS.
What will you bring to the team?
Strategic thinking, with the ability to turn ambitious goals into clear priorities and execution plans that deliver results.
Experience setting and tracking OKRs or similar frameworks, and holding teams accountable in a supportive way.
Analytical mindset, modelling scenarios to understand commercial models and pricing and to shape long-term strategy, using data and market intelligence to influence investment decisions.
Excellent relationship-building skills, with the credibility to work with senior stakeholders across Commercial, Product & Technology, Marketing and Operations.
The ability to translate customer and commercial insight into product priorities, and new capabilities into commercial opportunity.
A talent for finding creative solutions to client problems and shaping them into scalable, repeatable offerings.
Confident presence in senior forums and customer meetings, with clear, persuasive communication.
Strong organisation and attention to detail, able to run an operating rhythm and juggle multiple priorities at once.
A self-starter attitude, comfortable with change and thriving in fast-paced, high-growth environments.
A positive, proactive approach with a strong work ethic – celebrate team wins, own your results, and be happy to give and receive feedback.
At JET, this is how we play
Our teams forge connections internally and work with some of the best-known brands on the planet, giving us truly international impact in a dynamic environment.
Being the best at what we do isn’t just about delivering on our strategy. It's a competition for something incredibly valuable – our customers' choice. Every time a customer decides where to order, they're picking a side.
At the heart of the JET Customer League are our values and behaviours. They guide every interaction, every decision, every innovation. These are the actions we need to perform consistently and brilliantly, to surpass the competition and earn our customers’ loyalty, again and again.
Fun, fast-paced and supportive, the JET culture is about movement, growth, helping one another to succeed and celebrating wins. By truly living our values and embodying our behaviours, we’re building a customer-first culture which enables us to stay one step ahead of the competition.

title: Manager, Customer Success Technology
location: Edmonton or Toronto or Vancouver or Kitchener-Waterloo
description:
Do you get energized by building the systems and AI-powered workflows that help a Customer Success team deliver exceptional service at scale? 
Then Jobber might be the place for you! We're looking for a Manager, Customer Success Technology to be part of our Success Operations department.
Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!
Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers .
 The team: 
The Success Operations team is the operational backbone of Jobber's Success organization, spanning three connected pillars: operations, technology, and workforce management. Together, the team equips Customer Success with the people, process, systems, and insights they need to make decisions, scale consistently, and deliver against their goals.
 The role: 
Reporting to the Senior Manager, Success Operations, the Manager, Customer Success Technology will own the technology that powers Customer Success teams. This is a hands-on people leader and problem solver who develops technical talent, balances competing priorities, and delivers scalable systems and AI-first solutions.
 The Manager, Customer Success Technology will: 
Manage and develop a team of CS Tech Admins, building their skills and technical effectiveness.
Champion automation and process improvement by identifying manual work to streamline and prioritizing changes that balance speed, experience, accuracy, and maintainability.
Roll out and maintain AI tools and AI-enabled workflows, monitoring their performance and reliability and establishing governance and business continuity plans.
Set the standard for intake, triage, and issue resolution, assessing requests for scope, priority, and business impact and resolving them quickly and effectively.
Establish the KPIs and SLAs for CS Tech and hold the team accountable to clear, measurable outcomes.
Guide the team's delivery, from configuration changes to minor builds to large transformations, in partnership with Success Operations, Engineering, and cross-functional stakeholders.
Support complex technology projects from ideation to launch, surfacing technical risks, balancing business needs against technical constraints, and communicating trade-offs.
Establish and maintain best practices for technical delivery that make the team's work repeatable and scalable.
Own the health, performance, and roadmap of the Customer Success (CS) tech stack, and establish the frameworks and metrics to evaluate its ROI.
Manage vendor relationships and licensing across the CS tech stack, making informed decisions that balance capability and cost.
Build trusted partnerships with Success leaders, translating their needs into a coherent technology roadmap.
 To be successful, you should have: 
Demonstrated people leadership experience, with a track record of developing technical talent and building high-performing teams.
Experience working with or in a Customer Success organization, including a solid understanding of how Product Support and Onboarding teams operate and how technology helps them scale and deliver outcomes.
Extensive experience with customer success tools such as Salesforce Service Cloud, Amazon Connect, Intercom, Assembled, ChiliPiper, Revenue.IO , or similar.
Hands-on experience designing, building, and running AI-enabled workflows and agents, including monitoring their performance and reliability and establishing governance.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate with engineering teams on complex technology programs using Agile and Scrum methodologies, along with project and program best practices, tools, and techniques. Agile training and experience preferred.
Demonstrated ability to build strong cross-functional partnerships.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to turn data into clear, actionable recommendations for technical and non-technical audiences.
The ability to work on multiple projects at once, including establishing new processes and streamlining existing ones.
Comfort with ambiguity and change. We're growing fast, and what worked yesterday might not work today.
A bias toward action, with the judgment to make informed decisions, move work forward, and adapt as new information emerges.
 Compensation: 
At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $120,870, a midpoint of $142,200, and a maximum salary of $163,530 , designed to show the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.
We design our compensation to reflect each new hire's skills, experience against the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual's current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth.
Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You'll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.
We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we're happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!
 Location: 
We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo. 
 What you can expect from Jobber: 
A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.
A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.
A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.
To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.
 We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process. 
 A bit more about us: 
Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

Own CS tech stack health, roadmap and admin delivery

title: Senior Manager, Revenue Operations (Amsterdam)
description:
Senior Manager, Revenue Operations (Europe)
 Location: Hybrid, based from one of our European locations (London, Amsterdam, Oslo, Helsinki, Brussels, Stockholm or Munich), combined with remote working | European remit.
Permanent | Full-Time | Reports to Head of Commercial Operations, Europe.
 Why this role exists
 NEP is the business behind many of the world's biggest live Sports and Entertainment broadcasts. Across Europe we operate in more than a dozen countries, with production crews, mobile units, studios, remote and cloud capabilities, connectivity and software platforms serving broadcasters, streamers, rights holders and event owners.
Europe is building one commercial engine behind all of it. This role makes the numbers behind that engine work: targets, incentives, pricing and discount discipline, bid economics and forecasting. When it works well, sales teams trust their targets, get paid accurately and on time, get faster decisions on their bids, and can see clearly what is driving their performance.
It is a hands-on role with real ownership, sitting at the centre of how Europe sets targets, rewards performance and prices its work.
 What You Will Own
 Targets and incentives
The annual target process with Commercial Finance: the bottom-up view from business units and customers, the split across territories and sellers, and communicating targets clearly to the sales teams 
Running the incentive scheme day to day: crediting who sold what, tracking attainment, and calculating bonuses, commission, SPIFs and multi-year signing bonuses 
The payout list to Finance and payroll, and a monthly targets-to-actuals reconciliation that runs without being rebuilt by hand 
In-year target changes and incentive queries, handled consistently, quickly and fairly 
Checking with Finance that the scheme is driving the behaviour it was designed for, and recommending changes where it is not 
 Pricing, discounting and approvals
The rate card process across business units, kept current and version controlled 
Discount tracking against the agreed guardrails, including the effective discount and concessions beyond equipment such as crew, third-party hire and fees 
Approval compliance: deals routed to the right approver quickly, and exceptions visible and explained, using DealHub approval workflows as they go live 
 Bids and deal economics
Bid economics on larger deals, comparing bid, plan and actual at quote, close and renewal 
IA, RFP and tender support: pricing inputs, IA submissions and reusable tender content 
Post-bid win and loss reviews, so each bid learns from the last 
 Forecasting and performance insight
Forecast rigour: stage discipline, forecast categories and a review with sales leaders ahead of the weekly EU pipeline call 
Commercial analysis and KPI reporting across win rate, conversion, pricing, margin, discount and attainment 
Turning the numbers into clear recommendations that sales teams and leadership act on 
 Who You Will Work With
 You will report to the Head of Commercial Operations, Europe, and work closely with the Sales Support Manager, who leads Salesforce, DealHub adoption, dashboards and the exec pack. Day to day you will work with Commercial Finance on targets, accruals and payouts, with HR on incentive eligibility, with Managing Directors and their sales teams across the UK&I, Netherlands, Nordics and Mid & South Europe, and with the Global Commercial Operations teams.
Local sales teams own their customer relationships and make pricing decisions within the agreed guardrails. Your job is to make sure they have the numbers, controls and support to make those decisions well.
 What Good Looks Like After Twelve Months
Targets are issued on time, built on a model sales leaders understand and accept 
Incentives pay out accurately and on time, with few disputes and quick resolution of the ones that arise 
Every material discount is visible, approved by the right person and reported 
The forecast is more accurate, and the weekly pipeline call runs on numbers nobody needs to re-check 
Win and loss reviews have enhanced pricing and bid approach 
 What We Are Looking For
Experience in revenue operations, sales operations, commercial finance or incentive administration, in a business with complex or high-value sales 
Hands-on experience of target setting and incentive or commission calculations, ideally across more than one country 
Strong Excel and modelling skills, comfort working in Salesforce, and experience with Power BI or similar 
A good grasp of pricing, discount and margin, and the confidence to challenge a number 
Accuracy and control, with the judgement to keep processes simple for sales teams 
Clear communication: able to explain a payout to a salesperson and a trend to leadership 
Helpful but not required: DealHub or other CPQ tools, live production or broadcast experience, and/or incentive plan design 
Fluency in English is required for this role, and proficiency in additional languages is a strong advantage but not essential 
Applications close on 15 November 2026, although we reserve the right to close the advert early if we receive sufficient applications. Interviews are planned for 19 and 20 November 2026, with the successful candidate expected to start in January 2027, although we’re happy to be flexible for the right candidate.

title: Lead Revenue Operations Analyst
description:
Opentext - The Information Company
 OpenText is a global leader in information management, where innovation, creativity, and collaboration are the key components of our corporate culture. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to partner with the most highly regarded companies in the world, tackle complex issues, and contribute to projects that shape the future of digital transformation.
 AI-First. Future-Driven. Human-Centered.
 At OpenText, AI is at the heart of everything we do—powering innovation, transforming work, and empowering digital knowledge workers. We are hiring talent AI can't replace to help us shape the future of information management. Join us.
 YOUR IMPACT
 OpenText is seeking a Lead Revenue Operations Analyst to join our growing Support Revenue Operations team, acting as a key financial partner focused on adding value to the business. This position reports to the Manager, Revenue Operations, and will be responsible for supporting revenue forecasting, bookings analysis, planning, and reporting processes, while acting as a key interface with business leaders and other cross-functional stakeholders to optimize business performance. The successful candidate will be analytical, detail-oriented, and have a high degree of autonomy along with a broad understanding of business and finance. The individual will foster strong working relationships with various internal stakeholders, thrive on process improvements, and manage inputs from multiple sources.
 What The Role Offers
 Provide operational support and analysis to various business teams.
 Support continuous process improvement, automating and streamlining processes for forecasting, reporting, and analysis.
 Build relationships with leaders to improve how estimates and actual financials are consolidated and analyzed.
 Review and prepare weekly forecast and pipeline reports for accuracy and business insight.
 Support ongoing forecasting, planning, budgeting, and reporting.
 Understand what drives forecast changes and explain variances to plan, year-over-year, and quarter-over-quarter and share clear variance analysis with stakeholders and senior management.
 Learn and use new tools to gather data from multiple sources for better reporting.
 Work with internal teams like Revenue Recognition, Billing Operations, Sales Operations, and Business Operations.
 Handle ad-hoc analysis and reporting as needed.
 What You Need To Succeed
 Bachelor's degree (or equivalent experience) in Business Administration, Financial Analysis, Accounting, or a related field.
 5+ years of experience in business analysis, financial analysis, and/or reporting.
Advanced skills in Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Word. Basic SQL knowledge to run queries is a plus.
 Strong analytical skills, with attention to detail and accuracy in handling large amounts of data.
 Ability to build effective working relationships with senior management, business partners, and peers.
 Experience with Power BI, SAP, SAP AO, or Salesforce is an asset.
 Proven ability to compile and analyze data using pivot tables, VLOOKUP, and other advanced formulas.
 Experience reading customer contracts and interpreting revenue recognition schedules and policies.
 Strong problem-solving skills in a fast-changing, ambiguous environment.
 Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present ideas clearly to audiences at all levels, verbally and in writing.
