At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.
Our dedication to remote-first work , and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you’re part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we’re acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.
 . 
 Hiring and how we work 
We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions! 
Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings. 
 . 
 See yourself at Twilio 
Join the team as Twilio’s next Sales Operations, Planning Analyst
 About the Job 
Twilio is seeking a data-driven, strategically minded individual to join our Strategic Operations pillar within Sales, Operations, and Enablement. Reporting directly into the Strategic Operations team, this role sits at the intersection of business strategy, sales planning, and advanced analytics.
You will lead our target-setting process and align customer segmentation with broader GTM organizational objectives. This role goes beyond standard schedule management; you will define our operational "North Star"—ensuring targets are ambitious, achievable, and backed by robust analytical modeling, forecasting, and data infrastructure.
 Responsibilities 
In this role, you’ll:
Lead the annual and semi-annual target-setting cycles for the global sales organization
 Present target proposals, growth opportunities, and complex data insights to senior leadership using clear, data-backed narratives.
Develop and refine the sales customer segmentation model
Extract actionable insights from large, complex datasets using advanced analytical and statistical methods to optimize revenue efficiency.
Work closely with Sales, Finance, Product, Systems, and HR to align operational metrics with overall corporate strategy.
Develop, maintain, and automate dashboards & reporting to track important planning outcomes including target accuracy and territory outcomes
 Qualifications 
Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!
 Required: 
6+ years of combined experience in Strategic Operations, Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, or Data Analytics within a fast-paced technology environment.
Proven track record of leading target-setting cycles and planning frameworks for a GTM organization.

Strong project management skills, including experience managing cross-functional dependencies and scoping requirements.
Deep understanding of core GTM processes & metrics (productivity, pipeline conversion, forecasting).

Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to influence and build effective working relationships with all levels of the organization.
 Location

title: Sales and Sales Operations Lead
description:
About Mira
 Mira is a San Francisco-based hormonal health company hormonal testing for over 300,000 customers. In 2023, we were recognized by Inc. 5000 as America's fastest-growing femtech company.
Mira's breakthrough innovation was creating the market's only FDA-compliant at-home hormone monitor with quantitative testing technology. From the beginning, our mission has been to make hormone data accessible and meaningful - so women can understand their bodies and make confident health decisions at every stage of life, from cycle health and family planning to hormonal imbalances and the menopause transition.
We are committed to improving real health outcomes through personalized insights, cutting-edge technology, and science-backed data—turning hormone information into practical guidance for everyday wellbeing.
 About The Position
 We are looking for a Sales Operations Lead to build the sales process, data infrastructure, and operating rhythm that our fast-growing B2B business has never had. You’ll own the practitioner funnel end to end, from first outreach through retention, and build the systems, team, and processes that scale it. This is a hands-on, build-from-scratch role - you’ll start by working the funnel and speaking with practitioners yourself.
If you want to challenge yourself at a high-growth startup and make a difference for women's health, please join us!
 Responsibilities
 Sales
In the first months, get boots on the ground: work the funnel and speak directly with practitioners yourself
 Funnel Strategy & Analytics
Own the practitioner funnel end to end, from lead handoff through retention, and identify where and why practitioners get stuck
Segment funnel conversion by practitioner avatar to guide ongoing avatar refinement
Build a lead scoring model and the systems to prioritize outreach based on it
Report on funnel performance and deliver a quarterly plan with targets
 Systems & Cross-Functional Alignment
Vet, onboard, and manage the sales and marketing tech stack, including HubSpot pipeline architecture and product usage data integration
Partner with clinical and customer success teams on practitioner handoffs, onboarding milestones, and retention triggers
Build and manage the retention plan, including follow ups, win back outreach, and referral tracking
Lead cross functional projects across sales, marketing, and clinical teams, with clear owners, timelines, and results
 Sales Operations & Enablement
Build the sales process and playbook, and train the team to use it
Own enablement content, including sales scripts and training materials for the team
Design and manage a multi touch outreach cadence across the funnel
Build, manage, and grow the sales team as we scale, including hiring and commission plan design
 Requirements
 Must have
5+ years leading and scaling sales operations, revenue operations, or commercial teams in B2B
Clinical sales experience, ideally with long, relationship driven sales cycles
Clinical background or strong clinical fluency
Startup experience, having built teams and processes from scratch
Strong analytical skills, with a track record of turning data into clear action
Project management experience leading initiatives across multiple teams
Hands on experience with HubSpot or a comparable CRM, plus sales and marketing automation tools
Comfortable using AI tools to speed up analysis, content creation, and workflow automation
 Nice to Have
Sold to integrative or functional medicine practices
Strong hormone specific clinical background
HubSpot certified
PMP certification
 Details
 The role is a remote position, with a 40-hour workweek, flexible working hours and meaningful overlap with the US team (a US/Americas timezone is strongly preferred).
 What We Offer
Join one of the fastest-growing femtech companies in the U.S., driven by a strong mission to advance women's health and expand access to care
Be the first person to own sales operations for one of Mira's fastest-growing revenue lines, with real influence over process, comp design, and forecasting from day one
Be part of a passionate, highly motivated, and international team dedicated to making a real difference in people's lives
Thrive in a fast-paced startup environment where your work directly impacts company growth, strategy, and key decisions
Enjoy real opportunities for career growth, with the ability to shape, build, and develop teams as we scale
Work in a flexible, fully remote environment that supports autonomy, ownership, and independence
Receive a competitive salary along with a performance-based bonus system tied to OKRs

Amphenol Communications Solutions (ACS), a division of Amphenol Corporation, is a world leader in interconnect solutions for Communications, Mobile, RF, Optics, and Commercial electronics markets. Amphenol Corporation is one of the world’s largest designers and manufacturers of electrical, electronic and fiber optic connectors and interconnect systems, antennas, sensors and sensor-based products and coaxial and high-speed specialty cable. The **Assistant Sales Operation Manager** for Amphenol Highspeed IO business unit supports the Sales Operation team in executing marketing and business strategies, driving customer satisfaction, and supporting the development of key customer accounts. This position plays a dual role as both **a customer advocate**s the voice of the customer within the organization—and a representative of **Amphenol’s brand** externally, ensuring exceptional service and communication.
The role involves assisting in strategic planning, coordinating account management activities, managing customer demand, analyzing and presenting forecast and market data, and supporting process improvements that enhance business performance. The ideal candidate is outgoing, detail-oriented, highly organized, and thrives in a dynamic, time-sensitive environment.

* **Effective Communicator:** Communicates clearly and confidently, both verbally and in writing, with diverse audiences.
* **Customer Centric:** Acts as a strong advocate for customer needs, building lasting relationships and ensuring satisfaction.
* **Analytical:** Comfortable interpreting and presenting data to support decisions and drive improvements.
* **Collaborative:** Works effectively across sales, operations, finance, and product teams to achieve shared goals.
* **Team-Oriented Leader:** Motivates and supports team members, fostering a culture of accountability and growth.

* Track and report performance metrics, progress against objectives, and customer feedback. Provide actionable insights and support leadership in achieving annual marketing and revenue goals.

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related field.

* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage effectively with customers and stakeholders at all levels.
* Proficiency in demand planning tools, CRM systems, and excel.
* Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret complex data and provide strategic insights.
* Ability to work collaboratively across departments and manage cross-functional projects.
* Ability to travel up to 20% to meet with customers and teams across different locations.
**CORE COMPETENCIES**
* **Customer Focus:** Demonstrates a strong commitment to meeting customer needs and enhancing customer experience.
* **Analytical Skills:** Strong data analysis skills to interpret demand trends and adjust strategies accordingly.
* **Leadership:** Capable of building, mentoring, and leading a high-performing team in a dynamic environment.
* **Communication:** Excellent verbal and written communication skills, able to convey complex information clearly to both internal teams and customers.
* **Initiative:** Takes ownership of tasks and drives results proactively

title: Director, Sales Enablement
description:
***Please note:*** Our Talent team at Jobber will be offline for Jobber Impact - our flagship event of the year, bringing Jobberinos together to connect, learn, and celebrate what we're building - starting October 6th and extending until October 9th. We’ll be back to go through applications and reach out with an update on your candidacy once we return next week!
* This will be updated automatically on all job posts above our ***What you can expect from Jobber*** headline.
* The automated email to candidates will have the same message as above.
**Do you believe enablement should be measured in ramp speed and revenue, not completion rates?**
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Then Jobber might be the place for you! We’re looking for a **Director, Sales Enablement** to be part of our **Sales Enablement & Operations** department.
Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!
Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500 lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers.
**The team:**
Sales Enablement & Operations exists to make sure Jobber’s go-to-market org never has to choose between moving quickly and being ready. We build the systems, tools, and people development that turn strategy into execution: how we forecast and plan, how we pay and motivate, how our tech stack works for reps instead of against them, and how every seller gets better at their craft. The team is organized into peer pillars: Sales Operations, Revenue Technology, Sales Planning & Operations, and Enablement Programs.
**The role:**
Reporting to the Sr. Director, Sales Enablement & Operations, the **Director, Sales Enablement** will lead Enablement Programs and make sure every seller at Jobber has what they need to win: the skills, the confidence, and the readiness to perform from day one and through every new launch. You’ll lead a team of five to six, as a peer to the leads of Sales Operations, Revenue Technology, and Sales Planning & Operations. You’re accountable for outcomes, not activity — whether reps are actually ready, whether launches actually land in the field, and whether the enablement investment shows up in ramp speed, pipeline, and revenue.
**The Director, Sales Enablement will:**
* Set the strategy for onboarding, training, certification, and coaching across the sales org, and build, manage, and upskill a team of enablement managers and practitioners.
* Own ramp programs and certification standards across go-to-market roles, and hold the bar on what “certified and ready” actually means.
* Lead enablement for new product, pricing, and process launches, building workback plans that trace every training, content, and certification milestone back from the launch date.
* Build structured, repeatable playbooks and coaching frameworks, and keep them current as products, segments, and motions change.
* Bring AI into how the team builds and delivers enablement — content creation, coaching feedback loops, practice and roleplay, knowledge access — and into what reps are taught to use in their own workflow.
* Partner with Product, Product Marketing, Sales leadership, and Customer Success so enablement priorities match what the business needs next, and launches land with sales rather than at sales.
* Define success beyond completion rates, and report on ramp time, certification pass rates, and downstream impact on pipeline and revenue.
**To be successful, you should have:**
* Extensive experience in sales enablement, revenue operations, or sales leadership, including building and running onboarding, training, or certification programs at scale.
* Demonstrated people leadership experience, including managing managers, and a track record of developing your own team’s skills alongside the field’s.
* A proven track record of leading enablement for product or pricing launches in a B2B SaaS environment, with workback plans that hold up against a real launch timeline.
* Hands-on fluency with AI tools in enablement work itself: content generation, coaching and roleplay, and knowledge management.
* Experience building structured, scalable learning frameworks rather than one-off training events.
* Strong stakeholder management with director-level and senior partners across Product, Marketing, and Sales leadership, and the ability to influence roadmap and go-to-market timing rather than only execute against it.
* Comfort operating with ambiguity and building infrastructure where none exists yet.
* Sharp written and verbal communication.
* A bias toward outcomes over activity, and the judgment to know the difference.
**Compensation:**
At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $181,400, a midpoint of $213,500, and a maximum salary of $245,500, designed to show the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.
We design our compensation to reflect each new hire’s skills, experience against the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual’s current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth.
Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You’ll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.
We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we’re happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!
**Location:**
We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: **Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo.**
**What you can expect from Jobber:**
* A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.
* A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.
* A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.
* To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh\*t about our customers.
*We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process.*
**A bit more about us:**
Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

title: Lead, Go to Market Intelligence
description:
The Opportunity
Euna Solutions is hiring a Lead, Go to Market Intelligence, to own the account and contact intelligence layer that tells our sellers which public sector agencies to pursue and when. This covers the quality of the account and contact database, the Intent-to-Buy and Propensity-to-Buy scoring models, ICP and segmentation, and competitive intelligence. The role is hands-on technical: you will write SQL and Python daily, build and validate predictive models against closed outcomes, and own the analytical pipelines that turn raw public sector signal into ranked target lists.
What You'll Do
Account and Contact Data Foundation
Own account and contact data standards for prospect and target accounts, including completeness, accuracy, and coverage benchmarks by segment and territory
Monitor data hygiene on a published cadence and drive remediation with GTM Systems rather than reporting the problem and stopping
Define enrichment requirements for accounts and contacts, and manage vendor selection, ingestion logic, and refresh cadence across our data sources
Intent-to-Buy and Propensity-to-Buy Scoring
Own the design, feature engineering, and ongoing refinement of the Intent-to-Buy and Propensity-to-Buy scoring models across solutions and segments, selecting the modeling approach (weighted heuristics, logistic regression, tree-based machine learning classifiers) that the data volume and signal quality actually support
Validate model performance against closed outcomes using holdout testing and backtesting: measure lift, precision and recall by score band, and calibration of predicted versus actual conversion, and publish the results
Recalibrate the models on evidence, version the model logic and feature definitions in code, and document what changed, why, and what effect it had on predictive performance
Bring in public sector signal sources, including procurement and budget activity, grant awards, and audit and compliance data, and test each candidate feature for predictive contribution before it enters the model
ICP, Segmentation, and Targeting
Analyze win rate, sales cycle, churn, and expansion patterns by segment, vertical, and solution using cohort and regression analysis to sharpen the ideal customer profile, distinguishing signal from segment mix effects
Translate ICP findings into targeting rules the field can execute against, not just a slide
Support territory design with account-level intelligence on where the addressable opportunity actually sits
Competitive and Market Intelligence
Own competitive intelligence: who we win against, who we lose to, in which segments and solutions, and what the pattern in the loss reasons is telling us
Own our FOIA and public records strategy as an intelligence source, and convert findings into structured commercial insight
Maintain competitive positioning inputs that Sales and Marketing can use in live deals
Activation with the Field
Partner with Sales, BD, and Marketing to operationalize scoring and segmentation into territory views, prioritized target lists, and outbound workflows
Collect field feedback on scoring and targeting quality, and treat it as data rather than noise
What You Bring
You have 4+ years in go-to-market analytics, revenue operations, market intelligence, or a comparable analytical function
Hands-on experience building and validating an account scoring, lead scoring, or propensity model end to end: feature selection, model choice, holdout or back test validation, and measured performance against real outcomes
Strong SQL, including joins across large multi-table datasets and window functions, and working proficiency in Python for data analysis and modeling (pandas, scikit-learn or equivalent)
 Nice-to-Have Qualifications
Public sector or GovTech market exposure, and familiarity with public procurement and budget data
Experience with enrichment or intent data vendors, and with managing a vendor relationship
Applied statistics and machine learning grounding: regression and classification methods, evaluation metrics (precision, recall, lift, AUC), and the judgment to know when a simpler model wins
Experience with cloud data warehouse environments (Athena, Redshift, Snowflake) and transformation tooling, plus Tableau, Power BI, or Looker for delivery
Hands-on use of LLM-based tooling for enrichment, classification, or unstructured data extraction (e.g., mining call transcripts or public records at scale)
Location
This position will be hybrid with 3 days/week in our Oakville, ON office.
Travel required approximately two to four times per year for planning cycles and sales kickoff.
Compensation Range: $110-137,500K
We believe in openness, so we publish our range from the start. Where an offer will land depends on your background, strengths, and how you'll contribute to the work ahead.

We're looking for people who are curious about emerging technologies, eager to experiment, and committed to using AI responsibly to augment, not replace, their expertise.

 Here's What That Actually Looks Like

title: Head of Revenue Operations

Fintech | London | 4 days per week in London office | c.£120,000 + bonus
A high-growth fintech business is looking for a Head of Revenue Operations to take ownership of its global RevOps function and help build the commercial operating infrastructure for its next stage of growth.
This is a senior, hands-on leadership role. You’ll inherit an established RevOps function and a team of specialists across GTM systems, sales operations and GTM engineering, with responsibility for bringing the different parts together into a cohesive global function.
The business has recently evolved its commercial structure across the UK, Europe and US, creating a significant opportunity for RevOps to become a genuinely global enabling function across the organisation.
 The role 
You’ll report into the senior leadership team responsible for Strategy, Planning and RevOps, and will own the day-to-day leadership of the function.
Your remit will span:
Revenue Operations strategy, process and execution across multiple regions
Leading and developing a team of around 4-5 across RevOps, GTM engineering and commercial systems
Ownership of the commercial systems environment, including Salesforce
Improving pipeline management, forecasting, reporting and GTM performance
Building a consistent operating model across regional commercial teams
Turning commercial data into actionable insight for senior leadership
Identifying inefficiencies and opportunities for automation
Partnering closely with Sales, Account Management, Finance, Technology, Data and Strategy
Challenging existing processes and introducing better ways of working
Developing the foundations for a more AI-enabled and increasingly automated RevOps function
This isn't a role where you'll simply manage a team and review dashboards.
You'll need to be comfortable getting into the detail when required: understanding the data, interrogating systems, building reporting, improving processes and working alongside technical teams to actually make things happen.
 What we're looking for 
We're interested in people who have a strong grounding in Revenue Operations and have progressed beyond simply being the person who keeps the CRM running.
You'll likely have:
Significant experience across Revenue Operations / Sales Operations / Commercial Operations
Experience operating in a B2B SaaS, fintech or similarly complex technology environment
Experience managing and developing a RevOps or commercial operations team
Strong Salesforce and commercial systems knowledge
A strong understanding of pipeline, forecasting, funnel performance and GTM metrics
The ability to move comfortably between strategy and execution
Strong analytical ability and an instinct for finding insights within commercial data
Experience working with senior commercial stakeholders
A genuine interest in AI, automation and the future of GTM operations
We're not looking for someone who has already spent years building fully autonomous or "agentic" RevOps functions.
The technology is evolving too quickly for that to be a realistic prerequisite.
Instead, we're looking for someone with excellent RevOps fundamentals, strong commercial judgement and the curiosity to experiment with what comes next. 
 Why this role? 
This is an opportunity to join a business where RevOps sits at the centre of how the commercial organisation operates globally.
 You'll have: 
 Global scope 
Work across UK, European and US commercial teams while owning consistency of process, data, systems and reporting globally.
 A team to lead 
You'll inherit a capable team spanning GTM engineering, commercial systems and Sales Ops rather than having to build everything from scratch.
 Real ownership 
You'll have the autonomy to shape how RevOps operates, rather than simply maintaining an existing playbook.
 Technology and AI 
The business is actively exploring how AI and automation can improve GTM operations. You'll have the opportunity to experiment, test and ultimately embed those capabilities where they create genuine value.
 Executive exposure

title: Salesforce & RevOps Systems Administrator
description:
Job description
 Amilia is transforming the recreation and activities market with its innovative, purpose-built SaaS platform. Designed for municipalities, community centers, nonprofits, businesses, and recreation organizations, Amilia SmartRec™ streamlines operations, optimizes facility management, and simplifies program and membership management. 
 Since 2009, Amilia has been on a mission to revolutionize how communities connect and participate in activities. By combining cutting-edge technology with deep industry expertise, the software empowers organizations to manage registrations, memberships, facilities, and finances more efficiently while enhancing community engagement. 
 Over 1,500 organizations across 6,600 locations in North America rely on Amilia to serve 4.5 million participants and process $750M in transactions annually. 
 Caring is at the core of Amilia’s culture: for customers, tailored products, and colleagues alike. Driven by an entrepreneurial spirit and a passion for innovation, this mindset shapes everything we do. 
 Revenue Operations is a newly built function at Amilia, reporting to the COO, responsible for connecting Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Finance into one operating system across the customer journey. Salesforce is our system of record, and RevOps owns every tool that touches it. 
 What you can expect: 
 This is the first dedicated systems and tools hire inside RevOps. Reporting directly to the Director of Revenue Operations, you'll own the tools the GTM team runs on, and make them actually work: configuring the objects, building the flows, wiring the integrations, fixing the data, and using AI-assisted development to move faster than a traditional admin queue allows. 
 Claude and Claude Code are already how this team builds, and you'll be expected to work the same way, not layer AI on as an afterthought. 
 You'll also help shape a function that's still being built: a RevOps team that already works AI-natively, with the tooling and the mandate to use it, not just permission to ask. It's a category-leading vertical-SaaS environment with real technical depth in the systems you'd be running. 
 You will be responsible for: 
 Salesforce Administration 
 Declarative configuration: flows, validation rules, page layouts, permission sets, profiles, reports, and dashboards. 
 User and license management, security review, and the field-level hygiene that keeps Salesforce trustworthy as the system of record. 
 Triage and close out the standing data-quality and config backlog (duplicate records, broken flows, permission gaps, stale automation), work currently split between the Director and an external agency. 
 Partner with the Director on architectural decisions such as object-model changes and taxonomy rebuilds, and own the build, not just the ticket queue. 
 Marketing & GTM Tooling 
 Administer the martech stack RevOps is responsible for: HubSpot (workflows, lead scoring, campaign operations), Chili Piper (lead routing), Propensity (ABM), Fathom, RocketLane, CLM/quoting tools, and the sales-engagement and cadence tooling inside Salesforce. 
 Keep every tool's integration back to Salesforce clean. Salesforce is the hub, so nothing you administer should create a parallel data store. 
 Support tool evaluation and pilots: set up trials, define what “pass” looks like, and carry a pilot into permanent operation once it earns its place in the stack. 
 Data & Reporting Infrastructure 
 Own the connective tissue between Salesforce, the marketing stack, and the reporting layer: keeping syncs, exports, and integrations running, and diagnosing them fast with the analytics engineer when they break. 
 Build, maintain, and simplify the Salesforce reports, dashboards, and light data pipelines RevOps and its stakeholders depend on day to day, and support the shift to our “source of truth” cloud data-lake reporting system as we build it out in 2027. 
 Work alongside the data/analytics function on schema and warehouse questions without owning deep analytics engineering. This is the operational admin seat, not the data-architect seat. 
 AI-Native Systems Work 
 Use Claude and Claude Code as a standard part of how you build and maintain configuration: SFDX metadata changes, bulk data fixes, scripted QA, and automation that a point-and-click admin workflow would make too slow or too manual to attempt. 
 Bring judgment about what to automate and what not to. AI makes bad changes cheap to ship, so config changes still get scoped, tested, and reviewed like engineering work, not shipped straight to production. 
Job requirements
 What we want from you: 
 2 to 4 years of hands-on Salesforce administration (Sales Cloud). Salesforce Administrator certification preferred, not required. 
 Hands-on, shippable experience with at least one AI coding/automation tool (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, or similar) as a real part of your workflow today. This is a must-have, not a nice-to-have, and you can point to something you've actually shipped with one. 
 Experience administering at least one marketing automation or sales-engagement platform (HubSpot, Marketo, Salesloft, Pardot, or similar). 
 Comfortable writing basic SQL for data checks and light scripting for automation. 
 You've administered Salesforce for real users in production, not a sandbox project, and you know the line between what's safe to build declaratively and what needs escalation. 
 You default to fixing the data and the configuration, not building a report on top of the problem. 
 You're comfortable inheriting and prioritizing your own backlog; this role starts with significant standing technical debt, not a clean system. 
 You ask "does this write back to Salesforce cleanly?" before you ask "does this tool look nice?" 
 Bonus: exposure to a CPQ/quoting tool, a contract lifecycle management (CLM) tool, or a data warehouse/BI layer. 
 What you will get from us: 
 A competitive and progressive salary; 
 A group RRSP employer contribution up to 5%; 
 A group insurance for you and your family as well as an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and telemedicine; 
 A $750 wellness allowance per year; 
 The possibility of working in the office or at home, and up to 3 months abroad per year (conditions apply); 
 A strong work-life balance: flexible hours, 4 weeks' vacation and 8 sick days yearly, and year-round mini-Fridays; 
 Skill development opportunities through engaging workshops, communities of practice, trainings, access to Udemy and opportunities to attend conferences; 
 Companywide and team bonding activities to connect with your peers throughout the year and social activities to connect with your peers; 
 Weekly Bootcamp and Pilates classes for Amilians; 
 25% discount on annual membership for STM and EXO; 
 In-office snacks, including fresh fruit baskets, coffee, beverages, and free drinks. 
 Amilia is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity and encourages applications from women, members of visible minorities and ethnic groups, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, or any other status protected by the laws or regulations of the Province of Quebec. Amilia is committed to providing a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. Amilia’s strength lies in the sum of the ideas and innovations shared by its diverse and inclusive teams.

Administering integrations and a martech stack including CLM/quoting tools

title: Senior Manager, Commercial Operations, Northern European Cluster
location: Uxbridge or Lysaker or Solna or Copenhagen or Helsinki
description:
At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.
 The Opportunity 
Behind every high-performing commercial organisation is an engine that keeps everything running — the systems, the data, the processes, and the infrastructure that allow field teams to do their best work. This is that role.
As Commercial Operations Manager for the Northern Cluster, you will sit at the heart of a commercial organisation spanning the UK, Ireland, and the Nordic markets — Denmark, Sweden, Norway, and Finland. You will own the tools, systems, and data infrastructure that power our field teams, manage Sales Incentive Plans, lead territory design, and serve as the operational backbone of a complex, multi-market business.
This is not a passive support function. It is a critical enabling role that bridges strategy and execution — and the right person will bring genuine ambition to it. If you thrive on bringing order to complexity, take pride in operational precision, and are always asking how things can be done better, this role was built for you.
This role will be managing the Northern European Cluster, comprising of UK, Ireland and the Nordics and may require some travelling within the cluster.
 What You Will Be Doing 
 Commercial Excellence — Tools and Systems Ownership 
You will be the primary owner and single point of contact for key commercial tools and systems across the Northern Cluster — including Veeva CRM, our data lake and reporting platforms. That means ensuring optimal functionality, driving user adoption, maintaining data quality, and acting as the internal champion for these systems. You will lead onboarding of new tools, manage UAT, upload bi-annual Cycle Plans, and ensure global standards translate into locally reliable execution.
 Reporting, Dashboards, and Analytics 
You will build and maintain dashboards and reports — including Power BI — that give sales leaders and field teams clear, accessible visibility of performance and territory execution. You will deliver ad-hoc analyses, contribute to insight generation in partnership with cluster BI&A, and continuously improve data integration across systems. The goal is always the same: better information, faster decisions, stronger outcomes.
 Sales Incentive Scheme Design and Administration 
You will manage the end-to-end execution of Sales Incentive Plans twice a year — from data preparation and calculations through to pay-out — working in close partnership with HR and Finance. You will also partner with Business Unit leads to design and optimise incentive schemes that are motivating, commercially aligned, equitable, and audit-ready. This is high-stakes work that demands both analytical rigour and commercial instinct.
 Territory Planning and Field Support 
You will perform territory design and alignment across all brands and markets, lead territory change management end-to-end, and ensure field teams always have the accurate, up-to-date tools and data they need to operate effectively. You will maintain a continuous improvement mindset — regularly reviewing processes to identify where things can be streamlined and enhanced.
 Data Governance and Cluster Interfaces 
You will ensure data standards are set and maintained across commercial programmes, maintain local Business Rules in connection with commercial, medical, and compliance functions, and work with external data vendors such as IQVIA to ensure data quality and availability. You will represent operational realities in cluster and global forums — making sure the ground-level picture is always understood at the top.
 Process Optimisation and Ways of Working 
You will champion a culture of operational excellence across the Strategy and Operations function — proactively identifying gaps, inefficiencies, and duplication, and developing practical solutions that improve speed, accuracy, and impact. You will document and embed standardised ways of working that are consistent, scalable, and built to last.
 What We Are Looking For 
 Essential 
5 or more years of experience in the healthcare or pharmaceutical industry, with a demonstrable track record in commercial operations, commercial excellence, or a closely related function
Advanced, hands-on command of Veeva CRM or an equivalent life sciences CRM platform
Strong analytical skills — comfortable with large, complex data sets and hands-on with BI tooling such as Power BI, as well as advanced Microsoft Excel
Exceptional organisational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously without losing sight of the bigger picture
Confident operating in a highly matrixed environment, influencing upwards and across the organisation without formal authority
A proactive, self-directed mindset with a natural instinct to anticipate problems before they arise
Strong communication skills — able to translate technical and operational detail into clear, accessible language for diverse audiences
Excellent written and spoken English; a Nordic language is a distinct advantage for candidates based in the Nordics
 Preferred 
Prior involvement in Sales Incentive Plan administration or territory management within pharma or life sciences
Experience with Veeva, PowerBI and Data lakes 
Experience orchestrating complex processes across multiple countries or markets; familiarity with the Nordic context is a strong plus
A commercial, data & analytics or management consulting background
Familiarity with omnichannel strategy and connected tooling
Project management experience or relevant certification such as Prince2 or PMP
Postgraduate qualification in Business, Data Analytics, Information Systems, or a related field
 What Makes Someone Successful Here 
You are the kind of person who sees a broken process and cannot leave it alone until it is fixed. You think end-to-end — understanding dependencies, anticipating risks, and following through. You are equally comfortable in a data set and in a stakeholder meeting, and you know how to translate the operational detail into language that lands with a commercial audience.
You will be working across Oncology, Cardiovascular, and CAR-T/Haematology therapy areas, partnering with Field Force Excellence, Sales, HR, Finance, and cluster Commercial Operations teams across multiple markets. It is a broad, highly visible remit — and for someone who genuinely loves operational excellence, it is a compelling one.

We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway.
 How We Work 
Where you work matters – because collaboration, innovation and patient impact happen in many settings. title: Director of Revenue Operations
description:
About Otodata 
Otodata is the leading provider of remote tank monitoring (RTM) for the propane and LPG industry, with an installed base spanning North America, Europe, Latin America and Israel. Our devices and software platform give distributors real-time tank levels, route optimisation and delivery efficiency, and we are extending the same platform into adjacent verticals including fuels and lubricants, used cooking oil, industrial gas, ice box and metering.
Otodata is backed by GI Partners and is executing a value creation plan to double revenue by 2030 and shifting the mix towards recurring hardware-as-a-service (HaaS) and telemetry-as-a-service (TMaaS) models. We design and manufacture our devices in Montreal and sell through a direct sales team in North America, in-country teams in Europe and Latin America, and selected channel partners.
 The opportunity 
Otodata has grown to its current scale on the strength of its product and deep customer relationships. The next phase of growth takes us into more markets, more verticals and more selling motions at once: deeper penetration of our core, new adjacent verticals, country-by-country expansion in Europe and new-market entry in Latin America.
The Director of Revenue Operations will scale the infrastructure that enables this including a single CRM foundation for every region, disciplined forecasting and pipeline management, account prioritisation and territory design, quota and compensation mechanics, and the reporting that lets leadership see and steer the business in real time.
This is a hands-on build role with high visibility to the CEO, CRO and CFO.
 Role overview 
The Director of Revenue Operations owns the systems, processes, data and analytics behind Otodata's commercial engine across all regions and verticals. The role sits within Finance and works day to day with the CRO and the regional sales leaders as the operating partner to the front line.
Scope spans forecasting, pipeline management, Salesforce and the sales technology stack, account prioritisation, quota and compensation administration, sales enablement analytics, and commercial reporting to the executive team and Board. The role inherits the Sales Analytics team and will shape the RevOps organisation as the business scales.
 Key responsibilities 
 Forecasting, pipeline and deal intelligence 
Own the revenue forecasting model and process end to end, with customer, product, vertical and month-level granularity, and deliver forecast accuracy within ±5%.
Define and enforce opportunity stage definitions, entry and exit criteria and deal-stage acceptance criteria for enterprise and strategic pursuits
Run a consistent pipeline inspection cadence with the CRO and regional leaders that drives specific actions on coverage, stage ageing and at-risk deals.
Build the measures the GTM plan depends on: win rate, cycle time, demo-to-close rate, installed-base penetration by account, CAC and payback by vertical and country.
 Salesforce, sales systems and commercial reporting 
Lead the Salesforce territory, forecast and commercial reporting build-out in partnership with IT.
Own CRM configuration, data hygiene and adoption across the commercial organisation, and integrate commission, contract and device data alongside pipeline data.
Build and maintain executive dashboards for ARR, unit activations, ARPU by vertical and country, gross and net retention, HaaS and TMaaS conversion and pipeline coverage
Own the monthly commercial update and the GTM section of the quarterly Board deck, with consistent definitions and commentary.
 Account prioritisation, coverage and territory design 
Maintain the account tiering and refresh cadence, using penetration headroom and share of wallet estimates.
Design territories and coverage ratios by tier, region and vertical, and model the scale triggers (ARR, accounts or pipeline per rep)
Run capacity modelling and the hiring sequence implied by the GTM design, working with CRO, Finance and HR.
 Quota, compensation and planning 
In partnership with Finance and HR, design and administer sales compensation plans with clear crediting rules for named accounts, overlays, specialists and channel partners
Own quota setting and planning, aligned to ARR growth, net retention and ARPU expansion.
Partner with Finance on the annual budget, the 12-month rolling forecast and segment-level P&Ls
 Value realisation and sales enablement 
Own the standard customer economics model at target penetration for every Tier A account
Surface specific opportunity areas from pipeline, performance and installed-base insights, by vertical, segment and country, and translate them into recommended commercial actions.
Define the health score and early-warning signals from device and billing data that drive renewal management and expansion.
Enforce pricing governance and the discount approval framework on new and renewing contracts, working with Finance to report HaaS and TMaaS unit economics by model and cohort.
 GTM governance and cross-functional leadership 
Act as secretariat to the monthly GTM SteerCo: track decisions, owners and dates
Bring gravitas to the weekly sales reviews: challenge forecasts that are not supported by pipeline data, hold sellers to the stage and exit criteria, and coach them on how to work within the process rather than simply policing it.
Define the rules of engagement between account managers, customer success, solutions engineers, adjacency specialists and partners.
Partner with Manufacturing and Supply Chain so that device production, shipping and activation support the commercial forecast
Support commercial due diligence and GTM integration playbooks for tuck-in acquisitions.
Build and lead the Revenue Operations team, starting with Sales Analytics.
 Candidate profile 
 Required 
8 to 12 years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations or commercial finance, including at least 3 years leading a RevOps or Sales Ops function in a B2B business with recurring revenue (subscription, HaaS, usage-based or similar).
Experience building and managing forecast, pipeline and CRM discipline in a business
Experience with multi-region, multi-segment sales organisations: direct field teams, inside sales, overlay specialists and channel or distributor partners, ideally including international markets.
Demonstrated strength in forecasting and pipeline analytics, stage and exit criteria design, quota design, and sales compensation design and administration.
Hands-on Salesforce expertise, including configuration, territory management and forecasting
Comfortable with hardware and installed-base economics: units, ARPU, activations, retention and cost to serve, not just bookings.
Excellent executive communicator and cross-functional collaborator who can hold the line on data integrity with senior sales leaders while remaining a trusted partner to them.
 Preferred 
Industrial IoT, telematics, energy distribution (propane, LPG, fuels) or field-services industries.
Experience in a private equity-backed or similarly high-accountability environment, with exposure to Board-level reporting.
Building a standard value or ROI model used by the sales team with executive buyers.
Commercial diligence or GTM integration on acquisitions.
Working knowledge of French.
 Core competencies and attributes 
 Builder mindset: energised by creating structure and willing to do the detailed work
 Data integrity under pressure: keeps definitions consistent and the forecast honest and is comfortable being the independent voice between Sales and Finance.
 Gravitas and conviction: Confidence to hold their ground with experienced sales leaders while keeping that relationship strong and constructive.
 Commercial judgement: understands how sellers actually work and designs process that helps them sell more, not process for its own sake.
 Analytical rigour: turns device, billing, commission and CRM data into decisions on coverage, pricing and investment.
 Influence without authority: earns the trust of regional leaders in Montreal, the US, Europe and Latin America who do not report to the role, and coaches sellers towards compliance with the process rather than simply enforcing it.
 Pace and pragmatism: sequences the build so that the commercial team sees value quickly, rather than waiting for a perfect system.
 Ownership culture: accountable for outcomes, transparent on misses and proactive in surfacing issues before they reach the CEO or Board.
Location, compensation and how to apply
The role is based at Otodata's headquarters in Montreal with a hybrid working arrangement with periodic travel. Candidates must be able to work in Canada.

title: Director Go-to-Market and Revenue Strategy
description:
Who We Are
 You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.
We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.
Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.
Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.
Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.
 Who You Are
 You are a commercial leader who has built the go-to-market of a platform from a blank page and knows what it takes to turn a product that people already use into a business that pays for itself. You have priced and packaged products for marketplaces, brands or merchants, and you have seen the difference between a model that looks good in a spreadsheet and one that a small business owner actually adopts.
You are comfortable in a B2B2C world: the customer is reached through someone else's channel, the data belongs to the ecosystem, and the money comes from several ends of a transaction at once. You influence without authority, because the teams that execute will rarely report to you. You are rigorous with numbers and plain with people, and you are at ease saying what the evidence shows even when the room expects something else.
You want to build something that reaches millions of small businesses, you are prepared to work for it.
 THE OPPORTUNITY
 Toqan for Partners is the AI assistant for the merchants across the companies of the Prosus ecosystem: restaurants, pharmacies, hotels, sellers, real estate agencies and car dealers, five million businesses in total. It launched to restaurants on iFood in Brazil in September 2026 and reached 65,000 restaurants in four weeks with no media spend.
The next twelve months decide how it will become a business: which applications partners pay for and at what price, how value is shared with everyone the partner transacts with, how the uplift is measured and published so the next company embeds, and how the product travels from iFood to the rest of the ecosystem and to India and Europe. You will lead that work, as the owner of the go-to-market and the revenue strategy of Toqan for Partners, alongside the product and technology leads who own what gets built.
 What You’ll Do
 Own the commercial model
 Define pricing and packaging for the applications partners pay for, media management, supply, finance and operations, at a fraction of what they spend today and justified by the return they see. Design how Toqan takes part in the value it creates for the other end: take rate on agent-negotiated supply, credit origination, brand and industry media, and cross-sell of the ecosystem companies' own products. Set the rules that keep it honest, starting with the separation between paid placement and recommendation.
 Drive the rollout across the ecosystem
 With the Head of Operations, secure the commitment of each business in the ecosystem: sponsor, distribution, conditional yes and first market. Run the rollout inside each one, working through the teams that own the merchant relationship, and bring the product to its next verticals and markets.
 Build the measurement
 Own the scoreboard: active partners under a strict definition, uplift per business in retention and GMV, cost and value per active partner. Make the uplift the argument that brings the next company in and the evidence behind every pricing decision.
 Structure the partnerships that carry the revenue
 Lead the commercial agreements with distributors, industry, fintechs and the ecosystem companies' commercial platforms, from first conversation to signed terms, and the co-investment models that align their incentives with the partner's.
 Build and lead the team
 Hire and develop a small go-to-market and revenue team, growth on the merchant side, monetisation and analytics, and set its standard for rigour, ownership and candour.
 What You Bring
Ten or more years in go-to-market, revenue or commercial strategy, with at least one commercial function built from scratch and grown to scale.
Hands-on experience with pricing and packaging, ideally for marketplaces, retail media, payments or SaaS sold to small businesses.
Experience on more than one side of a marketplace: merchants or sellers, brands or suppliers, the platform itself.
A track record of adoption at scale with a long tail of small customers, not only of large enterprise deals.
Proven ability to move a result through teams that do not report to you, and to work inside another company's channel.
Fluency with data: you build the business case, run the analysis and read the uplift yourself, and use AI tooling as a normal part of how you work.
Candour, humility and patience: you say what the numbers say, you arrive to learn before you teach.
English required; Portuguese or Spanish strongly preferred.
 What We Offer
Global impact: a product that reaches five million small businesses across Latin America, Europe and India.
Ownership: the commercial model of a new business, with the numbers to be judged on and the autonomy to build it.
Growth: exposure to the leadership of the group and of its companies, and a clear path into operating roles in the ecosystem.
Competitive compensation and the Prosus benefits package for the location of the role.
 Why Prosus?
 At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.
 Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing.
 Curious about our perks and benefits? Take a look at this page .
 Our Diversity & Inclusion Commitment
 We respect the dignity and human rights of individuals and communities wherever we operate in the world. Building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome and can thrive is critical for us. We provide access to education, which helps everyone understand the important role they play and the positive impact they can have.
 Want to know more about life at Prosus? Explore our culture and values .

title: Senior GTM Operations Manager
description:
About Strava
 Strava is the app for active people. With over 200 million athletes in more than 185 countries, it’s more than tracking workouts—it’s where people make progress together, from new habits to new personal bests. No matter your sport or how you track it, Strava’s got you covered. Find your crew, crush your goals, and make every effort count. Start your journey with Strava today.
Our mission is simple: to motivate people to live their best active lives. We believe in the power of movement to connect and drive people forward.
 About The Role
 Strava for Business is scaling quickly across markets, products and commercial capabilities. As we grow, the operating model behind the business needs to scale with it.
Today, the individual stages of our commercial process have clear owners across Sales, Revenue Operations, Legal, Product and Finance. The gap is in how those stages work together end to end.
We're hiring a Senior GTM Operations Manager to own and improve that quote-to-cash operating system - from commercial conversation through contracting, delivery, billing and recognised revenue.
This role sits within GTM Strategy & Operations, reporting into the Global Lead of the function.
The role will work closely with Sales, Account Management, Partner Operations, Product Marketing, Legal, Finance, IT and Product. This is a cross-functional role for someone who can take complex business problems, redesign the underlying process and drive change across teams, systems and ways of working.
 We follow a flexible hybrid model that translates to more than half of your time on-site in our London, UK office — three days per week.
 What You'll Do
 Own and improve quote-to-cash. Map the end-to-end commercial journey, identify bottlenecks and redesign processes so deals move cleanly from opportunity through delivery and revenue recognition. 
 Lead cross-functional quote-to-cash transformation. Work across Sales, RevOps, Partner marketing science, Creative solutions, Campaign Operations, Legal, Finance, IT and Product to solve problems that sit between functions and drive improvements through to completion. 
 Integrate new products and capabilities. Make sure new propositions can be quoted, contracted, delivered, reported, invoiced and recognised cleanly before they scale. 
 Improve business systems and handoffs. Design better workflows across the commercial stack, including HubSpot, Ironclad, delivery tooling, billing and revenue systems. Ensure data, ownership and approvals move cleanly between them. 
 Build operational visibility. Establish the KPIs, reporting and escalation mechanisms needed to understand where the commercial engine is working - and where it is not. 
 Own the transformation roadmap. Prioritise the highest-value process, systems and operating-model improvements and drive the roadmap required to support a $200M business. 
 What You’ll Bring To The Team
 Strong experience in program management, Business Operations, Program management, Strategy & Operations or Sales technology. 
 Experience leading complex cross-functional programmes with multiple teams, systems and senior stakeholders. 
 Strong business systems architecture experience, particularly across CRM, contracting, delivery, finance and reporting workflows. 
 Experience working with HubSpot and Ironclad, ideally designing or improving workflows across both. 
 Ability to map complex processes, identify root causes and design simpler, scalable operating models. 
 Strong analytical skills and experience defining operational KPIs. 
 Comfortable moving between strategy and execution and owning outcomes without direct authority over every team involved. 
 Strong written and verbal communication, including with senior leaders. 
 Experience leading change across organisations. 
 Ideally, You'll Also Bring
 Experience in adtech, media, advertising platforms or digital partnerships, with an understanding of the operational complexity behind deal delivery, measurement, contracting and revenue recognition. 
 PMP or equivalent program/project management certification. 
 Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or equivalent process-improvement qualification. 
 Experience helping build or mature a Business Operations or Transformation function. 
 What Success Looks Like
 The end-to-end commercial process is documented and ownership is clear. 
 The biggest quote-to-cash bottlenecks have been identified and materially removed. 
 Critical handoffs between teams and systems are more reliable and measurable. 
 New products can enter the commercial process without bespoke workarounds. 
 Leadership has a clear view of operational health and where intervention is needed. 
 GTM operations are built ahead of the business's growth rather than catching up with it..

title: Senior Revenue Operations Manager (Remote Canada)
description:
About Directive
 At Directive, we’re a remote-first team of performance marketers obsessed with driving measurable growth for B2B SaaS and tech companies. We believe in data-backed strategy, radical accountability, and world-class execution across every channel — Paid Media, SEO & Content, CRO, Creative, and RevOps.
We’re building the next era of integrated marketing leadership, where creativity meets commercial discipline. Join us as we elevate how client strategy, retention, and growth are delivered at scale.
 Role Summary
 We're hiring a Senior Revenue Operations Manager to own the systems our go-to-market runs on. You'll sit on the internal marketing team as the operator behind the Marketing and Sales teams, owning CRM architecture across Salesforce and HubSpot, lead routing, attribution, reporting, and the tech stack that ties it all together. You’ll work cross-functionally with sales, executive leadership, and finance. This is a team-of-one role with direct leadership visibility: you'll set the ops strategy, and you'll also be the one building the workflows and systems that make it real.
We're looking for someone who has built ops functions, not just inherited them. You're fluent in Salesforce and HubSpot, you've rebuilt messy routing and attribution before, and you can walk an executive through why a conversion rate moved and what you're doing about it. You care about data integrity because you know every leadership decision sits on top of it.
If you love owning the full marketing stack, turning weekly numbers into a story leadership trusts, and leaving systems better than you found them, this role is built for you.
 Key Responsibilities
Own CRM architecture across Salesforce and HubSpot: objects, fields, validation rules, Flows, formula fields, page layouts, and the sync logic between the two.
Run lead routing and scheduling end to end across LeanData, Chili Piper, HubSpot, and Salesforce, including round robin logic, booking windows, booking rules, and capacity, so every handraiser reaches the right rep fast.
Own attribution strategy: first- and last-touch source tracking, lead source definitions and governance, marketing influence tagging, and offline conversion tracking (Google, LinkedIn, Meta).
Report weekly and monthly on full-funnel performance (handraisers, intro calls, strategy calls, proposals, closed won) against goal, with rolling conversion rates, pacing, and YoY context. Maintain the Growth Dashboard and MoM/QoQ trackers leadership runs the business on.
Protect data integrity: deduplication (Cloudingo, LeanData), email validation, enrichment, platform properties, and sync logic.
Own email marketing end to end: newsletters, promotional sends, and nurture programs, including segmentation, build, QA, scheduling, A/B testing, and performance reporting. Protect deliverability and sender health through list hygiene, validation, and suppression management.
Build and optimize inbound and outbound programs, including handraiser and non-booker follow-up strategy, workflows, suppression logic, and signal-based campaigns across HubSpot, Instantly, Gong Engage, and UserGems.
Manage the MarTech stack and its budget: tool audits, access, renewals and negotiations, consolidation decisions, and monthly actuals vs. forecast for marketing and sales spend.
Partner with marketing on campaigns and thought leadership, from webinar operations and event lists to benchmark data for The Verdict Report and standardized campaign setup in Salesforce.
Support sales and leadership with analysis that drives decisions: pipeline goals by stage and division, channel influence analysis, and spend allocation recommendations.
Enable the org by training Account Directors, sales, and new hires on Salesforce, HubSpot, and Gong, and by keeping ops documentation, process diagrams, and how-tos current.
Maintain customer data that powers retention and expansion: point-of-contact and decision maker tracking, CSAT and reference program workflows, and CRM adoption for client-facing teams.
Design and enforce the pipeline: opportunity stages, entry and exit criteria, and stage-by-stage goals modeled from historical conversion rates so forecasts hold up.
 Who You Are
 Experience & Background
5+ years in marketing operations, revenue operations, or a similar B2B go-to-market systems role, including experience building or rebuilding an ops function.
Advanced Salesforce admin skills (validation rules, Flows, formula fields, custom objects, reports and dashboards, Data Loader) and deep HubSpot experience (workflows, lists, properties, forms, integrations). HubSpot and/or Salesforce certification is a plus, but not required.
Hands-on experience with lead routing and scheduling tools like LeanData and Chili Piper.
A strong grasp of attribution models, lead source governance, UTM standardization and tracking, and offline conversion tracking with ad platforms.
The analytical chops to build funnel reporting and pacing models in Salesforce and Google Sheets, and the judgment to explain what the numbers mean, not just what they are.
Experience with sales engagement, outbound, and data tools such as Gong and Gong Engage, Instantly, UserGems, and Zapier.
The ability to turn messy, cross-functional requests into clean systems, and the backbone to push back when a request would break reporting.
Comfort operating as a team of one: you prioritize ruthlessly, communicate tradeoffs clearly in weekly updates, and still sweat the details.
Experience managing vendor relationships, renewals, and MarTech budgets.
Confident in presenting performance and recommendations to executive leadership.
Bonus points for using AI agents or LLMs to automate ops workflows, and for agency or professional services experience.
 Cultural Fit & Traits
You take ownership of outcomes and follow through on the details.
You’re curious about all aspects of marketing and are motivated to help the team succeed.
You’re comfortable building repeatable processes while staying hands-on with execution.
You communicate directly, welcome feedback, and work independently in a remote environment.
You put the team’s success first. We work as one marketing team, with shared goals and flexible responsibilities. You take ownership of your work, jump in where you can make an impact, and collaborate across functions to drive pipeline and revenue together.
You use AI thoughtfully to support research, personalization, and execution while maintaining accuracy and a natural human voice.
 What We Offer
🏠 We have a set living wage at Directive; the actual salary may vary based on Directive's compensation practices, job related skills, and depth of experience.
🙏 Medical, dental, vision plans, disability, and life insurance coverage for you and your family that fit your lifestyle
Including a 100% employer-paid plan for you and a 50% employer contribution for your dependents (US, CAD, MX)
Benefits to Support the Whole Person:
🧠 Mental - Access to certified therapists through Spring Health, membership to Headspace
💪 Physical - Physical therapy through Omada, thousands of Aaptiv virtual workouts, complimentary One Medical membership for primary and virtual care
🛫 Time Off - Unlimited PTO (2-week minimum), Paid Company Holidays, Your Birthday Off, End of Year Recharge (Closed December 24 - January 1), Paid Parental Leave
💰 Financial - Traditional and Roth 401(k) with a 3% company match
🌟 Bonus - Annual bonus based on tenure, which scales in total amount over time
🌴 Annual Company-wide Retreat
 Work Environment Requirements
 As a remote-first company, you’ll have the ability to work from your home office. For some positions, as posted, we will accommodate global opportunities where we have established businesses, including Canada, Mexico, and the UK. For global locations, you must have established and current work authorization and permanently reside in that country.
This role has the opportunity to operate 100% virtually from your home office. We primarily collaborate with our colleagues through virtual meetings (Zoom), and Slack. In this role, you will be required to operate a laptop computer (PC or Mac available), computer software platforms, and other office productivity tools as necessary. Due to the nature of this role, you must be able to remain stationary for extended periods, must be able to observe and interpret written and/or verbal communication, must have reliable internet access, and a professional background.
